title.zh: 卷十一 魏書十一 袁張涼國田王邴管傳
title.en: Volume 11: Book of Wei 11 - Biographies of Yuan, Zhang, Liang, Guo, Tian, Wang, Bing, and Guan
title.raw: 卷十一 魏書十一 袁張涼國田王邴管傳 Volume 11: Book of Wei 11 - Biographies of Yuan, Zhang, Liang, Guo, Tian, Wang, Bing, and Guan

sentences.zh: 袁渙字曜卿，陳郡扶樂人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Huan, courtesy name Yaqing, was a man of Fule in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huan, styled Yaqing, came from Fule in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 父滂，為漢司徒。

translations.literal: His father Pang served as Minister of Education 司徒 of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Pang had been Minister of Education under the Han.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《漢紀》曰：滂字公熈，純素寡欲，終不言人之短。

translations.literal: 〈The Han Ji by Yuan Hong states: Pang’s courtesy name was Gongxi; he was pure and plain with few desires, and to the end never spoke of others’ faults.
translations.idiomatic: (Yuan Hong’s Han Ji records: Pang was styled Gongxi—pure, retiring, and sparing of desire—and never spoke ill of others.)

sentences.zh: 當權寵之盛，或以同異致禍，滂獨中立於朝，故愛憎不及焉。〉

translations.literal: When factional favor was at its height, some brought calamity on themselves through agreement or disagreement; Pang alone stood impartial at court, so neither favor nor hatred touched him.〉
translations.idiomatic: When powerful factions rose and fell, many were ruined for taking sides; Pang alone kept to the middle at court, so neither side could claim him.

sentences.zh: 當時諸公子多越法度，而渙清靜，舉動必以禮。

translations.literal: At that time many sons of noble houses exceeded law and regulation, whereas Huan was quiet and pure and invariably acted according to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: While many young noblemen flouted the law, Huan remained restrained and measured, and never departed from propriety.

sentences.zh: 郡命為功曹，郡中姧吏皆自引去。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him Chief Clerk 功曹, whereupon corrupt petty officers in the commandery all withdrew of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery made him Chief Clerk, the corrupt clerks cleaned out their desks and left.

sentences.zh: 後辟公府，舉高第，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to the Excellencies’ offices, ranked highest in the recommendation, and was promoted to Palace Assistant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned to the central government, topped the civil-service examination, and became a Palace Assistant Clerk.

sentences.zh: 除譙令，不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Qiao but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the magistracy of Qiao but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 劉備之為豫州，舉渙茂才。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei served as Governor of Yu Province, he nominated Huan as a maocai recommended talent.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei held Yu Province, he recommended Huan as an outstanding candidate.

sentences.zh: 後避地江、淮間，為袁術所命。

translations.literal: Later he fled to the region between the Jiang and Huai and took employment under Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He later took refuge between the Yangzi and the Huai and entered Yuan Shu’s service.

sentences.zh: 術每有所咨訪，渙常正議，術不能抗，然敬之不敢不禮也。

translations.literal: Whenever Shu consulted him, Huan invariably responded with upright counsel; Shu could not overcome him in debate but respected him and dared not slight him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu often asked his opinion; Huan answered frankly every time. Shu could not shout him down, yet respected him too much to treat him roughly.

sentences.zh: 頃之，呂布擊術於阜陵，渙往從之，遂復為布所拘留。

translations.literal: Presently Lü Bu attacked Shu at Fuling; Huan went to join Bu and was again detained by Bu.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu struck Yuan Shu at Fuling, Huan went over to Lü Bu’s camp—and Bu kept him there against his will.

sentences.zh: 布初與劉備和親，後離隙。

translations.literal: Bu had first allied and formed marriage ties with Bei, then became estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu had first allied with Liu Bei and sealed the tie with marriage, then the two fell out.

sentences.zh: 布欲使渙作書詈辱備，渙不可，再三彊之，不許。

translations.literal: Bu wished to make Huan write a letter reviling and insulting Bei; Huan refused. Bu repeatedly pressed him, but he would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu ordered Huan to draft a letter vilifying Liu Bei. Huan refused; however hard Bu pressed, he would not budge.

sentences.zh: 布大怒，以兵脅渙曰：「為之則生，不為則死。

translations.literal: Bu was furious and threatened Huan with armed soldiers, saying, “Do it and you live; refuse and you die.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Lü Bu drew his troops on him and said: “Write it and you live; refuse and you die.”

sentences.zh: 」渙顏色不變，笑而應之曰：「渙聞唯德可以辱人，不聞以罵。

translations.literal: ” Huan’s expression did not change; smiling he replied, “I have heard that only virtue can shame others; I have not heard of doing so by abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Huan’s face never changed. Smiling, he answered: “I have heard that shame comes from virtue, not from vilification.

sentences.zh: 使彼固君子邪，且不恥將軍之言，彼誠小人邪，將復將軍之意，則辱在此不在於彼。

translations.literal: If he is truly a gentleman, he will not be shamed by your words; if he is truly a petty man, he will repay your intent—and then the shame lies here with you, not with him.
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Bei is a gentleman, your insults will not touch him; if he is a petty man, he will answer your spite in kind—and the shame will be yours to bear, not his.

sentences.zh: 且渙他日之事劉將軍，猶今日之事將軍也，如一旦去此，復罵將軍，可乎？

translations.literal: Besides, my serving General Liu in days past is as my serving you today; if one day I leave this place and revile you in turn, would that be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I served General Liu then as I serve you now. Should I leave your side someday and turn those same taunts on you, would you call that honor?

sentences.zh: 」布慙而止。

translations.literal: ” Bu was ashamed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was ashamed and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 布誅，乃得歸太祖。

translations.literal: After Bu was executed, Huan was able to return to Grand Progenitor Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Bu’s execution, Huan was free to join Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 〈《袁氏世紀》曰：布之破也，陳羣父子時亦在布之軍，見太祖皆拜。

translations.literal: 〈The Records of the Yuan Clan states: When Bu was defeated, Chen Qun and his son were also in Bu’s army; when they saw Grand Progenitor they both bowed.
translations.idiomatic: (The Yuan family chronicle notes: When Lü Bu fell, Chen Qun and his son were in Bu’s army; both kowtowed when they met Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 渙獨高揖不為禮，太祖甚嚴憚之。

translations.literal: Huan alone performed a high bow and offered no obeisance; Grand Progenitor stood in great awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan alone straightened his back and bowed at the waist only—never touching his forehead to the ground. Cao Cao regarded him with wary respect.

sentences.zh: 時太祖又給衆官車各數乘，使取布軍中物，唯其所欲。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Progenitor also granted each official several carriages and sent them to take goods from Bu’s army as each wished.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao also gave each officer wagons and told them to help themselves to Lü Bu’s stores.

sentences.zh: 衆人皆重載，唯渙取書數百卷，資糧而已，衆人聞之，大慙。

translations.literal: Everyone loaded heavily; only Huan took several hundred rolls of books and provisions—and when the others heard of it they were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The others hauled off loot by the cartload; Huan took only several hundred scrolls and enough food for the road. When word spread, they burned with shame.

sentences.zh: 渙謂所親曰：「脫我以行陳，令軍發足以為行糧而已，不以此為我有。

translations.literal: Huan said to those close to him, “Had they assigned me to the ranks, provisions enough for marching would have sufficed; I would not have treated those things as my own.
translations.idiomatic: Huan told his intimates: “If they had put me in the ranks, rations for the march would have been enough—I would never have treated booty as personal gain.

sentences.zh: 由是厲名也，大悔恨之。

translations.literal: It was by this that they established their reputation; they greatly regretted it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: That was how I meant to keep my name unstained.” The others bitterly regretted their greed.

sentences.zh: 」太祖益以此重焉。〉

translations.literal: ” Grand Progenitor esteemed him all the more for it.〉
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao respected him all the more for it.)

sentences.zh: 渙言曰：「夫兵者，凶器也，不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Huan stated: “Arms are instruments of ill omen; one employs them only when there is no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: Huan urged: “Weapons are ill-omened tools; they are a last resort.

sentences.zh: 鼓之以道德，征之以仁義，兼撫其民而除其害。

translations.literal: Stir them with virtue and the Way; campaign with benevolence and righteousness; together soothe the people and remove what harms them.
translations.idiomatic: Rouse them with moral power and the Way; wage campaigns with benevolence and right; comfort the people while rooting out what harms them.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故可與之死而可與之生。

translations.literal: Only then may they die with you or live with you.
translations.idiomatic: Only then will men face death or life at your side without wavering.

sentences.zh: 自大亂以來十數年矣，民之欲安，甚於倒縣，然而暴亂未息者，何也？

translations.literal: Since the great turmoil began it has been more than ten years; the people's desire for peace is keener than release from an inverted suspension—yet why has violent disorder not ceased?
translations.idiomatic: The realm has been torn apart for more than a decade; the people long for peace more than for relief from hanging upside down—so why does chaos still rage?

sentences.zh: 意者政失其道歟！

translations.literal: I suppose governance has lost the Way!
translations.idiomatic: Surely policy has strayed from the right path!

sentences.zh: 渙聞明君善於救世，故世亂則齊之以義，時偽則鎮之以樸；

translations.literal: I have heard that wise rulers excel at saving the age: when the age is chaotic they bring it into alignment with righteousness; when the times are false they steady them with simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Wise rulers rescue their age: in chaos they align it with justice; in decadent times they anchor it with plain sincerity.

sentences.zh: 世異事變，治國不同，不可不察也。

translations.literal: As generations differ and affairs change, governing the state cannot be the same—this cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: Times change and government must change with them—the difference cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 夫制度損益，此古今之不必同者也。

translations.literal: As for expanding or trimming institutions, past and present need not match.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting or adding institutions need not mirror antiquity.

sentences.zh: 若夫兼愛天下而反之於正，雖以武平亂而濟之以德，誠百王不易之道也。

translations.literal: But as for embracing love for all under Heaven and returning them to rectitude—though you quell disorder with arms, you complete it with virtue—this is indeed the Way no hundred kings may alter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet caring for the empire and steering it back toward right—even when you use arms to end disorder, you finish the work with virtue—that is the constant thread no succession of rulers may discard.

sentences.zh: 公明哲超世，古之所以得其民者，公旣勤之矣，今之所以失其民者，公旣戒之矣，海內賴公，得免於危亡之禍，然而民未知義，其唯公所以訓之，則天下幸甚！

translations.literal: You are enlightened and wise beyond the age; what the ancients did to win the people you have already diligently pursued; what causes the loss of the people today you have already taken as warning. Within the seas they rely on you and have been spared the calamity of peril and ruin—yet the people do not yet understand righteousness. If only you would instruct them as befits you, how fortunate would be all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Your insight rises above the age: you have already done what the ancients did to win hearts, and you already heed what loses them. The realm looks to you and has been spared utter ruin—yet ordinary folk still do not grasp moral duty. Teach them in your own fashion, and all under Heaven will be the richer for it.

sentences.zh: 」太祖深納焉。

translations.literal: ” Grand Progenitor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took his counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 拜為沛南部都尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Commandant of the southern part of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Chief Commandant for the southern districts of Pei.

sentences.zh: 是時新募民開屯田，民不樂，多逃亡。

translations.literal: At this time newly levied commoners had been opened for military-agricultural colonies; the people were unhappy and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just drafted civilians for military-agricultural colonies; morale was low and deserters were many.

sentences.zh: 渙白太祖曰：「夫民安土重遷，不可卒變，易以順行，難以逆動，宜順其意，樂之者乃取，不欲者勿彊。

translations.literal: Huan reported to Grand Progenitor: “The people are settled on their land and loathe to move; they cannot be suddenly changed. What accords with their wishes is easy to carry out; what runs counter is hard to set in motion. You should follow their intent: take only those who are willing; do not force those who do not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan urged Cao Cao: “People cling to their native soil and resist uprooting overnight. What follows their wishes moves easily; what cuts against them meets stubborn resistance. Bend with their inclinations—enroll the willing and leave the unwilling alone.

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之，百姓大恱。

translations.literal: ” Grand Progenitor followed this advice, and the common people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed, and popular morale soared.

sentences.zh: 遷為梁相。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chancellor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chancellor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 渙每勑諸縣：「務存鰥寡高年，表異孝子貞婦。

translations.literal: Huan routinely instructed the counties: “Be sure to provide for widowers, widows, and the elderly; commend exceptional filial sons and chaste wives.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly told the counties: “Care for widowers, widows, and the aged; lift up model sons and faithful wives.

sentences.zh: 常談曰『世治則禮詳，世亂則禮簡』，全在斟酌之間耳。

translations.literal: A common saying runs, “When the age is well ordered ritual is detailed; when the age is in turmoil ritual is simple”—the whole matter lies in what measure one strikes.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says, ‘Good times allow elaborate rites; troubled times call for simple ones’—the art is knowing where to draw the line.

sentences.zh: 方今雖擾攘，難以禮化，然在吾所以為之。

translations.literal: Though today is disturbed and hard to transform by ritual, still what can be done lies with us.
translations.idiomatic: Even now, though the age is violent and ritual reform will not come overnight, much still depends on how we conduct ourselves.

sentences.zh: 」為政崇教訓，恕思而後行，外溫柔而內能斷。

translations.literal: ” In conducting government he honored teaching and instruction; he thought things through with forgiving care before acting; outwardly gentle, inwardly decisive.
translations.idiomatic: In office he emphasized moral instruction, deliberated with humane patience before acting, appeared mild abroad, yet could judge firmly within.

sentences.zh: 〈王沈《魏書》曰：穀熟長呂岐善朱淵、爰津，遣使行學還，召用之，與相見，出署淵師友祭酒，津決疑祭酒。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Shu by Wang Chen states: Lü Qi, magistrate of Gushu, favored Zhu Yuan and Yuan Jin; he sent them on study missions and on their return summoned them for appointment. When he met them he appointed Yuan Instructor of the Friends of Learning and Jin Instructor for Resolving Doubts.
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Chen’s Wei Shu: Gushu district chief Lü Qi thought highly of Zhu Yuan and Yuan Jin. After sending them to study, he recalled them for appointment; at their meeting he named Yuan Libationer for the Friends of Learning and Jin Libationer for Resolving Doubts.

sentences.zh: 淵等因各歸家，不受署。

translations.literal: Yuan and the others thereupon each returned home and did not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan and his companions went home instead and refused the posts.

sentences.zh: 岐大怒，將吏民收淵等，皆杖殺之，議者多非焉。

translations.literal: Qi was furious and was about to have his clerks and people seize Yuan and the others; he had them all beaten to death. Many critics condemned this.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qi flew into a rage and ordered his officers and local residents to arrest them; he had every one of them clubbed to death. Opinion widely condemned him.

sentences.zh: 渙教勿劾，主簿孫徽等以為「淵等罪不足死，長吏無專殺之義，孔子稱『唯器與名，不可以假人』。

translations.literal: Huan instructed that no impeachment be filed. Chief Clerk Sun Hui and others held that “Yuan and the others’ offenses did not merit death; a senior magistrate has no authority to kill on his own initiative. Confucius said, ‘Only ritual vessels and titles may not be lent to others.’
translations.idiomatic: Huan directed that no charges be brought. Chief Clerk Sun Hui argued that Zhu Yuan’s party did not deserve death and that a county chief had no right of summary execution—citing Confucius: “Regalia and titles must never be handled lightly.”

sentences.zh: 謂之師友而加大戮，刑名相伐，不可以訓。

translations.literal: To call them friends of learning yet inflict great execution—punishment and title clash; this cannot instruct.
translations.idiomatic: To honor men as “friends of learning” and then beat them to death confuses law with courtesy—it teaches nothing good.

sentences.zh: 」渙教曰：「主簿以不請為罪，此則然矣。

translations.literal: ” Huan instructed: “That the chief clerk should bear blame for not having sought approval—this is so.
translations.idiomatic: Huan replied: “The chief clerk deserves blame for failing to seek higher approval—that much is true.

sentences.zh: 謂淵等罪不足死，則非也。

translations.literal: But to say Yuan and the others’ offenses did not merit death is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: To claim those men were innocent of capital crimes is wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫師友之名，古今有之。

translations.literal: The designation of friends of learning has existed in ancient and modern times alike.
translations.idiomatic: The title “friend of learning” has always had its uses.

sentences.zh: 然有君之師友，有士大夫之師友。

translations.literal: Yet there is the ruler’s “friend of learning” and there is the scholar-official’s “friend of learning.”
translations.idiomatic: But there is the sovereign’s “friend of learning” and there is the minister’s “friend of learning.”

sentences.zh: 夫君置師友之官者，所以敬其臣也；

translations.literal: When a ruler establishes the office of friend of learning, it is to show respect to his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler institutes such an office, he means to honor his officials.

sentences.zh: 有罪加於刑焉，國之法也。

translations.literal: When guilt is added and punishment applied, that is the law of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When crime is proven and sentence passed, that is the kingdom’s law.

sentences.zh: 今不論其罪而謂之戮師友，斯失之矣。

translations.literal: Now, without discussing their crimes yet calling it slaying the friend of learning—that misses the mark.
translations.idiomatic: To skip the facts of guilt and speak only of “murdering a friend of learning” misses the point.

sentences.zh: 主簿取弟子戮師之名，而加君誅臣之實，非其類也。

translations.literal: The chief clerk takes the name of a disciple executing his teacher and applies to it the substance of a ruler executing his minister—the categories do not match.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui borrows the language of a pupil killing his teacher to describe a ruler punishing a minister—the analogy fails.

sentences.zh: 夫聖哲之治，觀時而動，故不必循常，將有權也。

translations.literal: The governance of sages and wise men observes the times and acts; therefore one need not always follow routine—there is room for expedients.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings watch the times and adapt; they need not cling to precedent when circumstance demands flexibility.

sentences.zh: 間者世亂，民陵其上，雖務尊君卑臣，猶或未也，而反長世之過，不亦謬乎！

translations.literal: In recent generations the age has been in turmoil and the people have lorded it over their superiors; though one strives to honor the ruler and humble ministers, it may still not succeed—and instead you prolong the faults of the age: is that not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: These are chaotic generations in which common folk bully their betters; even when we stress honoring the throne and humbling ministers, it may not take hold—and you would pile another fashionable error on top? That is folly.

sentences.zh: 」遂不劾。〉

translations.literal: ” He therefore did not impeach.〉
translations.idiomatic: So Huan let the matter drop.)

sentences.zh: 以病去官，百姓思之。

translations.literal: He resigned office on grounds of illness; the common people missed him.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down citing illness, and the people longed for his return.

sentences.zh: 後徵為諫議大夫、丞相軍祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Grand Counselor of Remonstrance and Libationer for the Chancellor’s army.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as Grand Counselor of Remonstrance and army libationer under the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 前後得賜甚多，皆散盡之，家無所儲，終不問產業，乏則取之於人，不為皦察之行，然時人服其清。

translations.literal: The gifts he received before and after were many; he distributed them all until none remained and stored nothing at home. He never attended to property or estates; when short he took from others. He did not engage in ostentatiously scrutinizing conduct—yet men of the time admired his purity.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial largesse came often; he passed every gift on until his coffers were bare. He never fussed over fields or houses—when he lacked funds he borrowed—and though he never played the zealous fault-finder, contemporaries revered his integrity.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，為郎中令，行御史大夫事。

translations.literal: When Wei was first founded he served as Prefect of the Gentlemen of the Palace, acting as Imperial Clerk Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei dukedom was founded he became Prefect of the Gentlemen of the Palace, handling the duties of Imperial Clerk Grandee.

sentences.zh: 渙言於太祖曰：「今天下大難已除，文武並用，長久之道也。

translations.literal: Huan said to Grand Progenitor: “The great calamities under Heaven have now been removed; civil and military are both employed—this is the way to endure.
translations.idiomatic: He told Cao Cao: “The worst blows to the realm are over; blending civil and military policy is how dynasties last.

sentences.zh: 以為可大收篇籍，明先聖之教，以易民視聽，使海內斐然向風，則遠人不服可以文德來之。

translations.literal: I believe you may greatly gather books and documents, clarify the teaching of the former sages, and thereby alter what the people see and hear, so that within the seas they flourish and turn to the wind; then if distant peoples do not submit, you may draw them with the virtue of culture.
translations.idiomatic: Gather the classics, explain the sages’ teaching, and reshape what people hear and see until the realm stirs with admiration; then whatever borders still resist can be drawn in by civil virtue alone.

sentences.zh: 」太祖善其言。

translations.literal: ” Grand Progenitor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao praised the proposal.

sentences.zh: 時有傳劉備死者，羣臣皆賀；

translations.literal: At the time there was a rumor that Liu Bei had died; all the ministers congratulated the court.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors claimed Liu Bei was dead, and the courtiers crowded in with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 渙以甞為備舉吏，獨不賀。

translations.literal: Huan alone did not congratulate, for he had once been nominated as an official by Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Huan alone stayed away—Liu Bei had once sponsored his career.

sentences.zh: 居官數年卒，太祖為之流涕，賜穀二千斛，一教「以太倉穀千斛賜郎中令之家」，一教「以垣下穀千斛與曜卿家」，外不解其意。

translations.literal: After several years in office he died. Grand Progenitor wept for him and granted two thousand hu of grain—one edict read “grant the household of the Prefect of the Gentlemen one thousand hu from the Grand Granary,” another “grant one thousand hu from the granary below the wall to Yaqing’s family.” Outsiders did not understand his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office a few years later. Cao Cao mourned aloud and sent two thousand hu of grain—one rescript granting the Prefect’s household a thousand hu from the imperial granary, another granting Yaqing’s kin a thousand hu from the wall-side store. Observers puzzled over the distinction.

sentences.zh: 教曰：「以太倉穀者，官法也；

translations.literal: The edict explained: “What comes from the Grand Granary follows official statute.
translations.idiomatic: The order explained: “Grain from the Grand Granary follows public statute.

sentences.zh: 以垣下穀者，親舊也。

translations.literal: What comes from the granary below the wall is for kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from below the wall comes from my own stores for family and old allies.

sentences.zh: 」又帝聞渙昔拒呂布之事，問渙從弟敏：「渙勇怯何如？

translations.literal: ” The Emperor also heard of Huan’s past refusal of Lü Bu and asked Huan’s cousin Min, “Was Huan brave or timid?
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign later heard how Huan had defied Lü Bu and asked his cousin Min whether Huan had been bold or timid.

sentences.zh: 」敏對曰：「渙貌似和柔，然其臨大節，處危難，雖賁、育不過也。

translations.literal: ” Min replied: “Huan seems mild and yielding, yet when he faces great principle and stands amid peril and crisis, not even Ben or Yu could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Min answered: “He looks gentle, but when great principle or mortal danger is at stake, not even ancient heroes could surpass him.

sentences.zh: 」渙子侃，亦清粹閑素，有父風，歷位郡守尚書。

translations.literal: ” Huan’s son Kan was also pure and refined, leisurely and plain, with his father’s manner; he rose through posts as commandery governor and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan was clear-minded and retiring like his father, and rose to commandery governor and minister.

sentences.zh: 〈《袁氏世紀》曰：渙有四子，侃、㝢、奧、準。

translations.literal: 〈The Records of the Yuan Clan states: Huan had four sons—Kan, Yu, Ao, and Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: (The Yuan family chronicle lists four sons: Kan, Yu, Ao, and Zhun.

sentences.zh: 侃字公然，論議清當，柔而不犯，善與人交。

translations.literal: Kan’s courtesy name was Gongran; his discourse was clear and apt, yielding yet not yielding ground, skilled in dealing with others.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, styled Gongran, argued cleanly and fairly—flexible yet firm—and knew how to handle people.

sentences.zh: 在廢興之間，人之所趣務者，常謙退不為也。

translations.literal: Amid rise and fall of fortunes, what men eagerly pursued—he routinely modestly declined and did not do.
translations.idiomatic: When fortunes shifted and others scrambled for advantage, he habitually stood back.

sentences.zh: 時人以是稱之。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 歷位黃門選部郎，號為清平。

translations.literal: He rose to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and Supervisor of Selection—his reputation was for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and Director of Selection, famed for even-handed judgment.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至尚書，早卒。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Minister but died young.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually reached ministerial rank but died young.

sentences.zh: 㝢字宣厚，精辯有機理，好道家之言，少被病，未官而卒，奧字公榮，行足以厲俗，言約而理當，終於光祿勳。

translations.literal: Yu’s courtesy name was Xuanhou—acute in debate and possessed of subtle principle, fond of Daoist teachings; in youth he fell ill and died before holding office. Ao’s courtesy name was Gongrong—his conduct was enough to reform custom; his words brief yet apt to principle; he ended as Minister of Court Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Xuanhou, was sharp in debate, drawn to Daoism, and died young before serving. Ao, styled Gongrong, lived modestly enough to reform local habits; his speech was spare but exact, and he rose to Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 準字孝尼，忠信公正，不恥下問，唯恐人之不勝己。

translations.literal: Zhun’s courtesy name was Xiaoni—loyal, trustworthy, fair, and upright; he was not ashamed to learn from those below him and only feared others might not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun, styled Xiaoni, was loyal, candid, and humble enough to learn from social inferiors—yet anxious whenever peers fell short of his standard.

sentences.zh: 以世事多險，故常治退而不敢求進。

translations.literal: Because affairs of the age held many perils, he routinely sought withdrawal and dared not seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Danger stalked public life, so he preferred retreat and rarely pressed for promotion.

sentences.zh: 著書十餘萬言，論治世之務，為易、周官、詩傳，及論五經滯義，聖人之微言，以傳於世。

translations.literal: He wrote more than one hundred thousand characters on matters of ordering the age—commentaries on the Changes, the Offices of Zhou, and the Mao Commentary to the Odes, and treatises on doubtful points in the Five Classics and subtle words of the sages—to transmit to the world.
translations.idiomatic: He composed over one hundred thousand characters on statecraft—commentaries on the Zhou yi, Zhou li, and Mao Shi plus essays on unresolved issues in the Five Classics—intending them for posterity.

sentences.zh: 此準之自序也。

translations.literal: This was Zhun’s self-preface.
translations.idiomatic: Those lines come from Zhun’s own preface.

sentences.zh: 荀綽九州記稱準有儁才，泰始中為給事中。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo’s Record of the Nine Provinces states that Zhun had outstanding talent and served as palace attendant in the Taishi era.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo’s Jiuzhou ji describes Zhun as brilliant and records him as a palace attendant under Emperor Wu (Taishi era).

sentences.zh: 袁氏子孫世有名位，貴達至今。〉

translations.literal: Yuan descendants have held famous positions for generations and remain eminent to this day.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Yuans have kept high office for generations down to the present.)

sentences.zh: 初，渙從弟霸，公恪有功幹，魏初為大司農，及同郡何夔並知名於時。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huan’s cousin Ba was diligent, scrupulous, and capable; at the beginning of Wei he was Minister of Agriculture, and together with He Kui of the same commandery was renowned in the time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huan’s cousin Yuan Ba—meticulous and capable—had become Minister of Agriculture at Wei’s founding and, with fellow townsman He Kui, stood among the age’s leading names.

sentences.zh: 而霸子亮，夔子曾，與侃復齊聲友善。

translations.literal: Ba’s son Liang and Kui’s son Ceng were again on friendly terms with Kan with matching reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Ba’s son Liang and Kui’s son Zeng were as close to Kan as their fathers had been to one another.

sentences.zh: 亮貞固有學行，疾何晏、鄧颺等，著論以譏切之，位至河南尹、尚書。

translations.literal: Liang was firm and principled, with learning and conduct; he loathed He Yan, Deng Yang, and the like and wrote treatises to satirize them; he rose to Governor of Henan and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was upright, learned, and outspoken; he despised He Yan and Deng Yang and lampooned them in essays, rising to governor of Henan and minister.

sentences.zh: 〈《晉諸公贊》曰：亮子粲，字儀祖，文學博識，累為儒官，至尚書。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Appraisal of the Jin Worthies states: Liang’s son Can, courtesy name Yizu, was learned and broadly informed, repeatedly served as a scholar-official, and rose to Minister.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Jin zhugong zan adds: Liang’s son Can, styled Yizu, was a scholar of wide learning who repeatedly served in academic posts and reached ministerial rank.)

sentences.zh: 霸弟徽，以儒素稱。

translations.literal: Ba’s younger brother Hui was celebrated for Confucian simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Ba’s younger brother Hui was known as a plain Confucian gentleman.

sentences.zh: 遭天下亂，避難交州。

translations.literal: When turmoil engulfed the realm he fled for refuge to Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos spread he fled south to Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 司徒辟，不至。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education summoned him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him as Minister of Education; he refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《漢紀》曰：初，天下將亂，渙慨然歎曰：「漢室陵遲，亂無日矣。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong’s 《Han Ji》 states: Earlier, when turmoil was about to engulf the realm, Huan sighed in sorrow and said, “The house of Han declines; disorder will come any day.
translations.idiomatic: (Yuan Hong’s Han ji: Even before the collapse, Huan had sighed, “The Han house is failing; disaster cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 苟天下擾攘，逃將安之？

translations.literal: If all under Heaven is thrown into chaos, where would flight take one in safety?
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm dissolves in war, what refuge could exile possibly offer?”

sentences.zh: 若天未喪道，民以義存，唯彊而有禮，可以庇身乎！

translations.literal: If Heaven has not yet abandoned the Way and the people endure through righteousness, only he who is strong and observes ritual propriety may shelter his person, may he not!
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven still honors the Way and the people cling to right, only strength wedded to ritual can keep you safe—that is the path!

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「古人有言：『知機其神乎』！

translations.literal: ” Hui said, “The ancients had a saying: ‘To know the moment is to be spirit-like!’
translations.idiomatic: Hui answered: “The classic line runs, ‘To grasp the turning point is next to divine wisdom.’

sentences.zh: 見機而作，君子所以元吉也。

translations.literal: To see the moment and act—this is why the gentleman secures supreme good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Read the moment and move—that is how a gentleman wins the great blessing.

sentences.zh: 天理盛衰，漢其亡矣！

translations.literal: Heaven's principle waxes and wanes; Han is surely doomed!
translations.idiomatic: The tide of Heaven ebbs and flows; the house of Han is finished.

sentences.zh: 夫有大功必有大事，此又君子之所深識，退藏於密者也。

translations.literal: Where there is great merit there must be great events—this again is what gentlemen deeply understand: to withdraw and hide in secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Great deeds stir great crises—wise men see that far ahead and know when to vanish from sight.

sentences.zh: 且兵革旣興，外患必衆，徽將遠迹山海，以求免身。

translations.literal: Moreover, now that arms have been raised, external troubles will surely be many; I, Hui, shall seek tracks far among mountains and seas to preserve myself.
translations.idiomatic: War invites countless enemies from without; I mean to lose myself among coastal hills until the storm passes.

sentences.zh: 」及亂作，各行其志。〉

translations.literal: When disorder arose, each man followed his own intent.〉
translations.idiomatic: When chaos came, every cousin chose his own course.)

sentences.zh: 徽弟敏，有武藝而好水功，官至河隄謁者。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Min had martial skill and loved hydraulic works; his office rose to Director of River Works.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Min was handy with arms and obsessed with waterworks, rising to inspector of dikes and canals.

sentences.zh: 張範，字公儀，河內脩武人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan, courtesy name Gongyi, was a man of Xiuwu in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan, styled Gongyi, hailed from Xiuwu in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖父歆，為漢司徒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xin served as Minister of Education of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang Xin had been Minister of Education under the Han.

sentences.zh: 父延，為太尉。

translations.literal: His father Yan served as Commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yan had served as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 太傅袁隗欲以女妻範，範辭不受。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yuan Kui wished to marry his daughter to Fan; Fan declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yuan Kui offered him a daughter in marriage; Fan politely refused.

sentences.zh: 性恬靜樂道，忽於榮利，徵命無所就。

translations.literal: By nature tranquil and fond of the Way, he neglected glory and profit and answered no summons to office.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and devoted to learning, he cared nothing for rank or riches and ignored every appointment.

sentences.zh: 弟承，字公先，亦知名，以方正徵，拜議郎，遷伊闕都尉。

translations.literal: His younger brother Cheng, courtesy name Gongxian, was also renowned; summoned for incorruptibility he was appointed Gentleman Consultant and promoted to Commandant of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Cheng, styled Gongxian, was likewise celebrated; called up as a man of integrity he became a Gentleman Consultant and then commandant of Yique pass.

sentences.zh: 董卓作亂，承欲合徒衆與天下共誅卓。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo threw the realm into turmoil, Cheng wished to gather followers and join the world in executing Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo seized the capital, Cheng wanted to raise men and join the coalition against him.

sentences.zh: 承弟昭時為議郎，適從長安來，謂承曰：「今欲誅卓，衆寡不敵，且起一朝之謀，戰阡陌之民，士不素撫，兵不練習，難以成功。

translations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Zhao was then Gentleman Consultant; he had just come from Chang'an and said to Cheng: "Now if you wish to execute Zhuo, your forces cannot match his; moreover you would raise a plan in a single morning and fight with peasants from the fields—the officers have not been long soothed and the troops are not drilled; it will be hard to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhao, a Gentleman Consultant fresh from Chang’an, warned him: “You cannot match Zhuo’s army; a hasty plot backed only by untrained villagers will fail.”

sentences.zh: 卓阻兵而無義，固不能久；

translations.literal: Zhuo holds his army without righteousness; assuredly he cannot last long;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo commands troops without moral right—he cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 不若擇所歸附，待時而動，然後可以如志。

translations.literal: it is better to choose whom to attach yourself to, wait for the moment to move, and then you may fulfill your intent.
translations.idiomatic: Pick a patron, bide your time, and strike when fortune turns—that is how you get what you want.

sentences.zh: 」承然之，乃解印綬間行歸家，與範避地揚州。

translations.literal: Cheng agreed; thereupon he removed his seal and ribbon and by hidden routes returned home, and with Fan fled to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng agreed. He shed his official seals, slipped home by back roads, and joined Fan in flight to the south.

sentences.zh: 袁術備禮招請，範稱疾不往，術不彊屈也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu with full ceremony invited him; Fan pleaded illness and did not go, and Shu did not force him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu courted him with elaborate courtesy; Fan pleaded illness and Shu did not press the issue.

sentences.zh: 遣承與相見，術問曰：「昔周室陵遲，則有桓、文之霸；

translations.literal: He sent Cheng to meet him. Shu asked: "When the Zhou house declined, then there were the hegemonies of Huan and Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent Cheng to an audience and asked: “When the Zhou throne faltered, Qi Huan and Jin Wen rose as hegemons;

sentences.zh: 秦失其政，漢接而用之。

translations.literal: Qin lost its governance, and Han took it up and used it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin bungled the mandate and Han seized it.

sentences.zh: 今孤以土地之廣，士民之衆，欲徼福齊桓，擬迹高祖，何如？

translations.literal: Now I, with the breadth of my lands and the multitude of officers and people, wish to seek blessing like Duke Huan of Qi and model myself on the High Ancestor—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: I command vast territory and a huge population—why should I not rival Duke Huan or trace the path of the Han founder?”

sentences.zh: 」承對曰：「在德不在彊。

translations.literal: Cheng replied: "It lies in virtue, not in strength.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng answered: “Power follows virtue, not manpower.

sentences.zh: 夫能用德以同天下之欲，雖由匹夫之資，而興霸王之功，不足為難。

translations.literal: If one can employ virtue to unite the desires of all under Heaven, though starting with the resources of a common man, to raise the achievement of a hegemon or king is not hard.
translations.idiomatic: Win the world’s aspirations through moral authority and even a commoner can build a hegemon’s enterprise—that is not difficult.

sentences.zh: 若苟僭擬，干時而動，衆之所棄，誰能興之？

translations.literal: But if you rashly usurp the title and move against the times, those whom the multitude rejects—who can raise you up?"
translations.idiomatic: Usurp the throne against the tide and the realm will cast you off—who then can lift you up?”

sentences.zh: 」術不恱。

translations.literal: Shu was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shu’s face darkened.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖將征冀州，術復問曰：「今曹公欲以弊兵數千，敵十萬之衆，可謂不量力矣！

translations.literal: At that time Grand Progenitor was about to campaign in Ji Province; Shu again asked: "Now Lord Cao wishes with a few thousand worn troops to oppose a host of a hundred thousand—one may say he does not measure his strength!
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao prepared to march on Ji Province, Shu tried again: “He means to meet your hundred thousand men with a few thousand battered soldiers—is that not suicidal?

sentences.zh: 子以為何如？

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What say you?”

sentences.zh: 」承乃曰：「漢德雖衰，天命未改，今曹公挾天子以令天下，雖敵百萬之衆可也。

translations.literal: Cheng then said: "Though Han's virtue has waned, Heaven's Mandate has not changed. Now Lord Cao holds the Son of Heaven to command the realm—though he oppose a million soldiers he may do it."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said flatly: “Han’s prestige may fade, yet Heaven’s choice stands. Cao Cao holds the emperor—against him even a million spears will break.”

sentences.zh: 」術作色不懌，承去之。

translations.literal: Shu changed color and was displeased; Cheng departed from him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu flushed with anger; Cheng walked out.

sentences.zh: 太祖平冀州，遣使迎範。

translations.literal: After Grand Progenitor pacified Ji Province he sent an envoy to welcome Fan.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao took Ji Province he sent escorts to fetch Zhang Fan.

sentences.zh: 範以疾留彭城，遣承詣太祖，太祖表以為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Fan stayed at Pengcheng on account of illness and sent Cheng to visit Grand Progenitor; Grand Progenitor memorialized him as Grand Counselor of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Fan halted at Pengcheng, pleading illness, and sent Cheng ahead; Cao Cao memorialized him as grand counselor of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 範子陵及承子戩為山東賊所得，範直詣賊請二子，賊以陵還範。

translations.literal: Fan's son Ling and Cheng's son Jian were taken by bandits east of the mountains; Fan went straight to the bandits to ask for his two sons; the bandits returned Ling to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits east of the Taihang seized Fan’s son Ling and Cheng’s son Jian. Fan walked into their camp and bargained for both; they released Ling first.

sentences.zh: 範謝曰：「諸君相還兒厚矣。

translations.literal: Fan thanked them: "You gentlemen have been generous in returning my son.
translations.idiomatic: Fan bowed: “You honor me by sending my boy home.

sentences.zh: 夫人情雖愛其子，然吾憐戩之小，請以陵易之。

translations.literal: Though human feeling surely loves its children, I pity Jian's youth—please exchange Ling for him.
translations.idiomatic: Any father loves his sons, but Jian is younger—keep Ling and give me Jian instead.”

sentences.zh: 」賊義其言，悉以還範。

translations.literal: The bandits thought his words righteous and returned them all to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Touched by his fairness, they freed both children.

sentences.zh: 太祖自荊州還，範得見於陳，以為議郎，參丞相軍事，甚見敬重。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor returned from Jing Province, Fan was received audience at Chen and was made Gentleman Consultant and joined the Chancellor's military staff; he was greatly esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: On Cao Cao’s return from Jing Province he received Fan at Chen, named him a Gentleman Consultant and adviser on army affairs, and treated him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 太祖征伐，常令範及邴原留，與世子居守。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor campaigned he routinely ordered Fan and Bing Yuan to remain, dwelling with the heir apparent to guard the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cao Cao marched he left Fan and Bing Yuan with the heir to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂文帝：「舉動必諮此二人。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor told Emperor Wen: "In all your movements you must consult these two men.
translations.idiomatic: He told the future Wendi: “Before you act on anything, consult these two.

sentences.zh: 」世子執子孫禮。

translations.literal: The heir apparent performed the rites of grandson toward them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince treated them with grandsons’ deference.

sentences.zh: 救恤窮乏，家無所餘，中外孤寡皆歸焉。

translations.literal: He rescued and relieved the destitute; nothing remained in his home; orphaned widows from inside and outside all came to him.
translations.idiomatic: He poured his wealth into charity until his house was bare; widows and orphans everywhere sought him out.

sentences.zh: 贈遺無所逆，亦終不用，及去，皆以還之。

translations.literal: Gifts given him he did not reject, yet in the end he never used them; when he left he returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted presents but never spent them—when he moved on he sent every gift back.

sentences.zh: 建安十七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventeenth year of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 212 CE, the seventeenth year of the Jian’an era.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，承以丞相參軍祭酒領趙郡太守，政化大行。

translations.literal: When Wei was first founded Cheng as Libationer for the Chancellor's Army supervised Zhao commandery as Administrator; his administrative transformation went far.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Wei dukedom Cheng served as army libationer while governing Zhao commandery, and his reforms took deep root.

sentences.zh: 太祖將西征，徵承參軍事，至長安，病卒。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor was about to campaign west he summoned Cheng as military adviser; he reached Chang'an and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao summoned him for the western campaign; he reached Chang’an but died on the road.

sentences.zh: 涼茂字伯方，山陽昌邑人也。

translations.literal: Liang Mao, courtesy name Bofang, was a man of Changyi in Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Mao, styled Bofang, came from Changyi in Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 少好學，論議常據經典，以處是非。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; in debate he always relied on the classics to settle right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books from boyhood and anchored every argument in the canon.

sentences.zh: 太祖辟為司空掾，舉高第，補侍御史。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor summoned him as aide to the Minister of Works; he ranked highest and was appointed Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao hired him as an aide to the minister of works; he topped the rankings and became an attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 時泰山多盜賊，以茂為泰山太守，旬月之閒，襁負而至者千餘家。

translations.literal: At that time Mount Tai had many bandits; Mao was made Administrator of Mount Tai, and within a month or so over a thousand households arrived carrying infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tai swarmed with bandits, so Mao was sent as administrator; within weeks more than a thousand refugee families straggled in, babies bundled on their backs.

sentences.zh: 〈《博物記》曰：襁，織縷為之，廣八寸，長尺二，以約小兒於背上，負之而行。〉

translations.literal: The Bowu ji states: The carrying-cloth is woven from threads, eight inches wide and one foot two in length, used to bind a small child on the back and carry it while walking.
translations.idiomatic: (The Bowu ji explains the “back-bundle”: cloth eight inches wide and a foot long, slung to cradle an infant while walking.)

sentences.zh: 轉為樂浪太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Administrator of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as governor of Lelang commandery.

sentences.zh: 公孫度在遼東，擅留茂，不遣之官，然茂終不為屈。

translations.literal: Gongsun Du in Liaodong arbitrarily detained Mao and would not let him go to his post, yet Mao to the end did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du of Liaodong kept him under house arrest and blocked his posting, yet Mao never bent.

sentences.zh: 度謂茂及諸將曰：「聞曹公遠征，鄴無守備，今吾欲以步卒三萬，騎萬匹，直指鄴，誰能禦之？

translations.literal: Du said to Mao and the generals: "I hear that Lord Cao is on distant campaign and Ye has no garrison; now I wish to march thirty thousand foot and ten thousand horse straight against Ye—who can withstand me?"
translations.idiomatic: Du told Mao and his officers: “Cao Cao is far away and Ye lies undefended—I can strike with thirty thousand foot and ten thousand horse. Who will stop me?”

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The generals all said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The generals chorused their assent.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案此傳云公孫度聞曹公遠征，鄴無守備，則太祖定鄴後也。

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi notes: This biography says that Gongsun Du heard Lord Cao was on distant campaign and that Ye had no garrison, which would place the episode after Grand Progenitor had already settled Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi objects: the story has Gongsun Du speak as if Cao Cao were away and Ye weak only after Cao Cao had in fact taken Ye.

sentences.zh: 案

translations.literal: Investigating —
translations.idiomatic: His footnote continues —

sentences.zh: 〈度傳〉

translations.literal: the Biography of Du
translations.idiomatic: in Gongsun Du’s biography

sentences.zh: ，度以建安九年卒，太祖亦以此年定鄴，自後遠征，唯有北征柳城耳。

translations.literal: — Du died in the ninth year of Jian'an; Grand Progenitor also pacified Ye that same year. Afterward his distant campaigns were only the northern expedition against Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: — Du died in Jian’an 9, the very year Cao Cao took Ye. Later long campaigns were only the northern drive on Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 征柳城之年，度已不復在矣。〉

translations.literal: By the year of the Liucheng expedition Du was already dead.〉
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Liucheng campaign Du had been in the ground for years.)

sentences.zh: 又顧謂茂曰：「於君意何如？

translations.literal: He also turned to Mao and said, "What is your opinion of this?"
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Liang Mao he asked, “And you?”

sentences.zh: 」茂荅曰：「比者海內大亂，社稷將傾，將軍擁十萬之衆，安坐而觀成敗，夫為人臣者，固若是邪！

translations.literal: Mao replied: "Recently there has been great turmoil within the seas; the altars of soil and grain are about to topple. You, General, hold a host of a hundred thousand yet sit at ease watching success or failure—for a subject of another, should it indeed be thus!
translations.idiomatic: Mao answered: “The realm is tearing apart and the dynasty totters, yet you sit on a hundred thousand men and watch from the sidelines—can any loyal minister behave like that?

sentences.zh: 曹公憂國家之危敗，愍百姓之苦毒，率義兵為天下誅殘賊，功高而德廣，可謂無二矣。

translations.literal: Lord Cao grieves at the peril and ruin of the state and pities the bitter suffering of the common people; he leads righteous troops to execute the cruel rebels for the realm—his merit is high and his virtue broad; one may say he has no peer.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao mourns the empire’s peril and the people’s misery; he leads righteous armies against traitors—his achievements tower and his virtue spans the age.

sentences.zh: 以海內初定，民始安集，故未責將軍之罪耳！

translations.literal: Because the realm has only just been stabilized and the people have barely settled, he has not yet called you to account for your offenses!
translations.idiomatic: The land has barely quieted and families just begun to settle—that is why he has not yet punished you!

sentences.zh: 而將軍乃欲稱兵西向，則存亡之效，不崇朝而決。

translations.literal: Yet you, General, now wish to raise troops toward the west—the outcome of survival or destruction will be decided in less than a morning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would march west on Ye—your fate will be sealed before noon.

sentences.zh: 將軍其勉之！

translations.literal: General, exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Think twice, General.

sentences.zh: 」諸將聞茂言，皆震動。

translations.literal: When the generals heard Mao's words they were all shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The officers trembled at his rebuke.

sentences.zh: 良久，度曰：「涼君言是也。

translations.literal: After a long while Du said: "What Lord Liang says is right.
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence Du admitted, “He speaks truth.

sentences.zh: 」後徵遷為魏郡太守、甘陵相，所在有績。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and promoted to Administrator of Wei commandery and Chancellor of Ganling; wherever he went there were achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was later recalled to govern Wei commandery and Ganling principality, leaving a strong record at every post.

sentences.zh: 文帝為五官將，茂以選為長史，遷左軍師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was General of the Five Offices, Mao was selected as chief clerk and promoted to Left Army Master.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir, Wendi chose Mao as chief clerk of the Five Offices command and then raised him to master of the left army.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，遷尚書僕射，後為中尉奉常。

translations.literal: When Wei was first founded he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and later served as Commandant of Justice and Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Wei he became vice director of the secretariat, later commanding justice and court ritual.

sentences.zh: 文帝在東宮，茂復為太子太傅，甚見敬禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Heir Apparent, Mao again became Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and was greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi was crown prince, Mao served again as grand tutor and enjoyed singular esteem.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：茂名在八友中。〉

translations.literal: The Yingxiong ji states: Mao's name was among the Eight Friends.
translations.idiomatic: (The Yingxiong ji counts him among the “Eight Friends.”)

sentences.zh: 國淵字子尼，樂安蓋人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yuan, courtesy name Zini, was a man of Gai in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan, styled Zini, came from Gai county in Le’an.

sentences.zh: 師事鄭玄。

translations.literal: He studied under Zheng Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was a pupil of Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 〈《玄別傳》曰：淵始未知名，玄稱之曰：「國子尼，美才也，吾觀其人，必為國器。」〉

translations.literal: The separate biography of Xuan states: Yuan was at first not yet renowned; Xuan praised him, saying, "Guo Zini is a man of fine talent; observing this man, he will surely become a pillar of the state."〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zheng Xuan’s supplemental memoir: Before Yuan was famous, Zheng declared, “Guo Zini is brilliant—watch him become a pillar of the state.”)

sentences.zh: 後與邴原、管寧等避亂遼東。

translations.literal: Later with Bing Yuan, Guan Ning, and others he fled turmoil to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fled the fighting with Bing Yuan, Guan Ning, and company to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 〈王沈《魏書》曰：淵篤學好古，在遼東，常講學於山巖，士人多推慕之，由此知名。〉

translations.literal: Wang Chen's Wei Shu states: Yuan loved learning and antiquity; in Liaodong he often lectured on mountain cliffs; scholar-officials mostly admired him and he became renowned thereby.
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Chen’s Wei Shu: Yuan devoured the classics; on Liaodong’s cliffs he lectured until students flocked and his name spread.)

sentences.zh: 旣還舊土，太祖辟為司空掾屬，每於公朝論議，常直言正色，退無私焉。

translations.literal: After returning to his native soil Grand Progenitor summoned him as subordinate to the Minister of Works; at each court discussion he spoke frankly with stern countenance and in retirement showed no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he joined Cao Cao’s ministerial staff, spoke bluntly in council, and gave no favors behind closed doors.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲廣置屯田，使淵典其事。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor wished widely to establish military-agricultural colonies and ordered Yuan to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao planned widespread military colonies and put Yuan in charge.

sentences.zh: 淵屢陳損益，相土處民，計民置吏，明功課之法，五年中倉廩豐實，百姓競勸樂業。

translations.literal: Yuan repeatedly presented what to reduce and what to increase, assessed land and settled people, calculated people and placed officers, clarified the methods of merit assessment; within five years the granaries were full and the common people competed to take heart and delight in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He fine-tuned every regulation—surveying soil, settling households, assigning overseers, tying rewards to output—and within five years the bins overflowed while farmers rushed to the fields.

sentences.zh: 太祖征關中，以淵為居府長史，統留事。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor campaigned in Guanzhong he appointed Yuan chief clerk of the headquarters managing affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanzhong campaign Cao Cao named him chief clerk of rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 田銀、蘇伯反河閒，銀等旣破，後有餘黨，皆應伏法。

translations.literal: Tian Yin and Su Bo rebelled in Hejian; after Yin and the others were defeated there remained accomplices who all should have been executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yin and Su Bo rose in Hejian, scores of followers remained liable for execution after the leaders fell.

sentences.zh: 淵以為非首惡，請不行刑。

translations.literal: Yuan held they were not the chief culprits and requested that execution not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan argued they were not ringleaders and asked to spare them.

sentences.zh: 太祖從之，賴淵得生者千餘人。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor followed this; over a thousand persons owed their lives to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed; more than a thousand men lived because of Yuan’s plea.

sentences.zh: 破賊文書，舊以一為十，及淵上首級，如其實數。

translations.literal: In documents on defeating bandits it was formerly customary to report one as ten; when Yuan reported heads taken he used the true number.
translations.idiomatic: Victory bulletins usually multiplied kills tenfold; Yuan reported the actual tally.

sentences.zh: 太祖問其故，淵曰：「夫征討外寇，多其斬獲之數者，欲以大武功，且示民聽也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor asked the reason; Yuan said: "When campaigning against external foes, to inflate the count of those beheaded is to wish to magnify military achievement and moreover to show the people.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Yuan said: “Inflated body counts impress the realm when you fight foreign enemies.

sentences.zh: 河閒在封域之內，銀等叛逆，雖克捷有功，淵竊恥之。

translations.literal: Hejian lies within the sealed domain; Yin and the others were rebels—though we won a victory, I privately am ashamed of it."
translations.idiomatic: Hejian sits inside our borders—these men were fellow subjects in revolt. Victory here brings me no pride.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖大恱，遷魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor was greatly pleased and promoted him to Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Cao Cao named him governor of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 時有投書誹謗者，太祖疾之，欲必知其主。

translations.literal: At the time someone cast a calumnious letter; Grand Progenitor detested it and wished by all means to know its author.
translations.idiomatic: Someone circulated a slanderous pamphlet; Cao Cao burned to learn who wrote it.

sentences.zh: 淵請留其本書，而不宣露。

translations.literal: Yuan asked to keep the original document and not make it public.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan persuaded him to keep the original confidential.

sentences.zh: 其書多引二京賦，淵勑功曹曰：「此郡旣大，今在都輦，而少學問者。

translations.literal: The letter cited much from the Rhapsodies on the Two Capitals; Yuan instructed the Chief Clerk: "This commandery is large and now lies in the capital region, yet there are few learned men.
translations.idiomatic: The tract quoted Zhang Heng’s Two Capitals rhapsodies, so Yuan told his chief clerk: “We are a large commandery at the capital’s edge, yet scholars are scarce.

sentences.zh: 其簡開解年少，欲遣就師。

translations.literal: Select and enroll promising youths and send them to teachers."
translations.idiomatic: Round up bright young men and enroll them with tutors.”

sentences.zh: 」功曹差三人，臨遣引見，訓以「所學未及，二京賦，博物之書也，世人忽略，少有其師，可求能讀者從受之。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk assigned three men; as they were about to depart he introduced them and instructed them that "your studies are not yet advanced—the Rhapsodies on the Two Capitals are works of broad learning; the world neglects them and few have teachers—seek those who can read them and study under them."
translations.idiomatic: He picked three candidates and, seeing them off, announced that their schooling needed polish—the Two Capitals texts were encyclopedic rarities rarely taught—and ordered them to find masters who could parse them.

sentences.zh: 」又密喻旨。

translations.literal: He also secretly conveyed his true intent.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he explained the real purpose.

sentences.zh: 旬日得能讀者，遂往受業。

translations.literal: Within ten days they found those who could read and went to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days tutors appeared and lessons began.

sentences.zh: 吏因請使作箋，比方其書，與投書人同手。

translations.literal: The clerks then asked them to compose letters; comparing the handwriting to the letter, it matched the letter-writer's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks then had the students draft samples—the script matched the pamphlet exactly.

sentences.zh: 收攝案問，具得情理。

translations.literal: They seized, questioned, and examined the case and obtained the full truth.
translations.idiomatic: Arrest and interrogation broke the case wide open.

sentences.zh: 遷太僕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand coachman of the court.

sentences.zh: 居列卿位，布衣蔬食，祿賜散之舊故宗族，以恭儉自守，卒官。

translations.literal: While holding ministerial rank among the Nine Ministers he wore plain cloth and ate coarse greens; stipends and gifts he distributed to old associates and his lineage, guarding himself in respectful thrift; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Though he ranked among the Nine Ministers, he dressed like a commoner and ate simply, passing every stipend to kinsmen and old friends; he died as poor as he had lived.

sentences.zh: 〈王沈《魏書》曰：太祖以其子泰為郎。〉

translations.literal: The Wei Shu by Wang Chen states: Grand Progenitor appointed his son Tai as a Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Chen’s Wei Shu notes that Cao Cao gave Yuan Tai a place among the Gentlemen.)

sentences.zh: 田疇字子泰，右北平無終人也。

translations.literal: Tian Chou, courtesy name Zitai, was a man of Wuzhong in Right Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou, styled Zitai, came from Wuzhong in Right Beiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 好讀書、擊劒。

translations.literal: He loved reading books and practicing swordsmanship.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and fencing.

sentences.zh: 初平元年，義兵起，董卓遷帝于長安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuping the righteous armies rose and Dong Zhuo moved the emperor to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 190 CE coalition forces rose while Dong Zhuo dragged the court west to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 幽州牧劉虞歎曰：「賊臣作亂，朝廷播蕩，四海俄然，莫有固志。

translations.literal: Shepherd Liu Yu of Youzhou sighed: "Treacherous ministers make rebellion; the court is driven about; within the four seas all is suddenly adrift and none holds firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Yu of Youzhou mourned: “Rebel ministers hold the emperor hostage; the realm reels and no one knows where to stand.

sentences.zh: 身備宗室遺老，不得自同於衆。

translations.literal: I, though fitted out as a remnant elder of the imperial house, cannot deem myself the same as the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I carry the imperial surname—I cannot hide among ordinary folk.

sentences.zh: 今欲奉使展效臣節，安得不辱命之士乎？

translations.literal: Now I wish to dispatch an envoy to display a subject's devotion—how can I do without a man who will not disgrace his commission?"
translations.idiomatic: I need an envoy who can prove loyalty without losing face—where else will I find such a man?”

sentences.zh: 」衆議咸曰：「田疇雖年少，多稱其奇。

translations.literal: All in council said: "Though Tian Chou is young, many praise his extraordinariness.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly answered: “Tian Chou is young, but everyone calls him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 」疇時年二十二矣。

translations.literal: Chou was then twenty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 虞乃備禮請與相見，大恱之，遂署為從事，具其車騎。

translations.literal: Yu then prepared full ceremony and requested an audience, was greatly pleased, thereupon appointed him Attendant Clerk and fully provided carriage and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu received him with full honors, delighted in the interview, named him an attendant clerk, and furnished wagons and escort.

sentences.zh: 將行，疇曰：「今道路阻絕，寇虜縱橫，稱官奉使，為衆所指名。

translations.literal: About to depart, Chou said: "Now roads are blocked and bandits roam freely; calling oneself an official envoy makes one the target of every eye.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he urged: “The roads are closed and bandits swarm—a titled envoy draws every outlaw’s eye.

sentences.zh: 願以私行，期於得達而已。

translations.literal: I wish to travel as a private person, hoping only to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Let me travel as a private scholar—only reaching Chang’an matters.

sentences.zh: 」虞從之。

translations.literal: Yu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 疇乃歸，自選其家客與年少之勇壯慕從者二十騎俱往。

translations.literal: Chou then returned home and personally selected twenty riders from his household retainers and stalwart youths who admired him and wished to follow.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and picked twenty armed retainers willing to ride with him.

sentences.zh: 虞自出祖而遣之。

translations.literal: Yu personally went out to perform the farewell ritual and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu himself hosted the farewell feast and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 〈《先賢行狀》曰：疇將行，引虞密與議。

translations.literal: The Conduct of Former Worthies states: When Chou was about to depart he drew Yu aside for secret consultation.
translations.idiomatic: (The Conduct of Former Worthies: Before departure Tian Chou took Liu Yu aside.

sentences.zh: 疇因說虞曰：「今帝主幼弱，姧臣擅命，表上須報，懼失事機。

translations.literal: Chou therefore urged Yu: "Now the sovereign lord is young and weak and wicked ministers monopolize commands; memorials submitted upward must await reply—I fear losing the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: He warned: “The boy emperor is a pawn and corrupt ministers hold real power; waiting for court approval wastes precious time.

sentences.zh: 且公孫瓚阻兵安忍，不早圖之，必有後悔。

translations.literal: Moreover Gongsun Zan holds troops and is habitually cruel—if you do not plan against him early you will surely regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan commands troops and kills without mercy—move against him now or repent later.

sentences.zh: 」虞不聽。〉

translations.literal: Yu did not listen.〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu would not listen.)

sentences.zh: 旣取道，疇乃更上西關，出塞，傍北方，直趣朔方，循閒徑去，遂至長安致命。

translations.literal: Having taken the road, Chou altered course to ascend the western pass, exited the frontier, kept along the northern edge, went straight to Shuofang, followed hidden bypaths, and thus reached Chang'an and delivered his charge.
translations.idiomatic: He swung northwest through the passes, skirted the steppe to Shuofang, slipped past patrols, and delivered Liu Yu’s memorial at Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 詔拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: An imperial edict appointed him Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 疇以為天子方蒙塵未安，不可以荷佩榮寵，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Chou held that the Son of Heaven was still in exile and unrest had not ceased—he could not bear insignia of glory and firmly declined without accepting.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the commission while the emperor remained a fugitive—honors felt obscene.

sentences.zh: 朝廷高其義。

translations.literal: The court esteemed his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 三府並辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: The Three Offices jointly summoned him; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: All three senior ministries called him; he ignored every summons.

sentences.zh: 得報，馳還，未至，虞已為公孫瓚所害。

translations.literal: Having obtained the reply he rode swiftly back—before he arrived Yu had already been murdered by Gongsun Zan.
translations.idiomatic: He raced home with the emperor’s answer but Liu Yu was already dead at Gongsun Zan’s hands.

sentences.zh: 疇至，謁祭虞墓，陳發章表，哭泣而去。

translations.literal: When Chou arrived he visited Yu's tomb for sacrifice, displayed and read aloud the memorials, wept, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He rode straight to Liu Yu’s grave, read the imperial rescripts aloud, wept, and left.

sentences.zh: 瓚聞之大怒，購求獲疇，謂曰：「汝何自哭劉虞墓，而不送章報於我也？

translations.literal: When Zan heard of it he was furious, offered a reward and seized Chou, saying: "Why do you weep at Liu Yu's tomb yet not deliver the memorial to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan flew into a rage, had Tian Chou seized, and demanded: “Why mourn Liu Yu but hide the emperor’s letter from me?”

sentences.zh: 」疇荅曰：「漢室衰穨，人懷異心，唯劉公不失忠節。

translations.literal: Chou replied: "The house of Han declines and every man harbors a different heart—only Lord Liu did not abandon loyal principle.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou answered: “The Han totters and loyalty is rare—only Liu Yu kept faith.

sentences.zh: 章報所言，於將軍未美，恐非所樂聞，故不進也。

translations.literal: What the memorial reports would not speak well of you—I feared it was not what you would delight to hear, therefore I did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: That document praises virtues you lack—I doubt you wanted to hear it.

sentences.zh: 且將軍方舉大事以求所欲，旣滅無罪之君，又讎守義之臣，誠行此事，則燕、趙之士將皆蹈東海而死耳，豈忍有從將軍者乎！

translations.literal: Moreover you, General, now undertake great affairs seeking what you desire—having already destroyed a guiltless lord and made enemy of a minister who kept faith—if you truly carry this through, then men of Yan and Zhao will all cast themselves into the Eastern Sea to die—how could they bear to follow you!"
translations.idiomatic: You slaughtered an innocent patron and brand loyalty as crime—carry on like this and every north-China knight will drown himself before he serves you!”

sentences.zh: 」瓚壯其對，釋不誅也。

translations.literal: Zan admired his reply and released him without executing.
translations.idiomatic: Zan respected the nerve of it and spared him.

sentences.zh: 拘之軍下，禁其故人莫得與通。

translations.literal: He detained him under the army and forbade his old associates from communicating with him.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Tian Chou under military arrest and cut him off from friends.

sentences.zh: 或說瓚曰：「田疇義士，君弗能禮，而又囚之，恐失衆心。

translations.literal: Someone advised Zan: "Tian Chou is a man of principle—you cannot honor him yet imprison him—I fear losing popular hearts."
translations.idiomatic: An adviser warned: “Tian Chou is a hero—jailing him after failing to win him will cost you hearts.

sentences.zh: 」瓚乃縱遣疇。

translations.literal: Zan thereupon released Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Zan let him go.

sentences.zh: 疇得北歸，率舉宗族他附從數百人，埽地而盟曰：「君仇不報，吾不可以立於世！

translations.literal: Chou was able to return north; he gathered his lineage and several hundred followers who attached themselves to him, swept the ground and swore an oath: "My lord's vengeance unavenged—I cannot stand in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Free again, he rallied kin and followers, swept earth for an oath, and swore: “Until Liu Yu is avenged I have no place under Heaven!”

sentences.zh: 」遂人徐無山中，營深險平敞地而居，躬耕以養父母。

translations.literal: He then entered the Xu Wu mountains, camped on ground deep, defensible, level, and open, and personally plowed fields to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew into the Xu Wu range, built a settlement on a sheltered plateau, and farmed to feed their families.

sentences.zh: 百姓歸之，數年閒至五千餘家。

translations.literal: Common people attached themselves to him; within several years they reached over five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees streamed in until more than five thousand households gathered.

sentences.zh: 疇謂其父老曰：「諸君不以疇不肖，遠來相就。

translations.literal: Chou said to the elders: "You gentlemen do not despise Chou's lack of talent but come from afar to join me.
translations.idiomatic: He told the headmen: “You honor me though I am unworthy and trek here from afar.

sentences.zh: 衆成都邑，而莫相統一，恐非久安之道，願推擇其賢長者以為之主。

translations.literal: The multitude forms a settlement yet none unifies rule—I fear this is not the way to long-term peace; I wish to choose and elevate the worthy elder among you to be chief.
translations.idiomatic: We have become a town without government—that invites chaos. Choose the worthiest among you to lead.

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: All said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: They shouted approval.

sentences.zh: 」同僉推疇。

translations.literal: Together they nominated Chou.
translations.idiomatic: They elected Tian Chou.

sentences.zh: 疇曰：「今來在此，非苟安而已，將圖大事，復怨雪恥。

translations.literal: Chou said: "Those who have come here do not seek mere safety—we intend great affairs, to restore vengeance and wipe away shame.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: “We did not flee here for comfort—we came to settle scores with Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 竊恐未得其志，而輕薄之徒自相侵侮，偷快一時，無深計遠慮。

translations.literal: I secretly fear that before intent is achieved shallow men will insult one another among themselves, stealing pleasure for a moment without deep plans or far-reaching thought.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we impose order, hotheads will brawl for petty gain and ruin everything.

sentences.zh: 疇有愚計，願與諸君共施之，可乎？

translations.literal: Chou has a foolish plan—I wish to enact it together with you gentlemen—is it acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: I propose a simple code—will you adopt it?”

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「可。

translations.literal: All said: "It is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: They agreed.

sentences.zh: 」疇乃為約束相殺傷、犯盜、諍訟之法，法重者至死，其次抵罪，二十餘條。

translations.literal: Chou then drafted regulations for mutual killing and wounding, theft, and litigation—those heavily liable faced death, lesser offenses redeemed punishment—more than twenty articles.
translations.idiomatic: He promulgated twenty-odd statutes covering homicide, theft, and lawsuits—capital crimes for the worst, fines or labor for lesser faults.

sentences.zh: 又制為婚姻嫁娶之禮，興舉學校講授之業，班行其衆，衆皆便之，至道不拾遺。

translations.literal: He further instituted ritual for marriage and wedding, raised schools for lectures and instruction, promulgated these among the multitude—all found them convenient; lost goods went unclaimed on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He added marriage customs, opened schools, and taught the rules until travelers could drop purses untouched.

sentences.zh: 北邊翕然服其威信，烏丸、鮮卑並各遣譯使致貢遺，疇悉撫納，令不為寇。

translations.literal: The northern frontier uniformly submitted to his prestige and good faith; Wuhuan and Xianbei each sent interpreters bearing tribute—Chou soothed and accepted them all and ordered them not to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Steppe tribes deferred to him; Wuhuan and Xianbei envoys arrived with gifts, and he kept them from raiding Han settlements.

sentences.zh: 袁紹數遣使招命，又即授將軍印，因安輯所統，疇皆拒不受。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao repeatedly dispatched envoys with summons and immediately conferred a general's seal to pacify those under his rule—Chou refused every offer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao courted him with repeated missions and even tried to buy him with a general’s seal—Tian Chou refused each time.

sentences.zh: 紹死，其子尚又辟焉，疇終不行。

translations.literal: When Shao died his son Shang again summoned him—Chou to the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao died Yuan Shang summoned him again—still no answer.

sentences.zh: 疇常忿烏丸昔多賊殺其郡冠蓋，有欲討之意而力未能。

translations.literal: Chou constantly resented that the Wuhuan in former times had often murdered officials of his commandery—he wished to punish them but strength was not yet sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He burned to punish the Wuhuan for slaughtering Youzhou officials but lacked the force.

sentences.zh: 建安十二年，太祖北征烏丸，未至，先遣使辟疇，又命田預喻指。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jian'an Grand Progenitor campaigned north against the Wuhuan; before arriving he first dispatched an envoy to summon Chou and also ordered Tian Yu to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: In 207 CE Cao Cao marched against the Wuhuan; before the army arrived he summoned Tian Chou through Tian Yu.

sentences.zh: 疇戒其門下趣治嚴。

translations.literal: Chou instructed those of his gate to hurry and prepare baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou told his household to pack at once.

sentences.zh: 門人謂曰：「昔袁公慕君，禮命五至，君義不屈；

translations.literal: His retainers said to him: "Formerly Lord Yuan admired you—ceremonial summons came five times yet you remained righteous and unbending;
translations.idiomatic: His followers protested: “Yuan Shao honored you with five respectful summons and you stayed put;

sentences.zh: 今曹公使一來而君若恐弗及者，何也？

translations.literal: now Lord Cao's single envoy comes and you seem afraid not to catch up—why?"
translations.idiomatic: yet one word from Cao Cao sends you scrambling—why?”

sentences.zh: 」疇笑而應之曰：「此非君所識也。

translations.literal: Chou smiled and replied to them: "This is not something you gentlemen understand.
translations.idiomatic: Smiling, he said: “That is not for you to judge.

sentences.zh: 」遂隨使者到軍，署司空戶曹掾，引見諮議。

translations.literal: He then followed the envoy to the army, was appointed aide in the Household Bureau of the Minister of Works, was introduced and consulted.
translations.idiomatic: He rode to camp, took a temporary post in the minister’s household bureau, and briefed Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 明日出令曰：「田子泰非吾所宜吏者。

translations.literal: The next day an order was issued: "Tian Zitai is not someone I should employ as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning Cao Cao announced: “Tian Zitai is wasted on clerical duty.

sentences.zh: 」即舉茂才，拜為蓨令，不之官，隨軍次無終。

translations.literal: He immediately nominated him maocai and appointed him Magistrate of Tiao—Chou did not go to his office but followed the army and camped at Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated him recommended talent and named him magistrate of Tiao—knowing Tian Chou would not sit a desk, he kept him with the host at Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 時方夏水雨，而濵海洿下，濘滯不通，虜亦遮守蹊要，軍不得進。

translations.literal: At that time it was summer with rains; the coastal lowlands were sunken and muddy so that passage was blocked—the barbarians also guarded the narrow defiles—the army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Summer rains turned the coastal flats to mud while tribal pickets held the passes—the army stalled.

sentences.zh: 太祖患之，以問疇。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor worried over this and questioned Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao turned to Tian Chou for another route.

sentences.zh: 疇曰：「此道，秋夏每常有水，淺不通車馬，深不載舟船，為難久矣。

translations.literal: Chou said: "On this route, autumn and summer alike constantly have water—when shallow it does not admit carts and horses; when deep it does not float boats—it has been difficult for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He explained: “This coast floods summer and fall—too shallow for boats, too soft for wagons.

sentences.zh: 舊北平郡治在平岡，道出盧龍，達于柳城；

translations.literal: The old seat of Beiping commandery was at Pinggang—the road exited at Lulong and reached Liucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Old maps show the road from Pinggang through Lulong to Liucheng;

sentences.zh: 自建武以來，陷壞斷絕，垂二百載，而尚有微徑可從。

translations.literal: since the Jianwu era it has collapsed and been cut off—nearly two hundred years—yet a faint track still may be followed.
translations.idiomatic: It fell into ruin two centuries ago but a hunter’s trace remains.

sentences.zh: 今虜將以大軍當由無終，不得進而退，懈弛無備。

translations.literal: Now the enemy will expect the great army must come by way of Wuzhong—unable to advance they will retreat—slack and unprepared.
