translations.idiomatic: The tribes watch Wuzhong—the dead end we just quit—so they relax.

sentences.zh: 若嘿回軍，從盧龍口越白檀之險，出空虛之地，路近而便，掩其不備，蹋頓之首可不戰而禽也。

translations.literal: If we silently wheel the army back, cross the peril of White Sand from Lulongkou, emerge into empty terrain—the road is near and convenient—strike them unprepared—and Taodun's head may be taken without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Double back through Lulong Pass, burst onto the plateau behind them, and we could seize Taodun’s head without a pitched battle.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said: “Do it.”

sentences.zh: 」乃引軍還，而署大木表於水側路傍曰：「方今暑夏，道路不通，且俟秋冬，乃復進軍。

translations.literal: He then led the army back and posted large wooden notices by the waterside road stating: "Now in the heat of summer roads are impassable—wait until autumn and winter then advance the army again."
translations.idiomatic: They feigned retreat and nailed notices to trees: “Summer mud blocks us—we return in autumn.

sentences.zh: 」虜候騎見之，誠以為大軍去也。

translations.literal: Enemy scouts saw it and truly believed the great army had departed.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal scouts mistook the withdrawal for real.

sentences.zh: 太祖令疇將其衆為鄉導，上徐無山，出盧龍，歷平岡，登白狼堆，去柳城二百餘里，虜乃驚覺。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor ordered Chou to lead his people as guides—ascended Xu Wu mountain, exited Lulong, passed Pinggang, climbed Bailang pile—two hundred-some li from Liucheng—the enemy then became alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou guided the column up Xu Wu, through Lulong and Pinggang, over Bailang Mountain within two hundred li of Liucheng before the Wuhuan reacted.

sentences.zh: 單于身自臨陣，太祖與交戰，遂大斬獲，追奔逐北，至柳城。

translations.literal: The Chanyu personally came to the battlefield; Grand Progenitor engaged him in battle and thereupon achieved great slaughter—pursuing the fleeing north they reached Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu rode out to fight; Cao Cao shattered the horde and chased them to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 軍還入塞，論功行封，封疇亭侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When the army returned inside the frontier they assessed merit and enacted enfeoffments—Chou was enfeoffed Village Marquis with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Back inside the Wall he enfeoffed Tian Chou as a village marquis at five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 〈《先賢行狀》載太祖表論疇功曰：「文雅優備，忠武又著，和於撫下，慎於事上，量時度理，進退合義。

translations.literal: The Conduct of Former Worthies carries Grand Progenitor's memorial assessing Chou's merit: "Cultured grace fully prepared, loyalty and martial prowess equally evident, harmonious in soothing subordinates, careful in serving superiors—measuring times and principles, advancing and retreating accord with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: (His citation praised Tian Chou’s civil polish, martial nerve, care for troops and superiors, and timely judgment.

sentences.zh: 幽州始擾，胡、漢交萃，蕩析離居，靡所依懷。

translations.literal: Youzhou first was disturbed—Hu and Han mingled—scattered and dwelling apart—with nowhere to cling for shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou had shattered—steppe and Han peoples mingled in flight.

sentences.zh: 疇率宗人避難於無終山，北拒盧龍，南守要害，清靜隱約，耕而後食，人民化從，咸共資奉。

translations.literal: Chou led his clansmen to take refuge in the Xu Wu mountains—resisting Lulong to the north and guarding key points to the south—quiet, hidden, approximate—plowing first then eating—the people transformed and followed—all jointly supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou led kin into Xu Wu, blocking Lulong pass and guarding southern narrows while farming in quiet until thousands sustained him.

sentences.zh: 及袁紹父子威力加於朔野，遠結烏丸，與為首尾，前後召疇，終不陷撓。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao father and son extended their might over the northern wilds and far allied the Wuhuan as head and tail—summoning Chou repeatedly—he never yielded or bent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuans dominated the north and allied the Wuhuan, Tian Chou still ignored every summons.

sentences.zh: 後臣奉命，軍次易縣，疇長驅自到，陳討胡之勢，猶廣武之建燕策，薛公之度淮南。

translations.literal: Later your servant received command—the army halted at Yi county—Chou came at full gallop on his own initiative and laid out the plan against the Hu—like Guangwu's establishing Yan strategy or Duke Xue's estimating Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When this army camped at Yi, Tian Chou raced in with a strategy worthy of Guangwu’s Yan plan or Xue Gong’s Huainan calculus.

sentences.zh: 又使部曲持臣露布，出誘胡衆，漢民或因亡來，烏丸聞之震蕩。

translations.literal: Your servant also ordered retainers to carry your servant's open proclamation going out to lure the Hu multitude—Han people thereby fled to join—when the Wuhuan heard it they were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Agents waved edicts on the frontier; Han refugees slipped through while Wuhuan morale cracked.

sentences.zh: 王旅出塞，塗由山中九百餘里，疇帥兵五百，啟導山谷，遂威烏丸，蕩平塞表。

translations.literal: The royal army exited the frontier—the route through the mountains exceeded nine hundred li—Chou commanded five hundred troops—opening and guiding the valleys—thereupon awed the Wuhuan and swept the frontier clean.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial column marched nine hundred li of mountain track behind Tian Chou’s five hundred pioneers until the Wuhuan broke.

sentences.zh: 疇文武有效，節義可嘉，誠應寵賞，以旌其美。」〉

translations.literal: Chou effective in civil and military affairs—integrity commendable—truly should receive favor and reward—to signal his excellence."〉
translations.idiomatic: Reward him,’ the memorial thundered ‘for deeds civil and martial.’)

sentences.zh: 疇自以始為居難，率衆循逃，志義不立，反以為利，非本意也，固讓。

translations.literal: Chou himself thought that at the beginning he had faced hardship and led the multitude in flight—ambition and righteousness had not been established—yet he gained profit thereby—it was not his original intent—he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou refused the fief: he had fled disaster, not sought fortune.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其至心，許而不奪。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor knew his utmost sincerity and permitted him without forcing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao understood and did not insist.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載太祖令曰：「昔伯成棄國，夏后不奪，將欲使高尚之士，優賢之主，不止於一世也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu carries Grand Progenitor's order: "Formerly Bocheng abandoned his state and the Xia lord did not seize him—the intent was to allow lofty gentlemen and rulers who esteem worthies not to stop at one generation.
translations.idiomatic: (Wei Shu preserves Cao Cao’s comparison to the sage who refused office—honor men who spurn titles.

sentences.zh: 其聽疇所執。」〉

translations.literal: Hear what Chou insists upon."〉
translations.idiomatic: Let Tian Chou have his way.’)

sentences.zh: 遼東斬送袁尚首，令「三軍敢有哭之者斬」。

translations.literal: Liaodong decapitated Yuan Shang and sent his head—ordering that "whoever of the three armies dares weep shall be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong shipped Yuan Shang’s head south with orders to execute anyone who mourned.

sentences.zh: 疇以甞為尚所辟，乃往弔祭。

translations.literal: Because Chou had once been summoned by Shang he went to mourn and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou had once served Yuan Shang’s summons, so he offered incense anyway.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦不問。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor also did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為田疇不應袁紹父子之命，以其非正也。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Tian Chou ought not to have answered summons from Yuan Shao father and son—because they lacked legitimacy.
translations.idiomatic: (Pei Songzhi argues Tian Chou rightly ignored the Yuans as usurpers.

sentences.zh: 故盡規魏祖，建盧龍之策。

translations.literal: Therefore he laid full plans for Wei's ancestor and devised the Lulong strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he mapped the Lulong raid for Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 致使袁尚奔迸，授首遼東，皆疇之由也。

translations.literal: It caused Yuan Shang to flee in panic and lose his head in Liaodong—all came about because of Chou.
translations.idiomatic: That route drove Yuan Shang to his death—credit Tian Chou.

sentences.zh: 旣已明其為賊，胡為復弔祭其首乎？

translations.literal: Having already shown him to be a rebel—why again mourn and sacrifice to his head?
translations.idiomatic: Having branded him traitor, why mourn his skull?

sentences.zh: 若以甞被辟命，義在其中，則不應為人設謀，使其至此也。

translations.literal: If because he once received summons—righteousness lay therein—then he ought not to have devised stratagems that brought him to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: If past patronage bound him, he should never have plotted Yuan Shang’s ruin.

sentences.zh: 疇此舉止，良為進退無當，與王脩哭袁譚，貌同而心異也。〉

translations.literal: Chou's conduct in this matter—truly improper in advance and retreat—it shares outward appearance with Wang Xiu weeping for Yuan Tan yet the heart differs.〉
translations.idiomatic: His mourning contradicted his strategy—superficially like Wang Xiu weeping for Yuan Tan but morally elsewhere.)

sentences.zh: 疇盡將其家屬及宗人三百餘家居鄴。

translations.literal: Chou moved his entire household and more than three hundred persons of his lineage to dwell at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated three hundred kinsmen to Ye.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜疇車馬穀帛，皆散之宗族知舊。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor gifted Chou carriages, horses, grain, and silk—all he distributed to his lineage and old acquaintances.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao showered him with goods; he passed everything to relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 從征荊州還，太祖追念疇功殊美，恨前聽疇之讓，曰：「是成一人之志，而虧王法大制也。

translations.literal: Returning from the campaign in Jing Province, Grand Progenitor pursued his thoughts on Chou's merit being especially fine—he regretted earlier having listened to Chou's declination—saying: "This fulfills one man's aspiration yet harms the great institutions of royal law.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jingzhou campaign Cao Cao brooded: indulging Tian Chou’s modesty had slighted public law.

sentences.zh: 」於是乃復以前爵封疇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again enfeoffed Chou with the former noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: He reissued the original marquisate.

sentences.zh: 〈《先賢行狀》載太祖令曰：「蓨令田疇，志節高尚，遭值州里戎夏交亂，引身深山，研精味道，百姓從之，以成都邑。

translations.literal: The Conduct of Former Worthies carries Grand Progenitor's order: "Magistrate of Tiao Tian Chou—loftiness of intent and integrity—encountering barbarian turmoil in the commandery—he withdrew into deep mountains—refined learning and tasted the Way—the common people followed him until they formed a city.
translations.idiomatic: (Another edict recounts how Tian Chou fled chaos, studied in the hills, and founded a settlement.

sentences.zh: 袁賊之盛，命召不屈。

translations.literal: At the Yuan rebels' strength—summoned yet refused—unbending.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the Yuans were strongest he spurned their calls.

sentences.zh: 慷慨守志，以徼真主。

translations.literal: Generously guarding his resolve, he thereby awaited a true lord.
translations.idiomatic: He kept faith through chaos while watching for a legitimate sovereign.

sentences.zh: 及孤奉詔征定河北，遂服幽都，將定胡寇，特加禮命。

translations.literal: When I received the edict to campaign and pacify Hebei, then subdued Youdu and was about to settle the Hu bandits, I specially increased ritual summons.
translations.idiomatic: Once I held the emperor’s mandate to pacify the north, crush Youzhou, and strike the Hu, I courted him with unusual ceremony.

sentences.zh: 疇即受署，陳建攻胡蹊路所由，率齊山民，一時向化，開塞導道，供承使役，路近而便，令虜不意。

translations.literal: Chou immediately accepted appointment, laid out by what roads to attack the Hu, aligned the mountain people who at once turned to civilization, opened the passes and guided the route, supplying labor service—the road was near and convenient so the enemy did not expect it.
translations.idiomatic: He took office, mapped the mountain tracks, rallied local clans, opened the passes, and supplied guides so Cao Cao caught the tribes flat-footed.

sentences.zh: 斬蹋頓於白狼，遂長驅於柳城，疇有力焉。

translations.literal: Taodun was beheaded at Bailang; then they drove deep to Liucheng—Chou had strength therein.
translations.idiomatic: Taodun fell at Bailang and the army raced to Liucheng—Tian Chou made that blow possible.

sentences.zh: 及軍入塞，將圖其功，表封亭侯，食邑五百，而疇懇惻，前後辭賞。

translations.literal: When the army entered the frontier passes and planned to register merit, the memorial enfeoffed him Village Marquis with five hundred households—yet Chou earnestly and sorrowfully declined rewards before and after.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign Cao Cao listed his deeds and offered a village at five hundred households—Tian Chou refused again and again.

sentences.zh: 出入三載，歷年未賜，此為成一人之高，甚違王典，失之多矣。

translations.literal: Going out and coming in three years—years passed without grant—this achieves one man's loftiness yet greatly violates royal norms—the loss is much.
translations.idiomatic: Three years of honors deferred served his scruples but mocked the law of rewards.

sentences.zh: 宜從表封，無久留吾過。」〉

translations.literal: You should follow the memorial enfeoffment—do not long leave my fault."〉
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoff him now and spare me the scandal of stinginess.”)

sentences.zh: 疇上疏陳誠，以死自誓。

translations.literal: Chou submitted a memorial stating sincerity and swore by death.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou petitioned in tears and swore he would die before taking the fief.

sentences.zh: 太祖不聽，欲引拜之，至于數四，終不受。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor would not listen—he wished to summon him to appointment—reaching four or five times—Chou to the end did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao kept pressing appointments; Tian Chou refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 有司劾疇狷介違道，苟立小節，宜免官加刑。

translations.literal: The responsible officials impeached Chou as stubbornly isolated, violating the Way, hastily establishing petty integrity—the appropriate thing was to dismiss from office and add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry charged him with obstructing policy—some demanded stripes as well as dismissal.

sentences.zh: 太祖重其事，依違者久之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor took the matter seriously and vacillated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao hesitated, unwilling to punish integrity.

sentences.zh: 乃下世子及大臣博議，世子以疇同於子文辭祿，申胥逃賞，宜勿奪以優其節。

translations.literal: He then issued to the heir apparent and great ministers for broad deliberation—the heir apparent held Chou the same as Ziwen declining salary and Shenxu fleeing reward—one should not strip him in order to honor his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He polled the court; the crown prince likened Tian Chou to ancient worthies who spurned pay so virtue might shine.

sentences.zh: 尚書令荀彧、司隷校尉鍾繇亦以為可聽。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Xun Yu and Colonel Director of Retainers Zhong Yao also held that he could be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu and Zhong Yao agreed he should keep his pride.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載世子議曰：「昔薳敖逃祿，傳載其美，所以激濁世，勵貪夫，賢於尸祿素餐飡之人也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu carries the heir apparent's deliberation: "Formerly Wei Ao fled salary—the transmitted records carry his beauty—in order to stir a muddy age and encourage greedy men—better than those who hold corpse salaries and eat white meals.
translations.idiomatic: (Wei Shu records the heir comparing Tian Chou to Wei Ao, who refused salary to shame the greedy.

sentences.zh: 故可得而小，不可得而毀。

translations.literal: Therefore he may be lightly treated but cannot be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Such men may seem odd but must not be crushed.

sentences.zh: 至於田疇，方斯近矣。

translations.literal: As for Tian Chou—he is near to this.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou belongs in that company.

sentences.zh: 免官加刑，於法為重。

translations.literal: To dismiss from office and add punishment—in law is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Stripping and scourging him would be wildly disproportionate.

sentences.zh: 」《魏略》載教曰：「昔夷、齊棄爵而譏武王，可謂愚闇，孔子猶以為『求仁得仁』。

translations.literal: The Wei lue carries an edict: "Formerly Yi and Qi abandoned noble rank and mocked King Wu—one may call them foolish and dark—yet Confucius still thought them 'seeking benevolence and obtaining benevolence.'
translations.idiomatic: Another edict cited Boyi and Shuqi—even Confucius called their stubbornness “seeking humanity.

sentences.zh: 疇之所守，雖不合道，但欲清高耳。

translations.literal: What Chou guards—though it does not match the great principle—only wishes lofty purity.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou may miss the big political picture—he only wants a clean name.

sentences.zh: 使天下悉如疇志，即墨翟兼愛尚同之事，而老聃使民結繩之道也。

translations.literal: Supposing all under Heaven were entirely like Chou's intent—then it would be Mozi's universal love and upward sameness—and Laozi's way of causing the people to knot cords.
translations.idiomatic: If everyone behaved so, we would live in Mozi’s communal utopia or Laozi’s primordial village.

sentences.zh: 外議欲為復使令司隷決之。

translations.literal: Outside discussion wished again to have the Director of the Metropolitan Region decide it.
translations.idiomatic: Some wanted the metropolitan commandant to rule on the case.

sentences.zh: 」魏書載荀彧議，以為「君子之道，或出或處，期於為善而已。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu carries Xun Yu's deliberation, holding that "the way of the gentleman—sometimes emerging sometimes withdrawing—ends in doing good, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said a gentleman serves or retreats as duty demands.

sentences.zh: 故匹夫守志，聖人各因而成之」。

translations.literal: Therefore when a common man guards resolve—the sages each complete him accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: The sages bless stubborn integrity when it serves good.

sentences.zh: 鍾繇以為「原思辭粟，仲尼不與，子路拒牛，謂之止善，雖可以激清勵濁，猶不足多也。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao held that "Yuan Si declined grain—Confucius did not approve—Zilu refused an ox—this was called stopping goodness—though it can stir the clear and encourage the muddy—it is still not enough to praise much.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao cited Confucius scolding Yuan Si for refusing pay—pure gestures can discourage charity.

sentences.zh: 疇雖不合大義，有益推讓之風，宜如世子議。

translations.literal: Chou though does not match great righteousness—there is benefit to the wind of yielding—one should follow the heir apparent's deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Tian Chou errs on piety, let him model humility.

sentences.zh: 」臣松之案《呂氏春秋》：「魯國之法，魯人有為臣妾於諸侯，有能贖之者取其金於府。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates the Lüshi chunqiu: "Lu state's law—when Lu people became servants or concubines in feudal states—whoever could ransom them took gold from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi cites Lü Buwei: Lu paid citizens to ransom slaves from other states.

sentences.zh: 子貢贖人而辭不受金，孔子曰：『賜失之矣。

translations.literal: Zigong ransomed someone but declined accepting gold—Confucius said 'Ci missed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong refused reimbursement—Confucius scolded him.

sentences.zh: 自今以來魯人不贖矣。

translations.literal: From now on Lu people will not ransom.
translations.idiomatic: No one would ransom captives again.

sentences.zh: 』子路拯溺者，其人拜之以牛，子路受之。

translations.literal: Zilu rescued a drowning person—the person thanked him with an ox—Zilu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zilu pulled a man from the river and accepted the ox offered in thanks.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『魯人必拯溺矣。

translations.literal: Confucius said: Lu people will surely rescue drowning persons.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius answered that Lu men would keep hauling victims out.

sentences.zh: 』」案此語不與繇所引者相應，未詳為繇之事誤邪，而事將別有所出？〉

translations.literal: Investigating this speech—it does not correspond to what Yao cited—it is unclear whether Yao's matter was mistaken or whether the affair came out elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Pei doubts Zhong Yao’s anecdote matches the Analects.)

sentences.zh: 太祖猶欲侯之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor still wished to enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao still wanted him titled.

sentences.zh: 疇素與夏侯惇善，太祖語惇曰：「且往以情喻之，自從君所言，無告吾意也。

translations.literal: Chou was by nature friendly with Xiahou Dun; Grand Progenitor spoke to Dun: "Go for now and persuade him with feeling—follow whatever you yourself say—do not report my intent."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiahou Dun, Tian Chou’s friend, to persuade him—without revealing it was an order.

sentences.zh: 」惇就疇宿，如太祖所戒。

translations.literal: Dun went to lodge with Chou—as Grand Progenitor had admonished.
translations.idiomatic: Dun stayed overnight as instructed.

sentences.zh: 疇揣知其指，不復發言。

translations.literal: Chou guessed his intent and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou saw through the ruse and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 惇臨去，乃拊疇背曰：「田君，主意殷勤，曾不能顧乎！

translations.literal: When Dun was about to depart he then patted Chou's back saying: "Lord Tian—the lord's intent is earnest—can you really not consider it!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Dun gripped his shoulder: “The Chancellor begs you—will you not bend?”

sentences.zh: 」疇荅曰：「是何言之過也！

translations.literal: Chou replied: "How excessive are those words!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou flared: “That goes too far!

sentences.zh: 疇，負義逃竄之人耳，蒙恩全活，為幸多矣。

translations.literal: Chou is a man who betrayed duty and fled hiding—I have received grace entirely preserving my life—good fortune is already much.
translations.idiomatic: I am a fugitive whom your lord spared—I owe him my life.

sentences.zh: 豈可賣盧龍之塞，以易賞祿哉？

translations.literal: How could I sell the barrier of Lulong in exchange for rewards and stipends?"
translations.idiomatic: Shall I hawk the Lulong secret for a salary?”

sentences.zh: 縱國私疇，疇獨不愧於心乎？

translations.literal: Though the state privately favors Chou—would Chou alone not feel shame in his heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if the court forgives me, could I face myself?”

sentences.zh: 將軍雅知疇者，猶復如此，若必不得已，請願效死刎首於前。

translations.literal: You, General, know Chou well—yet still thus—if it must come to that—I beg to offer death and cut my throat before you."
translations.idiomatic: You know my heart—if you force me, I die here.”

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，涕泣橫流。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking tears streamed horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: He wept before finishing.

sentences.zh: 惇具荅太祖。

translations.literal: Dun fully reported to Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Dun reported every word.

sentences.zh: 太祖喟然知不可屈，乃拜為議郎。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor sighed, knowing he could not bend him—thereupon appointed him Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sighed and named him a ceremonial Gentleman Consultant instead.

sentences.zh: 年四十六卒。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 子又早死。

translations.literal: His son also died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son had predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，高疇德義，賜疇從孫續爵關內侯，以奉其嗣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne he esteemed Chou's virtue and righteousness and granted Chou's great-grandson Xu continuation of the noble rank as interior marquis of Guannei—to maintain his successor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen later ennobled Tian Chou’s great-grandson Xu to keep the line alive.

sentences.zh: 王脩字叔治，北海營陵人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xiu, courtesy name Shuzhi, was a man of Yingling in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu, styled Shuzhi, came from Yingling in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 年七歲喪母。

translations.literal: At age seven he lost his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was seven.

sentences.zh: 母以社日亡，來歲鄰里社，脩感念母，哀甚。

translations.literal: His mother died on the she sacrifice day; the next year when the neighborhood held the she sacrifice Xiu, moved recalling his mother, was extremely sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: She died on the spring communal festival; the next year’s revels shattered him with grief.

sentences.zh: 鄰里聞之，為之罷社。

translations.literal: When the neighborhood heard of it, for his sake they discontinued the she sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors canceled the festival out of respect.

sentences.zh: 年二十，游學南陽，止張奉舍。

translations.literal: At age twenty he traveled to study in Nanyang and lodged at Zhang Feng's house.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he studied in Nanyang as a guest of Zhang Feng.

sentences.zh: 奉舉家得疾病，無相視者，脩親隱恤之，病愈乃去。

translations.literal: Feng's whole household fell ill—there was none who looked after them—Xiu personally cared for them in secret sympathy until they recovered from illness then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhang household fell ill with no nurse, Xiu nursed them until they recovered.

sentences.zh: 初平中，北海孔融召以為主簿，守高密令。

translations.literal: In the Chuping era Kong Rong of Beihai summoned him as chief clerk and assigned him acting Magistrate of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: In the 190s Kong Rong made him chief clerk and acting magistrate of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 高密孫氏素豪俠，人客數犯法。

translations.literal: The Sun clan of Gaomi had always been heroic knights errant—guest retainers several times violated law.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful Sun clan harbored armed retainers who broke the law.

sentences.zh: 民有相劫者，賊入孫氏，吏不能執。

translations.literal: When common people robbed one another the bandits entered the Sun clan—the clerks could not seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers fled to the Sun compound and officials dared not enter.

sentences.zh: 脩將吏民圍之，孫氏拒守，吏民畏憚不敢近。

translations.literal: Xiu led clerks and people to surround them—the Sun clan resisted defense—the clerks and people feared and did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu besieged the compound but his men hung back.

sentences.zh: 脩令吏民：「敢有不攻者與同罪。

translations.literal: Xiu ordered clerks and people: "Whoever dares not attack shares the same crime."
translations.idiomatic: He threatened his troops: “Hang back and share the bandits’ guilt.

sentences.zh: 」孫氏懼，乃出賊。

translations.literal: The Sun clan feared and thereupon produced the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Suns surrendered the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 由是豪彊懾服。

translations.literal: Thereupon powerful magnates trembled and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Local bullies learned to behave.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，脩讓邴原，融不聽。

translations.literal: He was nominated Filially Pious and Incorrupt—Xiu yielded to Bing Yuan—Rong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and honest, he ceded the honor to Bing Yuan; Kong Rong refused.

sentences.zh: 〈融集有融荅脩教曰：「原之賢也，吾已知之矣。

translations.literal: The collected writings of Rong contain Rong's reply edict to Xiu saying: "Yuan's worthiness—I already know it.
translations.idiomatic: (Kong Rong’s letter: “I know Bing Yuan’s excellence.

sentences.zh: 昔高陽氏有才子八人，堯不能用，舜實舉之。

translations.literal: Formerly Gaoyangshi had eight talented sons—Yao could not employ them—Shun truly raised them up.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Paragons eluded Yao yet Shun raised them.

sentences.zh: 原可謂不患無位之士。

translations.literal: Yuan may be called a gentleman not worried about lacking position.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan is the sort who never fears obscurity.

sentences.zh: 以遺後賢，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: To leave him for later worthies—is it not acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: Save the spotlight for him later!”

sentences.zh: 」脩重辭，融荅曰：「掾清身絜己，歷試諸難，謀而鮮過，惠訓不倦。

translations.literal: Xiu heavily declined—Rong replied saying: "Clerk—you cleanse body and purify self—have undergone trials in many difficulties—planning yet seldom erring—instructing patiently without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu protested again; Kong Rong answered: “You have proved incorrupt through every trial.

sentences.zh: 余嘉乃勳，應乃懿德，用升爾于王庭，其可辭乎！」〉

translations.literal: I praise your merit and respond to your fine virtue—therefore promote you to the king's court—how can you decline!"〉
translations.idiomatic: Accept the court rank!”)

sentences.zh: 時天下亂，遂不行。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in turmoil—thereupon he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Chaos blocked his journey to the capital.

sentences.zh: 頃之，郡中有反者。

translations.literal: Presently there were rebels in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the commandery rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 脩聞融有難，夜往奔融。

translations.literal: When Xiu heard Rong was in difficulty he went by night running to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Rong was besieged, Xiu galloped through the night to help.

sentences.zh: 賊初發，融謂左右曰：「能冒難來，唯王脩耳！

translations.literal: When the bandits first arose Rong said to those at his side: "Who can brave difficulty to come—only Wang Xiu!"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong told his staff: “Only Wang Xiu would ride into this trap.

sentences.zh: 」言終而脩至。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking Xiu arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, Xiu appeared.

sentences.zh: 復署功曹。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was reinstated as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時膠東多賊寇，復令脩守膠東令。

translations.literal: At that time Jiaodong had many bandit raiders—he again ordered Xiu to defend as Magistrate of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiaodong infested by pirates, Kong Rong sent him as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 膠東人公沙盧宗彊，自為營塹，不肯應發調。

translations.literal: The man Gongsha Lu of Jiaodong—his lineage was strong—he himself built ramparts and ditches—would not respond to levies and call-ups.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsha Lu walled his clan and ignored taxes and levies.

sentences.zh: 脩獨將數騎徑入其門，斬盧兄弟，公沙氏驚愕莫敢動。

translations.literal: Xiu alone led several riders straight through his gate—beheaded Lu's brothers—the Gongsha clan was stunned and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu rode in with a handful of horsemen and executed Lu’s brothers on the spot.

sentences.zh: 脩撫慰其餘，由是寇少止。

translations.literal: Xiu soothed and comforted the rest—thereupon banditry slightly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the rest and piracy ebbed.

sentences.zh: 融每有難，脩雖休歸在家，無不至。

translations.literal: Whenever Rong had difficulty—though Xiu was resting and returned home—there was none he did not arrive for.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kong Rong faced disaster—even on leave—Xiu came.

sentences.zh: 融常賴脩以免。

translations.literal: Rong constantly relied on Xiu to escape peril.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong owed him his life more than once.

sentences.zh: 袁譚在青州，辟脩為治中從事，別駕劉獻數毀短脩。

translations.literal: When Yuan Tan was in Qing Province he summoned Xiu as administrative aide for affairs—the aide-de-camp Liu Xian several times slandered and shortened Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan hired him as administrative aide while Liu Xian maligned him.

sentences.zh: 後獻以事當死，脩理之，得免。

translations.literal: Later Xian because of an affair deserved death—Xiu arranged for him—he obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian faced execution, Xiu saved him.

sentences.zh: 時人益以此多焉。

translations.literal: People of the time increasingly on this account praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers admired the grace.

sentences.zh: 袁紹又辟脩除即墨令，後復為譚別駕。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao again summoned Xiu and appointed Magistrate of Jimo—later he again became Tan's aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: Shao named him magistrate of Jimo, then aide to Tan again.

sentences.zh: 紹死，譚、尚有隙。

translations.literal: When Shao died Tan and Shang had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao’s death the brothers feuded.

sentences.zh: 尚攻譚，譚軍敗，脩率吏民往救譚。

translations.literal: Shang attacked Tan—Tan's army was defeated—Xiu led clerks and people to go rescue Tan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang routed Tan, Xiu rallied officials and civilians to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 譚喜曰：「成吾軍者，王別駕也。

translations.literal: Tan rejoiced saying: "He who completes my army is Wang aide-de-camp."
translations.idiomatic: Tan cried: “Wang Xiu saved my army!

sentences.zh: 」譚之敗，劉詢起兵漯陰，諸城皆應。

translations.literal: When Tan was defeated Liu Xun raised troops at Luoyin—various cities all responded.
translations.idiomatic: In defeat Liu Xun rebelled at Luoyin and cities flipped.

sentences.zh: 譚歎息曰：「今舉州背叛，豈孤之不德邪！

translations.literal: Tan sighed saying: "Now the whole province betrays—is it my lack of virtue!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan groaned: “Has the whole province abandoned me?

sentences.zh: 」脩曰：「東萊太守管統雖在海表，此人不反。

translations.literal: Xiu said: "Administrator of Donglai Guan Tong though beyond the sea—this man will not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu answered: “Guan Tong beyond the sea stays loyal.

sentences.zh: 必來。

translations.literal: He is sure to come.
translations.idiomatic: He will come.

sentences.zh: 」後十餘日，統果棄其妻子來赴譚，妻子為賊所殺，譚更以統為樂安太守。

translations.literal: More than ten days later Tong indeed abandoned his wife and children to hurry to Tan—his wife and children were killed by bandits—Tan further appointed Tong Administrator of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Tong rode in—bandits slaughtered his family—Tan made him governor of Le’an.

sentences.zh: 譚復欲攻尚，脩諫曰：「兄弟還相攻擊，是敗亡之道也。

translations.literal: Tan again wished to attack Shang—Xiu remonstrated saying: "Brothers in turn attacking one another—is the way of defeat and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Tan planned another strike on Shang; Xiu warned: “Brothers who war invite ruin.

sentences.zh: 」譚不恱，然知其忠節。

translations.literal: Tan was not pleased—yet knew his loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tan scowled but recognized his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 後又問脩：「計安出？

translations.literal: Later he again asked Xiu: "What plan emerges?"
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked: “What now?

sentences.zh: 」脩曰：「夫兄弟者，左右手也。

translations.literal: Xiu said: "Brothers—they are left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said: “Brothers are two hands.

sentences.zh: 譬人將鬬而斷其右手，而曰『我必勝』，若是者可乎？

translations.literal: It is like a man about to fight who cuts off his right hand yet says 'I am sure to win'—can such be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Cutting off your right arm then boasting of victory—is that sane?”

sentences.zh: 夫棄兄弟而不親，天下其誰親之！

translations.literal: To abandon brothers and not be intimate—with whom under Heaven will you be intimate!
translations.idiomatic: Reject kin and you stand alone.

sentences.zh: 屬有讒人，固將交鬬其間，以求一朝之利，願明使君塞耳勿聽也。

translations.literal: Surely there are slanderous men—who therefore will struggle between them—seeking profit for one morning—I wish enlightened lord plug ears and do not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men stoke civil war for quick gain—plug your ears.

sentences.zh: 若斬佞臣數人，復相親睦，以禦四方，可以橫行天下。

translations.literal: If you behead several flattering ministers—again become intimate and harmonious—to resist the four quarters—you can roam horizontally under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Kill the whisperers, embrace your brother, and you can face the world.

sentences.zh: 」譚不聽，遂與尚相攻擊，請救於太祖。

translations.literal: Tan did not listen—thereupon engaged Shang in mutual attack—and requested rescue from Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Tan ignored him, fought Shang again, and begged Cao Cao for aid.

sentences.zh: 太祖旣破冀州，譚又叛。

translations.literal: After Grand Progenitor had defeated Ji Province Tan again rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao took Ji Province, Yuan Tan turned on him again.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂引軍攻譚於南皮。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor thereupon led the army to attack Tan at Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then besieged him at Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 脩時運糧在樂安，聞譚急，將所領兵及諸從事數十人往赴譚。

translations.literal: Xiu at the time was transporting grain in Le'an; hearing Tan was in crisis he led the troops under his command and several tens of staff members to hurry to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu was hauling grain in Le'an; when he heard Tan was hard pressed he rushed with his command and dozens of clerks to help.

sentences.zh: 至高密，聞譚死，下馬號哭曰：「無君焉歸？

translations.literal: Reaching Gaomi he heard Tan had died; he dismounted and wailed aloud: "Without my lord, whither shall I return?"
translations.idiomatic: At Gaomi he learned Tan was dead. He flung himself from the saddle: “My lord is gone—where can I go?”

sentences.zh: 」遂詣太祖，乞收葬譚屍。

translations.literal: He thereupon went to Grand Progenitor and begged to gather and bury Tan's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: He begged Cao Cao for Tan’s body for burial.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲觀脩意，默然不應。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor wished to observe Xiu's intent and was silent without responding.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said nothing, testing his resolve.

sentences.zh: 脩復曰：「受袁氏厚恩，若得收歛譚屍，然後就戮，無所恨。

translations.literal: Xiu again said: "I received the Yuan family's deep favor—if I can gather and enclose Tan's corpse, then accept execution afterwards—I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu said: “The Yuans showed me great kindness. Let me bury my lord, then execute me if you will—I will not complain.

sentences.zh: 」太祖嘉其義，聽之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor praised his righteousness and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao admired the loyalty and agreed.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖旣誅袁譚，梟其首，令曰：「敢哭之者戮及妻子。

translations.literal: The Fuzi states: After Grand Progenitor had executed Yuan Tan and displayed his head, an order said: "Whoever dares weep for him will have wife and children executed with him."
translations.idiomatic: (The Fuzi: Cao Cao displayed Yuan Tan’s head and threatened anyone who mourned.

sentences.zh: 」於是王叔治、田子泰相謂曰：「生受辟命，亡而不哭，非義也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Shuzhi and Tian Zitai said to one another: "In life we received appointment orders; in death not to weep—is not righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu and Tian Chou said: “We served him alive—to stay silent now would be cowardly.

sentences.zh: 畏死忘義，何以立世？

translations.literal: Fearing death and forgetting righteousness—how may one stand in the world?"
translations.idiomatic: Cowering to save our skins would disgrace us forever.”

sentences.zh: 」遂造其首而哭之，哀動三軍。

translations.literal: They thereupon went to the head and wept for it—grief moved the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: They walked to the severed head and wailed until the whole army wept.

sentences.zh: 軍正白行其戮，太祖曰：「義士也。

translations.literal: The Army Director reported to carry out the execution; Grand Progenitor said: "He is a man of principle."
translations.idiomatic: The provost moved to kill them; Cao Cao said: “These are men of honor.

sentences.zh: 」赦之。

translations.literal: He pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He spared them.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案《田疇傳》，疇為袁尚所辟，不被譚命。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates the Biography of Tian Chou: Chou was summoned by Yuan Shang—he did not receive orders from Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: Tian Chou served Yuan Shang, not Tan—so the story is muddled.

sentences.zh: 傅子合而言之，有違事實。〉

translations.literal: The Fuzi combined and spoke of it—there is violation of the facts.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Fuzi conflated two different men.)

sentences.zh: 以脩為督軍糧，還樂安。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiu to supervise military grain and returned to Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao put him in charge of army grain and sent him back to Le’an.

sentences.zh: 譚之破，諸城皆服，唯管統以樂安不從命。

translations.literal: When Tan was defeated the various cities all submitted—only Guan Tong in Le'an would not follow orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan fell every city yielded except Guan Tong in Le’an.

sentences.zh: 太祖命脩取統首，脩以統亡國之忠臣，因解其縛，使詣太祖。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor ordered Xiu to take Tong's head; Xiu, holding that Tong was a loyal minister of a vanquished state, thereupon loosed his bonds and had him go to Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wanted Guan Tong’s head; Wang Xiu cut his ropes and sent him in as a loyalist worth sparing.

sentences.zh: 太祖恱而赦之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor was pleased and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao welcomed the gesture and pardoned Guan Tong.

sentences.zh: 袁氏政寬，在職勢者多畜聚。

translations.literal: Yuan family governance was lenient—those holding office and position mostly hoarded wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuans ruled loosely, so officials grew rich.

sentences.zh: 太祖破鄴，籍沒審配等家財物貲以萬數。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor broke Ye he registered and confiscated the property of Shen Pei and others—goods counted in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao’s inventory of Ye seized Shen Pei’s hoards by the ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 及破南皮，閱脩家，穀不滿十斛，有書數百卷。

translations.literal: When he broke Nanpi and inspected Xiu's home—grain did not fill ten hu—there were several hundred rolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanpi Wang Xiu’s store held under ten hu of grain and a few hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎曰：「士不妄有名。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor sighed: "Scholars do not vainly have reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said: “The great name was earned.

sentences.zh: 」乃禮辟為司空掾，行司金中郎將，遷魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He thereupon with formal ceremony summoned him as aide to the Minister of Works, acting General of the Central Office of Metal, promoted to Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He hired him for the minister’s staff, made him director of the mint, then governor of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 為治，抑彊扶弱，明賞罰，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: In governing he repressed the strong and aided the weak—clarified rewards and punishments—the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed magnates, shielded the weak, and kept clear laws—people praised him.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：脩為司金中郎將，陳黃白異議，因奏記曰：「脩聞枳棘之林，無梁柱之質；

translations.literal: The Wei lue states: Xiu as General of the Central Office of Metal differed on yellow and white metal—thereupon he submitted a memorial saying: "Xiu has heard that in forests of thorn-apple there is no quality of pillar or roof-beam;
translations.idiomatic: (Wei lue: as mint director Wang Xiu wrote: “Thorn thickets yield no timbers;

sentences.zh: 涓流之水，無洪波之勢。

translations.literal: in water of trickling streams there is no force of great waves."
translations.idiomatic: trickles never swell to a flood.”

sentences.zh: 是以在職七年，忠讜不昭於時，功業不見於事，欣於所受，俯慙不報，未嘗不長夜起坐，中飯釋餐。

translations.literal: Therefore in office seven years loyal remonstrance has not shone in the time—merit and enterprise are not seen in affairs—rejoicing in what I have received, bowing in shame that I cannot repay—never not sitting up through the long night, at midday meal setting aside the bowl.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in a minor post left his advice ignored—he could not sleep for shame at failing the trust.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 力少任重，不堪而懼也。

translations.literal: Strength is scant and burden heavy—unable to bear and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The load overwhelmed him.

sentences.zh: 謹貢所議如左。

translations.literal: Respectfully I present the discussed matter as at left.
translations.idiomatic: He attached his policy memo.

sentences.zh: 」太祖甚然之，乃與脩書曰：「君澡身浴德，流聲本州，忠能成績，為世美談，名實相副，過人甚遠。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor greatly agreed and therefore wrote to Xiu saying: "You bathe body and bathe virtue—reputation flows through your native commandery—loyalty able to complete achievements—a fine tale for the age—name and substance matching—surpassing others very far.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied at length: “Your virtue fills your home commandery—loyalty and deeds match your fame.

sentences.zh: 孤以心知君，至深至孰，非徒耳目而已也。

translations.literal: I, solitary one, know you in heart—deepest and most familiar—not merely ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: I trust you with more than hearsay.

sentences.zh: 察觀先賢之論，多以鹽鐵之利，足贍軍國之用。

translations.literal: Examining former worthies' discussions—mostly consider salt and iron profits sufficient to supply army and state needs.
translations.idiomatic: History shows salt and iron fill military coffers.

sentences.zh: 昔孤初立司金之官，念非屈君，餘無可者。

translations.literal: Formerly when I first established the office of Director of Metal—I thought if not bending you—there was no other suitable person.
translations.idiomatic: When I created the mint I chose you because no one else would do.

sentences.zh: 故與君教曰：『昔遏父陶正，民賴其器用，及子媯滿，建侯于陳；

translations.literal: Therefore I instructed you saying: 'Formerly Efu was pottery supervisor—the people relied on his vessels—and his descendant Gui Man established a marquisate in Chen;
translations.idiomatic: I reminded you of Efu’s pottery line that founded Chen—and

sentences.zh: 近桑弘羊，位至三公。

translations.literal: near at hand Sang Hongyang rose to the Three Dukes."
translations.idiomatic: Sang Hongyang rose to the Three Dukes.”

sentences.zh: 此君元龜之兆先告者也』，是孤用君之本言也，或恐衆人未曉此意。

translations.literal: This is the tortoise shell omen your lord first announced—the root of my employing you—or perhaps I fear the multitude does not understand this intent.
translations.idiomatic: That was your mandate—some may not grasp why you stayed at the mint.

sentences.zh: 自是以來，在朝之士，每得一顯選，常舉君為首，及聞袁軍師衆賢之議，以為不宜越君。

translations.literal: Since this time—among officers at court—whenever there was a distinguished selection—they constantly nominated you first—and when hearing Yuan army adviser and various worthies' deliberation—they held one should not leapfrog you.
translations.idiomatic: Every promotion list put you first—Yuan Huan’s circle agreed you deserved senior posts.

sentences.zh: 然孤執心將有所厎，以軍師之職，閑於司金，至於建功，重於軍師。

translations.literal: Yet I hold my intent will reach somewhere—with army adviser duty leisurely compared to Director of Metal—as for establishing merit—weightier than army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao explained he meant the mint as rehearsal for higher command.

sentences.zh: 孤之精誠，足以達君；

translations.literal: My utmost sincerity is sufficient to reach you;
translations.idiomatic: His sincerity, he said, should reassure Wang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 君之察孤，足以不疑。

translations.literal: your observing me is sufficient to lack doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu should not doubt Cao Cao’s esteem.

sentences.zh: 但恐傍人淺見，以蠡測海，為蛇畫足，將言前後百選，輙不用之，而使此君沈滯冶官。

translations.literal: Only I fear shallow men at the side—measuring the sea with a shell—adding feet to a snake—will say that in a hundred earlier selections you were always unused—and made this lord sink in smelting official posts.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip might paint the mint as exile rather than preparation.

sentences.zh: 張甲李乙，尚猶先之，此主人意待之不優之效也。

translations.literal: Zhang A and Li B—still are advanced before him—this is the effect of the lord's intent not treating him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser men promoted ahead would prove poor patronage.

sentences.zh: 孤懼有此空聲冒實，淫鼃亂耳。

translations.literal: I fear there is this empty reputation assuming substance—croaking frogs confusing the ear.
translations.idiomatic: He dreaded frog croaks of rumor.

sentences.zh: 假有斯事，亦庶鍾期不失聽也；

translations.literal: Suppose there is such a matter—yet perhaps Zhong Qi does not lose listening;
translations.idiomatic: If rumor flies, may wise listeners still discern truth;

sentences.zh: 若其無也，過備何害？

translations.literal: if there is none—what harm in full precaution?"
translations.idiomatic: if not, over-explaining hurts nothing.”

sentences.zh: 昔宣帝察少府蕭望之才任宰相，故復出之，令為馮翊。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Xuan observed Shaofu Xiao Wangzhi's talent fit for chancellor—therefore sent him out again—ordering him Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Like Xuandi testing Xiao Wangzhi by sending him to Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 從正卿往，似於左遷。

translations.literal: Going from chief minister seemed like demotion to the left.
translations.idiomatic: It looked like a lateral move from chief minister.

sentences.zh: 上使侍中宣意曰：『君守平原日淺，故復試君三輔，非有所閒也。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered an attendant-in-chief to convey intent saying: 'Your guarding Pingyuan days were shallow—therefore again testing you in the Three Adjuncts—not because there was estrangement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor explained it was a test, not disfavor.

sentences.zh: 』孤揆先主中宗之意，誠備此事。

translations.literal: I, solitary one, gauge the intent of Former Lord Zhongzong—truly prepare this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao compared his intent to Zhongzong’s.

sentences.zh: 旣君崇勳業以副孤意。

translations.literal: Since you have honored merit and enterprise to match my intent.
translations.idiomatic: You have proved worthy of my hopes.

sentences.zh: 公叔文子與臣俱升，獨何人哉！

translations.literal: Gongsun Wenzi ascended with his minister together—what sort of man alone is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Like Gongsun Wenzi sharing rank with his servant—such honors await.”

sentences.zh: 」後無幾而遷魏郡太守。〉

translations.literal: Not long after he was promoted Administrator of Wei commandery.〉
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Wang Xiu became governor of Wei.)

sentences.zh: 魏國旣建，為大司農郎中令。

translations.literal: When Wei was established he became Prefect of the Gentlemen of the Palace under the Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Wei he served as palace prefect under the minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 太祖議行肉刑，脩以為時未可行，太祖採其議。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor debated implementing corporal punishment—Xiu held the times were not yet ready to implement—Grand Progenitor adopted his deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao debated mutilation laws; Wang Xiu said the times were wrong—Cao Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 徙為奉常。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 其後嚴才反，與其徒屬數十人攻掖門。

translations.literal: Afterward Yan Cai rebelled—with his followers several tens of persons—attacking the side gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Cai raided the palace side gate with dozens of men,

sentences.zh: 脩聞變，召車馬未至，便將官屬步至宮門。

translations.literal: When Xiu heard the alarm—carriages and horses had not yet arrived—he led subordinate officials on foot to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu ran to the gate on foot before his carriage arrived.

sentences.zh: 太祖在銅爵臺望見之，曰：「彼來者必王叔治也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor on the Bronze Bird Terrace saw him and said: "That one coming must be Wang Shuzhi."
translations.idiomatic: From the Bronze Bird Terrace Cao Cao said: “That must be Wang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 」相國鍾繇謂脩：「舊，京城有變，九卿各居其府。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhong Yao said to Xiu: "By old custom—when the capital had alarm—the Nine Ministers each remained at his office."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao protested: “Ministers used to stay at their yamens.

sentences.zh: 」脩曰：「食其祿，焉避其離？

translations.literal: Xiu said: "Eating its salary—how avoid its peril?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu answered: “Their pay buys their peril.

sentences.zh: 居府雖舊，非赴難之義。

translations.literal: Remaining at office though old custom—is not the righteousness of rushing to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Hiding in offices is not how loyal ministers behave.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，病卒官。

translations.literal: Presently he fell ill and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in harness.

sentences.zh: 子忠，官至東萊太守、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Zhong rose to office as Administrator of Donglai and Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Zhong became governor of Donglai and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，脩識高柔於弱冠，異王基於幼童，終皆遠至，世稱其知人。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiu recognized Gao Rou at the capping age and marked Wang Ji as a child—in the end both reached distant station—the age praised his knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: He had spotted Gao Rou young and Wang Ji as a boy—both rose high; contemporaries praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 〈王隱《晉書》曰：脩一子，名儀，字朱表，高亮雅直。

translations.literal: Wang Yin's Jin Shu states: Xiu had one son—named Yi—courtesy name Zhubiao—lofty, bright, refined, upright.
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Yin’s Jin shu names his son Wang Yi, styled Zhu biao—grave and upright.

sentences.zh: 司馬文王為安東，儀為司馬。

translations.literal: Sima Wenwang was General Pacifying the East—Yi was his marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao commanded the east, Wang Yi served as his marshal.

sentences.zh: 東關之敗，文王曰：「近日之事，誰任其咎？

translations.literal: At the defeat at Dongguan Wenwang said: "In recent matters—who bears the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: After the Dongguan defeat Sima Zhao asked who was at fault.

sentences.zh: 」儀曰：「責在軍師。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Blame lies with the army adviser."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi said: “The chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 」文王怒曰：「司馬欲委罪於孤邪？

translations.literal: Wenwang angrily said: "Marshal wishes to shift blame onto me, solitary one?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao snarled: “You blame me?”

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wang Yi executed.

sentences.zh: 子襃，字偉元。

translations.literal: His son Bao—courtesy name Weiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Bao, styled Weiyuan,

sentences.zh: 少立操尚，非禮不動。

translations.literal: In youth he established conduct and ideals—without ritual propriety he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: formed stern principles in youth—never stepped outside ritual.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺四寸，容貌絕異。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi four cun in height—appearance surpassingly unusual.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi four—striking in appearance.

sentences.zh: 痛父不以命終，絕世不仕。

translations.literal: Grieving that his father did not end life by natural decree—he cut off from the world and would not serve office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father died by violence he refused office for life.

sentences.zh: 立屋墓側，以教授為務。

translations.literal: He built a dwelling beside the tomb—taking instruction as his task.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by his father’s grave and taught for a living.

sentences.zh: 旦夕常至墓前拜，輙悲號斷絕。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he regularly came before the tomb to bow—always sorrowfully wailing till breath broke.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and night he keened at the grave until he could not breathe.

sentences.zh: 墓前有一柏樹，襃常所攀援，涕泣所著，樹色與凡樹不同。

translations.literal: Before the tomb was one cypress tree—Bao constantly climbed it—the tears he shed stained it—the tree's color differed from ordinary trees.
translations.idiomatic: His tears stained the graveyard cypress until its bark darkened.

sentences.zh: 讀詩至「哀哀父母，生我勞悴」，未曾不反覆流涕，泣下沾衿。

translations.literal: Reading the Odes to "Alas for father and mother—they bore me in toil and weariness"—never not repeatedly weeping—tears falling soaking the lapel.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read “Alas, my parents” he wept until his collar dripped.

sentences.zh: 家貧躬耕，計口而田，度身而蠶。

translations.literal: His household was poor—he personally plowed—measuring fields by mouths—measuring silkworms by bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he farmed by mouth and raised silkworms within his means.

sentences.zh: 諸生有密為襃刈麥者，襃遂棄之；

translations.literal: Students secretly harvested wheat for Bao—Bao thereupon abandoned it;
translations.idiomatic: When pupils secretly harvested grain for him he threw the crop away;

sentences.zh: 自是莫敢復佐刈者。

translations.literal: from this none dared again assist in harvesting.
translations.idiomatic: after that no one tried.

sentences.zh: 襃門人為本縣所役，求襃為屬，襃曰：「卿學不足以庇身，吾德薄不足以蔭卿，屬之何益？

translations.literal: Bao's disciple was conscripted by his native county—seeking Bao to write for him—Bao said: "Your learning is insufficient to shelter your person—my virtue is thin—insufficient to shade you—what benefit in writing?"
translations.idiomatic: A pupil asked him to write off corvée; Wang Bao refused: “Your scholarship cannot shield you—my virtue cannot shelter you.

sentences.zh: 且吾不捉筆已四十年。

translations.literal: Moreover I have not grasped the brush for forty years."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I have not picked up a brush in forty years.

sentences.zh: 」乃步擔乾飯，兒負鹽豉，門徒從者千餘人。

translations.literal: He thereupon carried dry rice on a shoulder pole—his son bore salted beans—disciples following numbered over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He shouldered dry rations, his son carried pickled beans, and a thousand students followed him south.

sentences.zh: 安丘令以為見己，整衣出迎之於門。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Anqiu thought he was coming to see himself—straightened robes and went out to welcome him at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Anqiu magistrate thought Wang Bao came to visit him and waited at the gate in full dress.

sentences.zh: 襃乃下道至土牛，磬折而立。

translations.literal: Bao thereupon stepped off the road to the earth ox—bowed deeply and stood.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao stopped at the milestone, bowed low, and stood aside.

sentences.zh: 云：「門生為縣所役，故來送別。

translations.literal: He said: "My disciple is being conscripted by the county—therefore I come to see him off."
translations.idiomatic: He said only: “I escort a drafted pupil.

sentences.zh: 」執手涕泣而去。

translations.literal: Clasping hands weeping he departed.
translations.idiomatic: He clasped the boy’s hand, wept, and left.

sentences.zh: 令即放遣諸生，一縣以為恥。

translations.literal: The magistrate immediately released the various students—the whole county took it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate freed every student—the county squirmed with shame.

sentences.zh: 同縣管彥，少有才力，未知名，襃獨以為當自達，常友愛之；

translations.literal: Guan Yan of the same county—in youth had talent and strength—not yet renowned—Bao alone thought he would rise of himself—constantly befriended and loved him;
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Guan Yan before anyone noticed him;

sentences.zh: 男女各始生，共許為婚。

translations.literal: when male and female children were first born they mutually pledged them in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: they betrothed their infants.

sentences.zh: 彥果為西夷校尉。

translations.literal: Yan indeed became Colonel of the Western Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yan became colonel of the western Yi.

sentences.zh: 襃後更以女嫁人，彥弟馥問襃，襃曰：「吾薄志畢願，山藪自處，姊妹皆遠，吉凶斷絕，以此自誓。

translations.literal: Bao afterward changed by marrying his daughter to another—Yan's younger brother Fu asked Bao—Bao said: "My meager intent having fulfilled its wish—in mountains and marshes I dwell myself—sisters all distant—good and ill fortune cut off—by this I swore myself.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Bao married the girl elsewhere. Guan Fu demanded why; Wang Bao said he had sworn to live as a recluse with kin far away.

sentences.zh: 賢兄子葬父於帝都，此則洛陽之人也，豈吾欲婚之本指邪？

translations.literal: Your worthy elder brother's son buried his father in the imperial capital—thereby he is a Luoyang person—how could this be my original intent for contracting marriage?"
translations.idiomatic: Your nephew buried his father in Luoyang—he is a Luoyang man now—not the rustic ally I pledged.

sentences.zh: 」馥曰：「嫂，齊人也。

translations.literal: Fu said: "My sister-in-law is a person of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu said: “But his wife is from Qi.

sentences.zh: 當還臨菑。

translations.literal: She ought to return to Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: She should return to Linzi.

sentences.zh: 」襃曰：「安有葬父河南，隨妻還齊！

translations.literal: Bao said: "How can there be burying father south of the Yellow River yet following wife back to Qi!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao shot back: “Who buries his father in Henan yet trails a wife to Qi?”

sentences.zh: 用意如此，何婚之有？

translations.literal: With intent thus—what marriage could there be?
translations.idiomatic: Given that stance, what wedding vow could stand?

sentences.zh: 」遂不婚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not marry.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the betrothal.

sentences.zh: 邴春者，根矩之後也。

translations.literal: Bing Chun was a descendant of Genju.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Chun traced his line to Bing Yuan.

sentences.zh: 少立志操，寒苦自居，負笈遊學，身不停家，鄉邑翕然，以為能係其先也。

translations.literal: In youth he established resolve and conduct—dwelling in cold hardship himself—carrying book-box on back traveling to study—body never stopping at home—the village harmoniously thought him able to tie to his ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Young Bing Chun apprenticed himself to hardship, studied away from home, and locals thought him worthy of his forebears.

sentences.zh: 襃以為春性險狹，慕名意多，終必不成，及後春果無學業，流離遠外，有識以此歸之。

translations.literal: Bao thought Chun's nature narrow and perilous—thought of reputation much—in the end surely could not complete—and afterward Chun indeed had no scholarly achievement—wandered far abroad—those with understanding on this account submitted to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao called him vain and shallow—Chun later proved a wanderer without learning, vindicating Bao’s judgment.

sentences.zh: 襃常以為人所行，其當歸於善道，不可以己所能而責人所不能也。

translations.literal: Bao constantly held that what people practice ought to return to the good path—one cannot with what oneself can do blame others for what they cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao taught that conduct must aim at virtue—never judge others by your own gifts.

sentences.zh: 有致遺者，皆不受。

translations.literal: When there were those who sent gifts—he all did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 及洛都傾覆，寇賊蠭起，襃宗親悉欲移江東，襃戀墳壠。

translations.literal: When the Luoyang capital overturned—bandits rose like bees—Bao's whole lineage all wished to move east of the Yangzi—Bao clung to grave mounds.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell and rebels swarmed, kin fled south but Wang Bao stayed by his father’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 賊大盛，乃南達泰山郡。

translations.literal: When bandits grew greatly strong—thereupon reached south to Taishan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders grew until they overran Taishan.

sentences.zh: 襃思土不肯去，賊害之。

translations.literal: Bao longed for native soil and would not leave—the bandits murdered him.
translations.idiomatic: He would not abandon home soil and the bandits killed him.

sentences.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：襃與濟南劉兆字延世，俱以不仕顯名。

translations.literal: The Han Jin chunqiu states: Bao and Liu Zhao of Jinan—courtesy name Yanshi—both by not serving became illustriously renowned.
translations.idiomatic: (Han Jin chunqiu pairs Wang Bao with Liu Zhao of Jinan—both famed refusers of office.

sentences.zh: 襃以父為文王所濫殺，終身不應徵聘，未甞西向坐，以示不臣於晉也。〉

translations.literal: Bao because his father was wantonly executed by Wenwang—to the end never answered summons or appointments—never sat facing west—to show he did not submit as subject to Jin.〉
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao blamed Sima Zhao for his father’s death—never served the Jin and avoided facing west—the emperor’s direction.)

sentences.zh: 邴原字根矩，北海朱虛人也。

translations.literal: Bing Yuan, courtesy name Genju, was a man of Zhuxu in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan, styled Genju, came from Zhuxu in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 少與管寧俱以操尚稱，州府辟命皆不就。

translations.literal: In youth together with Guan Ning he was famed for conduct and ideals—summons from province and prefecture he all did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Like Guan Ning he was famed for integrity and ignored every summons.

sentences.zh: 黃巾起，原將家屬入海，住鬱洲山中。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans arose Yuan led family dependents into the sea—dwelling in the mountains of Yu Isle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans rose he fled with kin to Yu Isle.

sentences.zh: 時孔融為北海相，舉原有道。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Rong was Chancellor of Beihai—he nominated Yuan as a man of moral attainment.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong, ruling Beihai, nominated him as a candidate for moral excellence.

sentences.zh: 原以黃巾方盛，遂至遼東，與同郡劉政俱有勇略雄氣。

translations.literal: Yuan because the Yellow Turbans were then flourishing—thereupon went to Liaodong—together with fellow commandery Liu Zheng both had courage, stratagem, and heroic spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Because rebels still raged he sailed to Liaodong where he and Liu Zheng of his commandery shared fame for daring.

sentences.zh: 遼東太守公孫度畏惡欲殺之，盡收捕其家，政得脫。

translations.literal: Administrator of Liaodong Gongsun Du feared and hated him and wished to kill him—wholly seized and arrested his household—Zheng escaped capture.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du meant to kill Liu Zheng—seized his family—but Liu escaped.

sentences.zh: 度告諸縣：「敢有藏政者與同罪。

translations.literal: Du announced to the counties: "Whoever dares harbor Zheng shares the same crime."
translations.idiomatic: Du ordered counties to execute anyone hiding Liu.

sentences.zh: 」政窘急，往投原，

translations.literal: Zheng cornered and desperate—went to seek Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Liu fled to Bing Yuan.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：政投原曰：「窮鳥入懷。

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu states: Zheng fled to Yuan saying: "A cornered bird flies into the bosom."
translations.idiomatic: (Wei shi chunqiu: Liu said: “A hunted bird dives into your cloak.

sentences.zh: 」原曰：「安知此懷之可入邪？」〉

translations.literal: Yuan said: "How know whether this bosom may be entered?"〉
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan answered: “How do you know this chest is safe?”)

sentences.zh: 原匿之月餘，時東萊太史慈當歸，原因以政付之。

translations.literal: Yuan hid him over a month—at that time Taishi Ci of Donglai was about to return south—Yuan therefore entrusted Zheng to him.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan hid him a month, then passed him to Taishi Ci sailing south.

sentences.zh: 旣而謂度曰：「將軍前日欲殺劉政，以其為己害。

translations.literal: Presently he said to Du: "General—the other day you wished to kill Liu Zheng—because he was harm to yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Then he told Du: “You wanted Liu dead because he threatened you.

sentences.zh: 今政已去，君之害豈不除哉！

translations.literal: Now Zheng has gone—is not your harm already removed!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Liu is gone—the threat is gone.

sentences.zh: 」度曰：「然。

translations.literal: Du said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Du agreed.

sentences.zh: 」原曰：「君之畏政者，以其有智也。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "What you feared in Zheng was that he had wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan continued: “You feared his wit.

sentences.zh: 今政已免，智將用矣，尚奚拘政之家？

translations.literal: Now Zheng has escaped—his wisdom will be employed—why still detain Zheng's household?"
translations.idiomatic: He is free—why jail his kin?

sentences.zh: 不若赦之，無重怨。

translations.literal: Better to pardon them—do not multiply resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Release them before hatred deepens.

sentences.zh: 」度乃出之。

translations.literal: Du thereupon released them.
translations.idiomatic: Du freed Liu’s family.

sentences.zh: 原又資送政家，皆得歸故郡。

translations.literal: Yuan again supplied funds to escort Zheng's household—all were able to return to native commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan paid their passage home.

sentences.zh: 原在遼東，一年中往歸原居者數百家，游學之士，教授之聲，不絕。

translations.literal: While Yuan was in Liaodong—within one year those who came to attach themselves to Yuan's residence numbered several hundred households—students traveling to study—the sound of instruction—unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In Liaodong hundreds of families settled under him; his school never quieted.

sentences.zh: 後得歸，太祖辟為司空掾。

translations.literal: Later able to return—Grand Progenitor summoned him as aide to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Han lands Cao Cao hired him for the minister’s staff.

sentences.zh: 原女早亡，時太祖愛子倉舒亦沒，太祖欲求合葬，原辭曰：「合葬，非禮也。

translations.literal: Yuan's daughter died early—at that time Grand Progenitor's beloved son Cangshu also perished—Grand Progenitor wished joint burial—Yuan declined saying: "Joint burial—is not according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao’s son Cao Chong died, he asked to bury him with Bing Yuan’s daughter; Bing Yuan refused: “Joint burial breaches ritual.

sentences.zh: 原之所以自容於明公，公之所以待原者，以能守訓典而不易也。

translations.literal: The reason Yuan thereby holds himself tolerable to enlightened lord—the reason lord thereby treats Yuan—is because able to guard canonical instruction without altering it.
translations.idiomatic: You employ me because I uphold the classics—do not ask me to break them.

sentences.zh: 若聽明公之命，則是凡庸也，明公焉以為哉？

translations.literal: If I obey enlightened lord's order—then I am ordinary and mediocre—how should enlightened lord deem this acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: If I obey, I am just another timeserver.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃止，徙署丞相徵事。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor thereupon desisted—transferred appointment to Chancellor's Investigator.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dropped the idea and named him chancellor’s investigator.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：建安十五年，初置徵事二人，原與平原王烈俱以選補。〉

translations.literal: The Daily Notes of Emperor Xian state: In the fifteenth year of Jian'an—first established two Investigators—Yuan together with Wang Lie of Pingyuan were both selected to fill the posts.〉
translations.idiomatic: (Xian di qiju zhu: in 210 CE two investigator posts were created—Bing Yuan and Wang Lie filled them.)

sentences.zh: 崔琰為東曹掾，記讓曰：「徵事邴原、議郎張範，皆秉德純懿，志行忠方，清靜足以厲俗，貞固足以幹事，所謂龍翰鳳翼，國之重寶。

translations.literal: Cui Yan as aide of the Eastern Bureau submitted deferentially: "Investigator Bing Yuan and Gentleman Consultant Zhang Fan—both hold virtue pure and fine—intent and conduct loyal and upright—quiet purity sufficient to reform custom—chaste firmness sufficient to manage affairs—what is called dragon pinion phoenix wing—the state's heavy treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan memorialized: “Bing Yuan and Zhang Fan are dragon wings for the state.

sentences.zh: 舉而用之，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Raise and employ them—the unkind depart far.
translations.idiomatic: Promote them and petty men flee.

sentences.zh: 」代涼茂為五官將長史，閉門自守，非公事不出。

translations.literal: He succeeded Liang Mao as chief clerk of the General of the Five Offices—closing gate and guarding himself—not emerging except on public business.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Liang Mao as the heir’s chief clerk and rarely left his house.

sentences.zh: 太祖征吳，原從行，卒。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor campaigned against Wu—Yuan accompanied the march—and died.
translations.idiomatic: He died on Cao Cao’s Wu campaign.

sentences.zh: 〈《原別傳》曰：原十一而喪父，家貧，早孤。

translations.literal: The Separate Biography of Yuan states: Yuan at eleven lost his father—household poor—early orphaned.
translations.idiomatic: (Yuan bie zhuan: orphaned at eleven in poverty.

sentences.zh: 鄰有書舍，原過其傍而泣。

translations.literal: Next door was a schoolhouse—Yuan passed beside it and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept outside a neighbor’s school.

sentences.zh: 師問曰：「童子何悲？

translations.literal: The teacher asked: "Boy—why grieve?"
translations.idiomatic: The teacher asked why he cried.

sentences.zh: 」原曰：「孤者易傷，貧者易感。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Orphans are easily wounded—the poor are easily moved."
translations.idiomatic: He said: “Orphans bruise easily—the poor feel everything.

sentences.zh: 夫書者，必皆具有父兄者，一則羨其不孤，二則羨其得學，心中惻然而為涕零也。

translations.literal: As for scholars—they surely all have fathers and elder brothers—first I envy them as not orphaned—second I envy them obtaining study—in my heart sad and therefore shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars have fathers who pay tuition—I envy them twice over.

sentences.zh: 」師亦哀原之言而為之泣曰：「欲書可耳！

translations.literal: The teacher also pitied Yuan's words and wept for him saying: "If you wish to study—you may!"
translations.idiomatic: The teacher wept and said: “Study if you wish!

sentences.zh: 」荅曰：「無錢資。

translations.literal: He replied: "I lack funds."
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan said he had no fees.

sentences.zh: 」師曰：「童子苟有志，我徒相教，不求資也。

translations.literal: The teacher said: "Boy—if you indeed have intent—I as teacher instruct you—not seeking funds."
translations.idiomatic: The teacher taught him for free.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂就書。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to study.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled.

sentences.zh: 一冬之間，誦孝經、論語。

translations.literal: Within one winter he recited from memory the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects.
translations.idiomatic: One winter later he knew the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects by heart.

sentences.zh: 自在童齓之中，嶷然有異。

translations.literal: While still in childhood teeth—he stood out as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he seemed extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 及長，金玉其行。

translations.literal: When grown—his conduct was gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: As a man his conduct was flawless.

sentences.zh: 欲遠游學，詣安丘孫崧。

translations.literal: Wishing to travel far to study—he went to Sun Song of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He sought Sun Song of Anqiu before roaming.

sentences.zh: 崧辭曰：「君鄉里鄭君，君知之乎？

translations.literal: Song declined saying: "Your village worthy Master Zheng—do you know him?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Song asked whether he knew Master Zheng nearby.

sentences.zh: 」原荅曰：「然。

translations.literal: Yuan replied: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan said yes.

sentences.zh: 」崧曰：「鄭君學覽古今，博聞彊識，鉤深致遠，誠學者之師模也。

translations.literal: Song said: "Master Zheng's learning surveys ancient and modern—broad hearing strong memory—hooking deep reaching far—truly a model teacher for scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Song praised Zheng Xuan’s learning.

sentences.zh: 君乃舍之，躡屣千里，所謂以鄭為東家丘者也。

translations.literal: Yet you abandon him—treading slippers a thousand li—what is called taking Zheng as the mound east of one's house."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you skip him—that is ignoring Confucius’s eastern mound.

sentences.zh: 君似不知而曰然者，何？

translations.literal: You seem not to know yet say yes—why?"
translations.idiomatic: You nod though you barely know him—why?

sentences.zh: 」原曰：「先生之說，誠可謂苦藥良鍼矣；

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Sir's discourse—truly may be called bitter medicine and fine needles;
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan answered: “Your lecture is bitter medicine;

sentences.zh: 然猶未達僕之微趣也。

translations.literal: yet still has not penetrated my servant's subtle inclination.
translations.idiomatic: but you miss my purpose.

sentences.zh: 人各有志，所規不同，故乃有登山而採玉者，有入海而採珠者，豈可謂登山者不知海之深，入海者不知山之高哉！

translations.literal: People each have intent—what they plan differs—therefore there are those who climb mountains to gather jade—those who enter the sea to gather pearls—how can one say those climbing mountains do not know the sea's depth—those entering the sea do not know the mountain's height!"
translations.idiomatic: Some quarry jade on peaks, others pearls in the sea—each trade need not mock the other.

sentences.zh: 君謂僕以鄭為東家丘，君以僕為西家愚夫邪？

translations.literal: You deem my servant takes Zheng as mound east of house—you deem my servant west-house foolish husband?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you think me blind to Master Zheng?

sentences.zh: 」崧辭謝焉。

translations.literal: Song apologized with words.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Song apologized.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「兖、豫之士，吾多所識，未有若君者；

translations.literal: He also said: "Among gentlemen of Yanzhou and Yuzhou—I know many—there has been none like you;
translations.idiomatic: He added: “I know many scholars in Yan and Yu—none like you;

sentences.zh: 當以書相分。

translations.literal: I ought to write letters of introduction for you."
translations.idiomatic: I should give you letters of introduction.

sentences.zh: 」原重其意，難辭之，持書而別。

translations.literal: Yuan weighed his intent—found it hard to decline—held the letter and parted.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan took the letters to be polite.

sentences.zh: 原心以為求師啟學，志高者通，非若交游待分而成也。

translations.literal: Yuan in heart thought that seeking teachers and opening learning—those of lofty intent penetrate—not like social visiting relying on introductions to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: True learning depends on intent, not introductions.

sentences.zh: 書何為哉？

translations.literal: What use letters?
translations.idiomatic: Why cart letters?

sentences.zh: 乃藏書於家而行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stored the book at home and went.
translations.idiomatic: He left them in a drawer and set out.

sentences.zh: 原舊能飲酒，自行之後，八九年間，酒不向口。

translations.literal: Yuan formerly could drink wine—since traveling—within eight or nine years—wine did not approach mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Though once fond of wine he touched none for nine years on the road.

sentences.zh: 單步負笈，苦身持力，至陳留則師韓子助，潁川則宗陳仲弓，汝南則交范孟博，涿郡則親盧子幹。

translations.literal: Walking alone carrying book-box—bittering body maintaining strength—reaching Chenliu then studied under Han Zizhu—in Yingchuan then took Chen Zhonggong as teacher—in Runan then befriended Fan Mengbo—in Zhuo commandery then drew close to Lu Zigàn.
translations.idiomatic: He walked to Chenliu to study with Han Zizhu, Yingchuan with Chen Zhonggong, Runan with Fan Mengbo, Zhuo with Lu Zigàn.

sentences.zh: 臨別，師友以原不飲酒，會米肉送原。

translations.literal: At parting—teachers and friends because Yuan did not drink wine—gathered rice and meat to send Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Friends offered a farewell feast though he abstained from wine.

sentences.zh: 原曰：「本能飲酒，但以荒思廢業，故斷之耳。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Originally able to drink wine—but because idle thoughts waste enterprise—therefore cut it off."
translations.idiomatic: He said he quit drink to save his studies.

sentences.zh: 今當遠別，因見貺餞，可一飲燕。

translations.literal: Now about to part far—because seeing gifts for farewell—may once drink and feast.
translations.idiomatic: Farwell allowed one toast.

sentences.zh: 」於是共坐飲酒，終日不醉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sat together drinking wine—all day not drunk.
translations.idiomatic: They drank all day; Bing Yuan never stumbled.

sentences.zh: 歸以書還孫崧，解不致書之意。

translations.literal: Returning he gave the letter back to Sun Song—explaining the intent of not delivering the letter.
translations.idiomatic: He returned Sun Song’s letters unused.

sentences.zh: 後為郡所召，署功曹主簿。

translations.literal: Later summoned by the commandery—appointed Chief Clerk registrar.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery later made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時魯國孔融在郡，教選計當任公卿之才，乃以鄭玄為計掾，彭璆為計吏，原為計佐。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Rong of Lu state was in the commandery—ordering selection for accounting ought to employ worthy of ministerial talent—thereupon appointed Zheng Xuan as accounting aide—Peng Qiu as accounting clerk—Yuan as accounting assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong stacked his revenue office with Zheng Xuan, Peng Qiu, and Bing Yuan.

sentences.zh: 融有所愛一人，常盛嗟嘆之。

translations.literal: Rong had one person he loved—constantly greatly sighing and praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong doted on a favorite.

sentences.zh: 後恚望，欲殺之，朝吏皆請。

translations.literal: Later resentful—wished to kill him—all morning officials pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: Later he meant to execute him; every official begged mercy.

sentences.zh: 時其人亦在坐，叩頭流血，而融意不解。

translations.literal: At that time that person also sat in the assembly—knocking head bleeding—yet Rong's intent did not relent.
translations.idiomatic: The man kowtowed bloodily; Kong Rong would not relent.

sentences.zh: 原獨不為請。

translations.literal: Yuan alone did not plead.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bing Yuan stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 融謂原曰：「衆皆請而君何獨不？

translations.literal: Rong said to Yuan: "All plead—yet why do you alone not?"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong asked why he alone refused.

sentences.zh: 」原對曰：「明府於某，本不薄也，常言歲終當舉之，此所謂『吾一子』也。

translations.literal: Yuan replied: "Enlightened prefect toward a certain person—originally was not stingy—constantly said at year's end would recommend him—this is what is called 'my one son.'"
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan said: “You called him your adopted son and promised him promotion.
