sentences.zh: 如是，朝吏受恩未有在某前者矣，而今乃欲殺之。

translations.literal: Like this—morning officials receiving favor—none ranked before a certain person—yet now you wish to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: No clerk owed you more—yet now you mean to kill him.

sentences.zh: 明府愛之，則引而方之於子，憎之，則推之欲危其身。

translations.literal: Enlightened prefect loving him—then draws and compares him to a son—hating him—then pushes wishing to endanger his body.
translations.idiomatic: Love likens him to a son; hate wants him dead.

sentences.zh: 原愚，不知明府以何愛之？

translations.literal: Yuan is foolish—does not know by what enlightened prefect loves him?
translations.idiomatic: I cannot tell love from spite.

sentences.zh: 以何惡之？

translations.literal: By what do you hate him?"
translations.idiomatic: Which is real?

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「某生於微門，吾成就其兄弟，拔擢而用之；

translations.literal: Rong said: "A certain person was born in humble gate—I accomplished his brothers—raised and employed him;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong said: “I raised him from nothing;

sentences.zh: 某今孤負恩施。

translations.literal: a certain person now betrays favor received.
translations.idiomatic: He repaid kindness with treason.

sentences.zh: 夫善則進之，惡則誅之，固君道也。

translations.literal: As for good then advance it—as for evil then punish it—solidly is lord's way.
translations.idiomatic: Reward good, kill evil—that is rule.

sentences.zh: 往者應仲遠為泰山太守，舉一孝廉，旬月之間而殺之。

translations.literal: Formerly Ying Zhongyuan was Administrator of Mount Tai—recommended one Filially Pious and Incorrupt—within ten days or a month then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao once nominated a candidate then executed him within the month.

sentences.zh: 夫君人者，厚薄何常之有！

translations.literal: As for lording over people—thick and thin—what constancy is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Rulers swing from love to hate overnight.

sentences.zh: 」原對曰：「仲遠舉孝廉，殺之，其義焉在？

translations.literal: Yuan replied: "Zhongyuan recommended Filially Pious and Incorrupt—killed him—where is the righteousness in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan asked what justice lay in killing a nominee.

sentences.zh: 夫孝廉，國之俊選也。

translations.literal: Filially Pious and Incorrupt—is the state's splendid selection.
translations.idiomatic: Such nominees are national jewels.

sentences.zh: 舉之若是，則殺之非也；

translations.literal: If recommending him thus—then killing him is not right;
translations.idiomatic: If the nomination was sound, killing him was wrong;

sentences.zh: 若殺之是，則舉之非也。

translations.literal: if killing him was right—then recommending him was not right.
translations.idiomatic: if killing him was right, nominating him was wrong.

sentences.zh: 詩云：『彼己之子，不遂其媾。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'That person's son—not completing his match.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: “Those friends failed their troth.

sentences.zh: 』蓋譏之也。

translations.literal: '—thus he mocked them.
translations.idiomatic: —that line exposes Ying Shao’s contradiction.

sentences.zh: 語云：『愛之欲其生，惡之欲其死。

translations.literal: The saying runs: "Love him and wish him to live—hate him and wish him dead.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects say: love someone and you want him to thrive—hate him and you want him dead.

sentences.zh: 旣欲其生，又欲其死，是惑也。

translations.literal: Having wished him to live—yet wishing him dead—that is confusion."
translations.idiomatic: To promote him then execute him is sheer muddle.

sentences.zh: 』仲遠之惑甚矣。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's confusion was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao’s confusion ran deeper still.

sentences.zh: 明府奚取焉？

translations.literal: What does enlightened prefect take from that?
translations.idiomatic: Which lesson do you draw from that tale?

sentences.zh: 」融乃大笑曰：「吾但戲耳！

translations.literal: Rong then laughed loudly and said: "I was only joking!
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong laughed: “Only teasing!

sentences.zh: 」原又曰：「君子於其言，出乎身，加乎民；

translations.literal: Yuan again said: "For the gentleman concerning his speech—it emerges from his person and attaches to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan answered: “A gentleman’s words leave his mouth and bind the people;

sentences.zh: 言行，君子之樞機也。

translations.literal: speech and action are the hinge and trigger of the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: speech and deed are his pivot.

sentences.zh: 安有欲殺人而可以為戲者哉？

translations.literal: How can there be wishing to kill someone yet treating it as jest?"
translations.idiomatic: You cannot joke about killing a man.

sentences.zh: 」融無以荅。

translations.literal: Rong had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 是時漢朝陵遲，政以賄成，原乃將家人入鬱洲山中。

translations.literal: At that time Han declined—government succeeded through bribery—Yuan thereupon led his family into the Yu Isle mountains.
translations.idiomatic: As Han rotted and offices sold for silver, Bing Yuan fled with his kin to Yu Isle.

sentences.zh: 郡舉有道，融書喻原曰：「脩性保貞，清虛守高，危邦不入，久潛樂土。

translations.literal: The commandery nominated him as attained in the Way—Rong wrote instructing Yuan saying: "You cultivate nature preserving purity—pure emptiness guarding loftiness—you do not enter perilous states—you long conceal yourself in happy soil.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong urged him: “You refine yourself and shun dangerous courts.

sentences.zh: 王室多難，西遷鎬京。

translations.literal: The royal house faces many hardships—it moved west to Haojing.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty staggers west like the Zhou move to Haojing.

sentences.zh: 聖朝勞謙，疇咨儁乂。

translations.literal: The sacred court is laboriously humble—it consults outstanding talents.
translations.idiomatic: The court humbly seeks worthies.

sentences.zh: 我徂求定，策命懇惻。

translations.literal: We march seeking stability—policy commands are earnest and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Every edict pleads for help.

sentences.zh: 國之將隕，釐不恤緯，家之將亡，緹縈跋涉，彼匹婦也，猶執此義。

translations.literal: When the state is about to fall—even the widow neglects her weaving—when the house is about to die—Tiying traveled weary—that mere woman—yet upheld this righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Even widows and girls like Tiying rush to save a doomed realm.

sentences.zh: 實望根矩，仁為己任，授手援溺，振民於難。

translations.literal: Truly I hope Genju—takes benevolence as self-assigned duty—extends hand to rescue the drowning—raises people from hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Genju—take humanity as your burden—pull men from the flood.

sentences.zh: 乃或晏晏居息，莫我肯顧，謂之君子，固如此乎！

translations.literal: Yet perhaps you leisurely dwell at ease—none deign look on me—is this called gentleman conduct!
translations.idiomatic: Will you lounge in safety while the realm burns—is that the gentleman’s way?

sentences.zh: 根矩，根矩，可以來矣！

translations.literal: Genju—Genju—you may come now!
translations.idiomatic: Genju—Genju—it is time to come!

sentences.zh: 」原遂到遼東。

translations.literal: Yuan thereupon arrived in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: So Bing Yuan sailed for Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 遼東多虎，原之邑落獨無虎患。

translations.literal: Liaodong had many tigers—Yuan's settlement alone had no tiger trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers plagued Liaodong—yet Bing Yuan’s hamlet never saw one.

sentences.zh: 原甞行而得遺錢，拾以繫樹枝，此錢旣不見取，而繫錢者愈多。

translations.literal: Yuan once while walking found lost coins—picked them and tied them to a tree branch—the coins since none took—and those tying coins grew ever more.
translations.idiomatic: He tied stray cash to a tree; others piled offerings until the trunk glittered.

sentences.zh: 問其故，荅者謂之神樹。

translations.literal: Asked the reason—responders called it a divine tree.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers mistook it for a sacred tree.

sentences.zh: 原惡其由己而成淫祀，乃辨之，於是里中遂斂其錢以為社供。

translations.literal: Yuan hated that through himself it became excessive sacrifice—thereupon explained it—thereupon the village collected the money for community offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed the fraud and pooled the coins for proper village rites.

sentences.zh: 後原欲歸鄉里，止於三山。

translations.literal: Later Yuan wished to return to his native village—stopped at Three Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Later he tried to go home and halted at Three Mountains.

sentences.zh: 孔融書曰：「隨會在秦，賈季在翟，諮仰靡所，歎息增懷。

translations.literal: Kong Rong wrote saying: "Sui Hui stayed in Qin—Jia Ji stayed in Di—nowhere to turn for counsel—sighs pile in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong wrote: “Like exiles yearning for news of home.

sentences.zh: 頃知來至，近在三山。

translations.literal: Recently learned you have arrived—near at Three Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have reached Three Mountains.

sentences.zh: 詩不云乎，『來歸自鎬，我行永久』。

translations.literal: Does not the Odes say—'Coming back from Hao—my march long enduring.'"
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes sing: “Home from the west—the road seemed endless.”

sentences.zh: 今遣五官掾，奉問榜人舟楫之勞，禍福動靜告慰。

translations.literal: Now dispatching the aide of the Five Offices—inquiring of boatmen the labor of oars—fortune and calamity movement and stillness reporting consolation.
translations.idiomatic: He sends an aide to ask after your voyage—whatever fortune finds you.

sentences.zh: 亂階未已，阻兵之雄，若棊奕爭梟。

translations.literal: Steps of chaos not yet ceased—heroes blocking arms—like weiqi players contesting the owl piece.
translations.idiomatic: Warlords still wrestle like chess masters fighting over the king.

sentences.zh: 」原於是遂復反還。

translations.literal: Yuan thereupon again returned.
translations.idiomatic: So Bing Yuan turned back.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，後乃遁還。

translations.literal: Accumulating over ten years—afterward then secretly returned.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years passed before he slipped away.

sentences.zh: 南行已數日，而度甫覺。

translations.literal: Southward march already several days—yet Du only then noticed.
translations.idiomatic: He was days south before Gongsun Du noticed.

sentences.zh: 度知原之不可復追也，因曰：「邴君所謂雲中白鶴，非鶉鷃之網所能羅矣。

translations.literal: Du knew Yuan could not again be pursued—thereupon said: "Lord Bing—what men call the white crane amid clouds—not nets for quail and sparrow can catch.
translations.idiomatic: Du admitted: “Lord Bing is the crane above the clouds—no quail net holds him.

sentences.zh: 又吾自遣之，勿復求也。

translations.literal: Moreover I myself sent him away—do not again seek.
translations.idiomatic: I let him go—do not chase.

sentences.zh: 」遂免危難。

translations.literal: Thereupon escaped peril.
translations.idiomatic: So Bing Yuan escaped.

sentences.zh: 自反國土，原於是講述禮樂，吟詠詩書，門徒數百，服道數十。

translations.literal: Since returning to native soil—Yuan thereupon lectured ritual and music—chanted Odes and Documents—disciples several hundred—those serving the Way several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Home again he taught ritual and classics—hundreds enrolled, dozens mastered the Way.

sentences.zh: 時鄭玄博學洽聞，注解典籍，故儒雅之士集焉。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Xuan was learned broadly and heard widely—annotated classical texts—therefore scholar-gentlemen gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan’s glosses drew every scholar in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 原亦自以高遠清白，頤志澹泊，口無擇言，身無擇行，故英偉之士向焉。

translations.literal: Yuan also himself held lofty remoteness pure clarity—nurturing intent bland and plain—mouth without selective speech—body without selective conduct—therefore heroic worthies turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan matched him—aloof, precise in word and deed—and heroes flocked.

sentences.zh: 是時海內清議，云青州有邴、鄭之學。

translations.literal: At that time pure discussion within the seas—said Qingzhou had Bing and Zheng studies.
translations.idiomatic: Critics spoke of “the Bing and Zheng schools” in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏太祖為司空，辟原署東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: Wei Grand Progenitor was Minister of Works—summoned Yuan appointing Eastern Pavilion Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named him eastern-pavilion libationer.

sentences.zh: 太祖北伐三郡單于，還住昌國，燕士大夫。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor northern campaign against three commandery Chanyu—returned lodging at Changguo—feasted Yan scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: After campaigning against the steppe khans he banqueted Yan scholars at Changguo.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，太祖曰：「孤反，鄴守諸君必將來迎，今日明旦，度皆至矣。

translations.literal: Wine heated—Grand Progenitor said: "I return—Ye guardians you gentlemen surely will come welcome—today clear dawn—I estimate all will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Cao Cao said: “Every Ye official will ride out to greet me by dawn.

sentences.zh: 其不來者，獨有邴祭酒耳！

translations.literal: Those not coming—only Libationer Bing!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone except Libationer Bing.

sentences.zh: 」言訖未久，而原先至。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking long—yet Yuan first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, Bing Yuan arrived first.

sentences.zh: 門下通謁，太祖大驚喜，擥履而起，遠出迎原曰：「賢者誠難測度！

translations.literal: Gate reported visit—Grand Progenitor greatly startled pleased—grabbed shoes and rose—went far out to welcome Yuan saying: "Worthy ones truly hard to measure!
translations.idiomatic: Word came—Cao Cao snatched his sandals and ran: “Sages are unpredictable!

sentences.zh: 孤謂君將不能來，而遠自屈，誠副饑虛之心。

translations.literal: I thought you would not be able to come—yet from afar yourself bending—truly matches hungry empty heart.
translations.idiomatic: I feared you would stay away—you shame me by coming.

sentences.zh: 」謁訖而出，軍中士大夫詣原者數百人。

translations.literal: Visit finished and exited—army scholar-officials who visited Yuan numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of officers lined up to see him.

sentences.zh: 太祖怪而問之，時荀文若在坐，對曰：「獨可省問邴原耳！

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor wondered and asked—at that time Xun Wenruo sat—replied saying: "Only need ask Bing Yuan!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked why; Xun Yu said: “Ask Bing Yuan.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「此君名重，乃亦傾士大夫心？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: "This lord's name weighty—yet also overturns scholar-official hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: Could one scholar sway them all?

sentences.zh: 」文若曰：「此一世異人，士之精藻，公宜盡禮以待之。

translations.literal: Wenruo said: "This generation's unusual man—essence and brilliance of scholars—lord ought use full ritual to treat him."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said: “He is singular—honor him fully.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「固孤之宿心也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: "Solidly my long-standing heart."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said: “Always my intent.

sentences.zh: 」自是之後，見敬益重。

translations.literal: From this after—seen respect increasingly heavy.
translations.idiomatic: After that Cao Cao esteemed him more.

sentences.zh: 原雖在軍歷署，常以病疾，高枕里巷，終不當事，又希會見。

translations.literal: Yuan though in army passed through offices—constantly citing illness—high pillow in lanes—to end did not handle affairs—also rarely met audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan stayed on sick leave in his lane—avoiding duty and audiences.

sentences.zh: 河內張範，名公之子也，其志行有與原符，甚相親敬。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan of Henei—son of famed lord—his intent and conduct matched Yuan's—very mutually intimate and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan of Henei—kindred spirit—became his closest friend.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「邴原名高德大，清規邈世，魁然而峙，不為孤用。

translations.literal: Order said: "Bing Yuan—name high virtue great—pure regulation distant from age—towering standing—not employed by me.
translations.idiomatic: An edict lamented: “Bing Yuan towers above the age yet will not serve me.

sentences.zh: 聞張子頗欲學之，吾恐造之者富，隨之者貧也。

translations.literal: Hearing Zhang Zi quite wishes to study him—I fear makers thereof rich—followers thereof poor."
translations.idiomatic: If Zhang Fan copies him, donors grow rich and hangers-on stay poor.

sentences.zh: 」魏太子為五官中郎將，天下向慕，賔客如雲，而原獨守道持常，自非公事不妄舉動。

translations.literal: Wei heir became General of the Five Offices—all under Heaven turned admiration—guests like clouds—yet Yuan alone guarded Way holding constant—unless public business did not rashly move.
translations.idiomatic: While the heir filled his salon, Bing Yuan ignored fashion unless duty called.

sentences.zh: 太祖微使人從容問之，原曰：「吾聞國危不事冢宰，君去不奉世子，此典制也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor subtly sent someone casually ask him—Yuan said: "I have heard state in peril does not serve chief minister—lord departed does not attend heir apparent—this is canonical regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why he shunned the heir, he cited canon: crisis forbids serving grand ministers; absence frees one from the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 」於是乃轉五官長史，令曰：「子弱不才，懼其難正，貪欲相屈，以匡勵之。

translations.literal: Thereupon then transferred chief clerk of Five Offices—order said: "Son weak lacking talent—fear him hard to correct—greedy desire bend you—to rectify and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: So Cao Cao made him chief clerk to the heir: “My son needs discipline—I burden you.

sentences.zh: 雖云利賢，能不恧恧！

translations.literal: Though called benefiting worthy—how can one not feel ashamed!
translations.idiomatic: Even benefiting him leaves me ashamed.

sentences.zh: 」太子燕會，衆賔百數十人，太子建議曰：「君父各有篤疾，有藥一丸，可救一人，當救君邪，父邪？

translations.literal: Heir feast gathering—guests over a hundred—heir raised proposal saying: "Lord and father each have grave illness—there is medicine one pill—can save one person—ought save lord or father?"
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the heir asked: “One pill saves one dying man—father or lord?

sentences.zh: 」衆人紛紜，或父或君。

translations.literal: Crowd confused—some father some lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guests split evenly.

sentences.zh: 時原在坐，不與此論。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan sat—did not join this discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan stayed out of the debate.

sentences.zh: 太子諮之於原，原悖然對曰：「父也。

translations.literal: Heir consulted Yuan—Yuan bluntly replied: "Father."
translations.idiomatic: Pressed for an answer he said: “Father.

sentences.zh: 」太子亦不復難之。〉

translations.literal: Heir also did not again challenge him.〉
translations.idiomatic: The heir dropped the subject.)

sentences.zh: 是後大鴻臚鉅鹿張泰、河南尹扶風龐辿以清賢稱，

translations.literal: Afterward Grand Herald Zhang Tai of Julu—Governor of Henan Pang Chan of Fufeng—by pure worthiness praised,
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Tai of Julu as grand herald and Pang Chan of Fufeng as Henan governor won fame for purity,

sentences.zh: 〈荀綽《冀州記》曰：鉅鹿張貔，字邵虎。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Jizhou ji states: Zhang Pi of Julu—courtesy name Shaohu.
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuzhou ji adds Zhang Pi, styled Shaohu.

sentences.zh: 祖父泰，字伯陽，有名於魏。

translations.literal: Grandfather Tai—courtesy name Boyang—had fame in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang Tai, styled Boyang, was celebrated in Wei.

sentences.zh: 父邈，字叔遼，遼東太守。

translations.literal: Father Miao—courtesy name Shuliao—Administrator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Miao governed Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 著名自然好學論，在嵇康集。

translations.literal: Famous for Treatise on Natural Love of Learning—in Ji Kang's collection.
translations.idiomatic: His essay on loving learning appears in Ji Kang’s works.

sentences.zh: 為人弘深有遠識，恢恢然，使求之者莫之能測也。

translations.literal: As person vast deep with far insight—expansively—making seekers unable to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded and unreadable as water.

sentences.zh: 宦歷二宮，元康初為城陽太守，未行而卒。〉

translations.literal: Served passing two palaces—early Yuankang became Administrator of Chengyang—before going died.
translations.idiomatic: He served two courts, took Chengyang, then died before posting.

sentences.zh: 永寧太僕東郡張閣以簡質聞。

translations.literal: Yongning Grand Coachman Zhang Ge of Dongjun—by simplicity heard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ge of Dongjun, grand coachman under Yongning, was famed for plain living.

sentences.zh: 杜恕著家戒稱閣曰：「張子臺，視之似鄙樸人，然其心中不知天地間何者為美，何者為好，敦然似如與陰陽合德者。

translations.literal: Du Shu in Family Admonitions called Ge saying: "Zhang Zitai—looking at him seems rustic plain person—yet in his heart does not know between Heaven and Earth what is beauty what is good—solidly seems like joining yin-yang in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shu wrote: “Zhang Ge looks dull yet embodies harmony with heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 作人如此，自可不富貴，然而患禍當何從而來？

translations.literal: Being human thus—naturally may not be rich noble—yet disaster calamity from where should come?
translations.idiomatic: Such men may never grow rich—what calamity could touch them?

sentences.zh: 世有高亮如子臺者，皆多力慕，體之不如也。」

translations.literal: Age has lofty bright like Zitai—all much admire—embodying not equal.
translations.idiomatic: The world admires men like him though few match him.

sentences.zh: 管寧字幼安，北海朱虛人也。

translations.literal: Guan Ning—courtesy name You'an—was a man of Zhuxu in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning, styled You’an, came from Zhuxu in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：齊相管仲之後也。

translations.literal: The Fuzi states: descendant of Qi minister Guan Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: (The Fuzi traces him to Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 昔田氏有齊而管氏去之，或適魯，或適楚。

translations.literal: Formerly Tian clan possessed Qi yet Guan clan left—some went Lu—some Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tian seized Qi, the Guan clan scattered to Lu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 漢興有管少卿為燕令，始家朱虛，世有名節，九世而生寧。〉

translations.literal: Han rose had Guan Shaoqing as Yan magistrate—first household Zhuxu—generations had fame and integrity—nine generations then bore Ning.〉
translations.idiomatic: A Guan Shaoqing settled Zhuxu under Han; nine generations later came Guan Ning.)

sentences.zh: 年十六喪父，中表愍其孤貧，咸共贈賵，悉辭不受，稱財以送終。

translations.literal: Age sixteen lost father—cousins pitied him orphan poor—all together offered funeral gifts—all declined not accepting—matching wealth to bury.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at sixteen, he refused kinfolk’s funeral gifts and buried his father with what he could afford.

sentences.zh: 長八尺，美須眉。

translations.literal: Height eight chi—beautiful beard and brows.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall with striking beard and brows.

sentences.zh: 與平原華歆、同縣邴原相友，俱游學於異國，並敬善陳仲弓。

translations.literal: With Hua Xin of Pingyuan—Bing Yuan same county—mutual friends—all traveled study in foreign lands—together revered Chen Zhonggong.
translations.idiomatic: With Hua Xin of Pingyuan and Bing Yuan he studied abroad and revered Chen Zhonggong.

sentences.zh: 天下大亂，聞公孫度令行於海外，遂與原及平原王烈等至于遼東。

translations.literal: Realm great chaos—heard Gongsun Du commands executed beyond seas—thereupon with Yuan and Wang Lie of Pingyuan etc. reached Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos erupted they heard Gongsun Du ruled Liaodong and sailed there with Bing Yuan and Wang Lie.

sentences.zh: 度虛館以候之。

translations.literal: Du emptied lodge to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du cleared a guesthouse for them.

sentences.zh: 旣往見度，乃廬於山谷。

translations.literal: Already gone saw Du—thereupon hut in mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: After the courtesy call Guan Ning built a hut in the hills.

sentences.zh: 時避難者多居郡南，而寧居北，示無遷志，後漸來從之。

translations.literal: At that time fugitives mostly dwelt south of commandery—yet Ning dwelt north—showing no intent to move—afterward gradually came follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees clustered south; Guan Ning camped north to show he would not drift—and disciples followed.

sentences.zh: 太祖為司空，辟寧，度子康絕命不宣。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Minister of Works—summoned Ning—Du's son Kang cut command not proclaim.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao summoned Guan Ning, Gongsun Kang suppressed the edict.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：寧往見度，語唯經典，不及世事。

translations.literal: The Fuzi states: Ning went saw Du—speech only classics—not reaching worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: (The Fuzi: Guan Ning discussed only the canon with Du.

sentences.zh: 還乃因山為廬，鑿坏為室。

translations.literal: Returned then by mountain made hut—chiseled earth for room.
translations.idiomatic: Home in the hills he dug a cellar hut.

sentences.zh: 越海避難者，皆來就之而居，旬月而成邑。

translations.literal: Sea-crossing fugitives—all came attach dwell—ten days month became settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles moored beside him until a town grew in weeks.

sentences.zh: 遂講詩、書，陳俎豆，飾威儀，明禮讓，非學者無見也。

translations.literal: Thereupon lectured Odes Documents—displayed vessels—adorned awe-inspiring deportment—clarified ritual yielding—non-students none saw.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the classics, staged sacrifices, drilled deportment, and shut his door to casual callers.

sentences.zh: 由是度安其賢，民化其德。

translations.literal: Thereby Du peaceful his worth—people transformed his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Du trusted his virtue; commoners copied his manners.

sentences.zh: 邴原性剛直，清議以格物，度已下心不安之。

translations.literal: Bing Yuan nature rigid straight—pure discussion to regulate things—Du already lowered heart uneasy with him.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan’s blunt criticism unsettled Gongsun Du.

sentences.zh: 寧謂原曰：「潛龍以不見成德，言非其時，皆招禍之道也。

translations.literal: Ning said to Yuan: "Submerged dragon by not appearing completes virtue—speech not its time—all roads inviting calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning warned him: “Hidden dragons stay silent—untimely words invite ruin.

sentences.zh: 」密遣令西還。

translations.literal: Secretly sent order west return.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged Bing Yuan to flee west.

sentences.zh: 度庶子康代居郡，外以將軍太守為號，而內實有王心，卑己崇禮，欲官寧以自鎮輔，而終莫敢發言，其敬憚如此。

translations.literal: Du's bastard son Kang replaced dwelling commandery—outwardly used general administrator titles—yet inwardly truly had king mind—humbled self revered ritual—wished to office Ning to self stabilize assist—yet to end never dared speak—such his awe.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Kang played king in all but name—yearned to hire Guan Ning as minister yet never dared ask aloud.

sentences.zh: 皇甫謐《高士傳》曰：寧所居屯落，會井汲者，或男女雜錯，或爭井鬬鬩。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi's Gaoshi zhuan states: Ning's dwelling settlement—gathered well drawers—some male female mixed—some quarreling well fighting.
translations.idiomatic: (Huangfu Mi: at the village well men and women jostled and brawled.

sentences.zh: 寧患之，乃多買器，分置井傍，汲以待之，又不使知。

translations.literal: Ning worried—thereupon bought many vessels—distributed place well beside—draw to await them—again not let know.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning bought buckets, left them at the well, and filled them anonymously.

sentences.zh: 來者得而怪之，問知寧所為，乃各相責，不復鬬訟。

translations.literal: Those who came found it strange—asked and learned what Ning had done—thereupon each blamed themselves—no longer quarreling or suing.
translations.idiomatic: Drawers found the filled buckets and guessed Guan Ning’s handiwork—they stopped brawling at the well.

sentences.zh: 鄰有牛暴寧田者，寧為牽牛著涼處，自為飲食，過於牛主。

translations.literal: A neighbor had an ox rampage Ning's field—Ning led the ox to a cool place—fed it himself—more generously than the ox's owner.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor’s ox trampled his crop, Guan Ning led it to shade, fed it better than its master.

sentences.zh: 牛主得牛，大慙，若犯嚴刑。

translations.literal: The ox owner recovered the ox—greatly ashamed—as if suffering harsh punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The owner was humiliated as if flogged.

sentences.zh: 是以左右無鬬訟之聲，禮讓移於海表。〉

translations.literal: Therefore on left and right no sounds of quarrel or lawsuit—ritual yielding moved beyond the seas.〉
translations.idiomatic: Neighbor disputes vanished—courtesy reached even Liaodong.)

sentences.zh: 王烈者，字彥方，於時名聞在原、寧之右。

translations.literal: Wang Lie—courtesy name Yanfang—at that time his fame was heard to the right of Yuan and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lie, styled Yanfang, outranked Bing Yuan and Guan Ning in renown.

sentences.zh: 辭公孫度長史，商賈自穢。

translations.literal: He declined chief clerk to Gongsun Du—and debased himself among merchants.
translations.idiomatic: He refused Du’s chief clerk post and worked as a tradesman to stay obscure.

sentences.zh: 太祖命為丞相掾，徵事，未至，卒於海表。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor ordered him aide to the minister and Investigator—before arriving he died beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao summoned him as investigator—he died en route from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 〈《先賢行狀》曰：烈通識達道，秉義不回。

translations.literal: The Conduct of Former Worthies states: Lie comprehended the Way and held righteousness without bending.
translations.idiomatic: (The Xianxian xingzhuang: Wang Lie grasped the Way and never bent principle.

sentences.zh: 以潁川陳太丘為師，二子為友。

translations.literal: He took Chen Taiqiu of Yingchuan as teacher—and the two sons as friends.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Chen Shi and befriended his sons.

sentences.zh: 時潁川荀慈明、賈偉節、李元禮、韓元長皆就陳君學，見烈器業過人，歎服所履，亦與相親。

translations.literal: At that time Xun Ciming, Jia Weijie, Li Yuanli, and Han Yuanchang of Yingchuan all studied under Lord Chen—seeing Lie's capacity and enterprise surpass others—they admired his conduct—and also drew close to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingchuan luminaries who studied with Chen Shi admired Wang Lie’s stature.

sentences.zh: 由是英名著於海內。

translations.literal: By this his heroic name became renowned within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 道成德立，還歸舊廬，遂遭父喪，泣淚三年。

translations.literal: The Way completed and virtue established—he returned to his old hut—thereupon encountered his father's death—and wept three years.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue won, he went home—then mourned his father three years.

sentences.zh: 遇歲饑饉，路有餓殍，烈乃分釜庚之儲，以救邑里之命。

translations.literal: He met a year of famine—corpses of the starved lay on the roads—Lie divided his cauldron-grain stores—to save the lives of his village.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he emptied his granary for the hamlet.

sentences.zh: 是以宗族稱孝，鄉黨歸仁。

translations.literal: Therefore his lineage called him filial—the village submitted to his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Kin called him filial; neighbors deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 以典籍娛心，育人為務，遂建學校，敦崇庠序。

translations.literal: Using the classics to entertain his heart—and nurturing people as his task—he established schools and honored the village schools.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools and taught the classics.

sentences.zh: 其誘人也，皆不因其性氣，誨之以道，使之從善遠惡。

translations.literal: In winning people over—he never tailored lessons to temper alone—but instructed with the Way—and made them follow good and flee evil.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the Way and steered men toward good.

sentences.zh: 益者不自覺，而大化隆行，皆成寶器。

translations.literal: Those benefited did not themselves realize it—yet great transformation flourished—and all became vessels of treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Pupils hardly noticed the change—yet every graduate shone.

sentences.zh: 門人出入，容止可觀，時在市井，行步有異，人皆別之。

translations.literal: Disciples coming and going—bearing and gait worth viewing—sometimes in the market—their gait unusual—people distinguished them.
translations.idiomatic: His students walked so upright that crowds spotted them.

sentences.zh: 州閭成風，咸競為善。

translations.literal: Village customs became a wind—all competed to do good.
translations.idiomatic: The district raced to outdo one another in virtue.

sentences.zh: 時國中有盜牛者，牛主得之。

translations.literal: At that time in the state someone stole an ox—the ox owner caught him.
translations.idiomatic: When a cattle thief was caught,

sentences.zh: 盜者曰：「我邂逅迷惑，從今已後將為改過。

translations.literal: The thief said: "I stumbled into error—from now on I shall reform.
translations.idiomatic: the thief swore reform.

sentences.zh: 子旣已赦宥，幸無使王烈聞之。

translations.literal: Since you have already pardoned me—pray do not let Wang Lie hear of it."
translations.idiomatic: He begged silence lest Wang Lie learn of it.

sentences.zh: 」人有以告烈者，烈以布一端遺之。

translations.literal: Someone informed Lie—Lie gave him one bolt of cloth as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lie heard, he sent the thief a bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 或問：「此人旣為盜，畏君聞之，反與之布，何也？

translations.literal: Someone asked: "This man was a thief—he feared you would hear—yet you give him cloth—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Critics asked why reward a thief.

sentences.zh: 」烈曰：「昔秦穆公，人盜其駿馬食之，乃賜之酒。

translations.literal: Lie said: "Formerly Duke Mu of Qin—someone stole his fine horse and ate it—and he gifted wine."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lie cited Duke Mu of Qin, who forgave horse thieves.

sentences.zh: 盜者不愛其死，以救穆公之難。

translations.literal: The thief did not spare his own life—to save Duke Mu from peril.
translations.idiomatic: Those thieves later died saving Mu.

sentences.zh: 今此盜人能悔其過，懼吾聞之，是知恥惡。

translations.literal: Now this thief can regret his fault—and fears I will hear—is to know shame of evil.
translations.idiomatic: Shame proves a conscience.

sentences.zh: 知恥惡，則善心將生，故與布勸為善也。

translations.literal: Knowing shame of evil—then a good heart will arise—therefore I give cloth to encourage good."
translations.idiomatic: That deserves encouragement.

sentences.zh: 」間年之中，行路老父擔重，人代擔行數十里，欲至家，置而去，問姓名，不以告。

translations.literal: Within the year—an old father on the road carried a heavy load—someone carried it for him several tens of li—about to reach home—he set it down and left—asked his name—he would not tell.
translations.idiomatic: Later a stranger hauled an old man’s load for miles and vanished without giving his name.

sentences.zh: 頃之，老父復行，失劒於路。

translations.literal: Presently the old father walked again—and lost a sword on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The same elder dropped a sword.

sentences.zh: 有人行而遇之，欲置而去，懼後人得之，劒主於是永失，欲取而購募，或恐差錯，遂守之。

translations.literal: Someone walking met it—wished to set it down and leave—feared a later passerby would take it—the sword owner would thereby lose it forever—wished to take it and offer reward—or feared mistake—therefore guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: A passerby guarded the blade rather than pocket it.

sentences.zh: 至暮，劒主還見之，前者代擔人也。

translations.literal: At dusk—the sword owner returned and saw—the former person who had carried the load.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the owner found the same helper.

sentences.zh: 老父擥其袂，問曰：「子前者代吾擔，不得姓名，今子復守吾劒于路，未有若子之仁，請子告吾姓名，吾將以告王烈。

translations.literal: The old father grasped his sleeve and asked: "You formerly carried for me yet I learned no name—now you guard my sword on the road—none so benevolent as you—please tell me your name—I shall report it to Wang Lie."
translations.idiomatic: The elder seized his sleeve and demanded his name for Wang Lie.

sentences.zh: 」乃語之而去。

translations.literal: He told him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The man whispered his name and fled.

sentences.zh: 老父以告烈，烈曰：「世有仁人，吾未之見。

translations.literal: The old father reported to Lie—Lie said: "The age has a benevolent man—I have not seen him."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lie marveled: “I never met such goodness.

sentences.zh: 」遂使人推之，乃昔時盜牛人也。

translations.literal: Thereupon sent men investigate—it was the former ox thief.
translations.idiomatic: An inquiry proved he was the cattle thief.

sentences.zh: 烈歎曰：「韶樂九成，虞賔以和：人能有感，乃至於斯也！

translations.literal: Lie sighed: "When Shao music reaches nine completions—the Yu guests harmonize—human beings can be moved—even to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lie sighed: “Music moves gods—men can change too!

sentences.zh: 」遂使國人表其閭而異之。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered the countrymen to mark his gate as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a plaque hung on the man’s gate.

sentences.zh: 時人或訟曲直，將質於烈，或至塗而反，或望廬而還，皆相推以直，不敢使烈聞之。

translations.literal: When people sometimes disputed right and wrong—and were about to arbitrate with Lie—some reached the road and returned—some saw his hut and returned—all yielded the right—dared not let Lie hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants settled out of court rather than trouble Wang Lie.

sentences.zh: 時國主皆親驂乘適烈私館，疇諮政令。

translations.literal: State rulers all personally rode in the side carriage to Lie's private lodge—to consult on policy commands.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong’s rulers drove to his cottage for advice.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，三府並辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: Nominated Filially Pious and Incorrupt—the Three Offices jointly summoned—he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every capital summons.

sentences.zh: 會董卓作亂，避地遼東，躬秉農器，編於四民，布衣蔬食，不改其樂。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo rebelled—he fled to Liaodong—personally wielded farm tools—woven among the four peoples—plain cloth and coarse greens—did not alter his joy.
translations.idiomatic: He fled Zhuo to Liaodong, farmed among commoners, and stayed content.

sentences.zh: 東域之人，奉之若君。

translations.literal: People of the eastern domain served him as they would a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Liaodong treated him like a prince.

sentences.zh: 時衰世弊，識真者少，朋黨之人，互相讒謗。

translations.literal: The age decayed and flaws multiplied—few recognized truth—faction members mutually slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Faction politics poisoned everyone who could judge.

sentences.zh: 自避世在東國者，多為人所害，烈居之歷年，未甞有患。

translations.literal: Those avoiding the world in the eastern lands—many were harmed by others—Lie dwelt there years—never suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles usually died—Wang Lie did not.

sentences.zh: 使遼東彊不淩弱，衆不暴寡，商賈之人，市不二價。

translations.literal: He made Liaodong strong not bully weak—many not brutalize few—merchants in market did not hold two prices.
translations.idiomatic: Under his moral sway the strong spared the weak and markets stayed honest.

sentences.zh: 太祖累徵召，遼東為解而不遣。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor repeatedly summoned—Liaodong made excuses and did not dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao called repeatedly; Liaodong stalled.

sentences.zh: 以建安二十三年寢疾，年七十八而終。〉

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jian'an he fell ill—and died at age seventy-eight.〉
translations.idiomatic: He died in 218 CE at seventy-eight.)

sentences.zh: 自黃初至于青龍，徵命相仍，常以八月賜牛酒。

translations.literal: From Huangchu down to Qinglong—summons followed one after another—often in the eighth month oxen and wine were gifted.
translations.idiomatic: From Huangchu through Qinglong the court sent oxen and wine each autumn.

sentences.zh: 詔書問青州刺史程喜：「寧為守節高乎，審老疾尪頓邪？

translations.literal: An edict asked Qingzhou Inspector Cheng Xi: "Is Ning guarding integrity out of loftiness—or truly old, sick, and exhausted?"
translations.idiomatic: An edict asked Cheng Xi whether Guan Ning refused office on principle or from frailty.

sentences.zh: 」喜上言：「寧有族人管貢為州吏，與寧鄰比，臣常使經營消息。

translations.literal: Xi memorialized: "Ning has a clansman Guan Gong who serves as state clerk—living adjacent to Ning—your servant often sent him to gather news.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xi cited his neighbor Guan Gong as witness.

sentences.zh: 貢說：『寧常著皁帽、布襦袴、布裠，隨時單複，出入閨庭，能自任杖，不須扶持。

translations.literal: Gong reported: Ning constantly wears a black cap, cloth jacket and trousers, cloth skirt—according to season single or layered—enters and exits the inner courtyard—can lean on a staff himself—needs no support.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gong described Guan Ning’s dress and steady gait.

sentences.zh: 四時祠祭，輙自力彊，改加衣服，著絮巾，故在遼東所有白布單衣，親薦饌饋，跪拜成禮。

translations.literal: At the four seasons' sacrifices—he always forces himself—changes clothes—wears a cotton turban—still has the white cloth single garment from Liaodong—personally presents food—kneels and bows completing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At ancestral rites he still dons his Liaodong robe and completes every bow.

sentences.zh: 寧少而喪母，不識形象，常特加觴，泫然流涕。

translations.literal: Ning young lost his mother—did not know her appearance—always sets an extra cup—tears flowing.
translations.idiomatic: For the mother he never knew he pours an extra cup and weeps.

sentences.zh: 又居宅離水七八十步，夏時詣水中澡灑手足，闚於園圃。

translations.literal: Also his dwelling is seventy or eighty paces from water—in summer he goes to the water to bathe hands and feet—and peers into the garden.
translations.idiomatic: His hut stands near a stream; he still bathes and gardens in summer.

sentences.zh: 』臣揆寧前後辭讓之意，獨自以生長潛逸，耆艾智衰，是以栖遲，每執謙退。

translations.literal: Your servant gauges Ning's intent in repeatedly declining—he alone because he was born and grew in hidden reclusion—old age and wisdom declining—therefore lingers—always holding humble retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xi argued Guan Ning declined from modest old age, not posturing.

sentences.zh: 此寧志行所欲必全，不為守高。」

translations.literal: This is Ning's intent and conduct—what he desires he must complete—not for guarding loftiness."
translations.idiomatic: He seeks sincerity, not fame.

sentences.zh: 〈《高士傳》曰：管寧自越海及歸，常坐一木榻，積五十餘年，未甞箕股，其榻上當膝處皆穿。〉

translations.literal: The Gaoshi zhuan states: Guan Ning from crossing the sea to returning—constantly sat on one wooden couch—for more than fifty years—never sat with legs apart—the places on the couch where knees rested are all worn through.〉
translations.idiomatic: (Huangfu Mi: Guan Ning sat fifty years on one couch—knees wore holes in the wood.)

sentences.zh: 正始二年，太僕陶丘一、永寧衞尉孟觀、侍中孫邕、中書侍郎王基薦寧曰：

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi—Grand Coachman Tao Qiuyi—Commandant of Yongning Meng Guan—attendant Sun Yong—Secretariat attendant Wang Ji recommended Ning saying:
translations.idiomatic: In 241 Tao Qiuyi, Meng Guan, Sun Yong, and Wang Ji jointly memorialized for Guan Ning:

sentences.zh: 臣聞龍鳳隱耀，應德而臻，明哲潛遁，俟時而動。

translations.literal: Your servants have heard that dragon and phoenix hide their radiance—and respond to virtue by arriving—that the wise conceal themselves—and await the moment to move.
translations.idiomatic: They opened: worthies wait for the right sovereign.

sentences.zh: 是以鸞鷟鳴岐，周道隆興，四皓為佐，漢帝用康。

translations.literal: Therefore the luan and zhuo sang on Qi—and the Zhou Way rose and flourished—the Four Elders assisted—and the Han emperor enjoyed peace.
translations.idiomatic: They cited omens from Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 伏見太中大夫管寧，應二儀之中和，總九德之純懿，含章素質，冰絜淵清，玄虛澹泊，與道逍遙；

translations.literal: We behold Grand Counsellor Guan Ning—who responds to the harmony of the Two Pivots—who gathers the purity of the Nine Virtues—who holds pattern in plain substance—pure as ice, clear as an abyss—dark void and bland—and roams free with the Way;
translations.idiomatic: They praised Guan Ning’s cosmic virtue.

sentences.zh: 娛心黃老，游志六藝，升堂入室，究其閫奧，韜古今於胷懷，包道德之機要。

translations.literal: His heart delights in Huang-Lao—his mind roams the Six Arts—he ascends the hall and enters the inner chamber—probing their inner depths—concealing ancient and modern in his breast—wrapping the essentials of Way and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They listed his mastery of Daoism and the classics.

sentences.zh: 中平之際，黃巾陸梁，華夏傾蕩，王綱弛頓。

translations.literal: In the Zhongping era—the Yellow Turbans rampaged—Huaxia was overturned—the royal net slackened.
translations.idiomatic: They recalled the Zhongping turmoil.

sentences.zh: 遂避時難，乘桴越海，羈旅遼東三十餘年。

translations.literal: Therefore he avoided the hardship of the times—rode a raft across the sea—and sojourned in Liaodong more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He fled thirty years in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 在乾之姤，匿景藏光，嘉遁養浩，韜韞儒墨，潛化傍流，暢於殊俗。

translations.literal: In the hexagram Qian's Gou—he hid shadow and concealed light—fine retreat nurturing vastness—concealing Confucian and Mohist teaching—secretly transforming those beside him—flowing even into alien customs.
translations.idiomatic: There he hid like the Book of Changes counsels—teaching even barbarians.

sentences.zh: 黃初四年，高祖文皇帝疇咨羣公，思求儁乂，故司徒華歆舉寧應選，公車特徵，振翼遐裔，翻然來翔。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangchu—the High Ancestor Wendi consulted the assembled lords—seeking outstanding talents—therefore Minister Hua Xin nominated Ning in response to selection—imperial carriage made special summons—he spread wings on distant shores—and fluttered down to soar.
translations.idiomatic: In 223 Wendi summoned him via Hua Xin.

sentences.zh: 行遇屯厄，遭罹疾病，即拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: Going he met obstruction and hardship—encountered disease—and was appointed Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: Illness waylaid him—court named him grand counsellor.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝嘉美其德，登為光祿勳。

translations.literal: Liezu Mingdi praised his virtue—and promoted him Minister of Court Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi raised him to minister of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 寧疾彌留，未能進道。

translations.literal: Ning's illness lingered—unable to advance into office.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness kept him from duties.

sentences.zh: 今寧舊疾已瘳，行年八十，志無衰倦。

translations.literal: Now Ning's old illness is healed—his traveling year is eighty—his intent shows no decline or weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Now eighty and recovered, he remains vigorous.

sentences.zh: 環堵篳門，偃息窮巷，飯鬻餬口，并日而食，吟詠詩書，不改其樂。

translations.literal: Ringed walls and wicker gate—reclining in rest in a poor lane—eating gruel to fill his mouth—eating every other day—chanting Odes and Documents—he does not alter his joy.
translations.idiomatic: He lives in a lane on gruel yet stays cheerful.

sentences.zh: 困而能通，遭難必濟，經危蹈險，不易其節，金聲玉色，乆而彌彰。

translations.literal: Troubled yet able to penetrate—encountering hardship he surely fords—passing danger and treading peril—he does not change his integrity—gold sound and jade color—long enduring grows brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Hardship only polished his integrity.

sentences.zh: 揆其終始，殆天所祚，當贊大魏，輔亮雍熙。

translations.literal: Surveying his beginning and end—probably Heaven blesses him—he ought to assist great Wei—and aid the bright harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven meant him to serve Wei.

sentences.zh: 袞職有闕，羣下屬望。

translations.literal: The imperial robe post stands vacant—subordinates gaze expectantly.
translations.idiomatic: The realm waits for him to fill high office.

sentences.zh: 昔高宗刻象，營求賢哲，周文啟龜，以卜良佐。

translations.literal: Formerly Gaozong carved images—to camp and seek the wise—Zhou Wen opened the tortoise—to divine a good aide.
translations.idiomatic: They cited Shang Gaozong and Zhou Wen seeking ministers.

sentences.zh: 況寧前朝所表，名德已著，而乆栖遲，未時引致，非所以奉遵明訓，繼成前志也。

translations.literal: Moreover Ning was memorialized by the former court—his name and virtue already manifest—yet long he lingers—not timely summoned and brought in—not thereby obeying the bright instruction—or continuing to complete the former intent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier memorials praised him—delay dishonors precedent.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐阼，纂承洪緒。

translations.literal: Your majesty has ascended the throne—and inherits the great continuity.
translations.idiomatic: Your majesty inherits the mandate.

sentences.zh: 聖敬日躋，超越周成。

translations.literal: Sacred reverence climbs daily—surpassing Zhou Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue surpasses the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 每發德音，動諮師傅。

translations.literal: Each time issuing virtuous edicts—you move to consult teachers.
translations.idiomatic: You consult tutors with every edict.

sentences.zh: 若繼二祖招賢故典，賔禮儁邁，以廣緝熙，濟濟之化，侔於前代。

translations.literal: If you continue the two ancestors' pattern of summoning worthies—and guest-ritual for the outstanding—to broaden the harmonious brightness—and crowd the transformation—to match the former generation.
translations.idiomatic: Continue Wendi and Mingdi’s guest ritual.

sentences.zh: 寧清高恬泊，擬跡前軌，德行卓絕，海內無偶。

translations.literal: Ning is pure, lofty, and bland—traces former tracks—his virtue and conduct are exceptional—within the seas none rivals him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning has no peer.

sentences.zh: 歷觀前世玉帛所命，申公、枚乘、周黨、樊英之儔，測其淵源，覽其清濁，未有厲俗獨行若寧者也。

translations.literal: Surveying former generations whom jade and silk commanded—Shen Gong, Mei Cheng, Zhou Dang, Fan Ying and their sort—measuring their origins—viewing their clarity and muddiness—none hardened custom and walked alone like Ning.
translations.idiomatic: No hermit rivaled Guan Ning.

sentences.zh: 誠宜束帛加璧，備禮徵聘，仍授几杖，延登東序，敷陳墳素，坐而論道，上正璇璣，恊和皇極，下阜羣生，彝倫攸叙，必有可觀，光益大化。

translations.literal: Truly one ought bundle silk and add jade disks—complete the ritual of summons—still grant stool and staff—extend him to ascend the eastern hall—spread the tomb-texts—sit and discuss the Way—above rectify the celestial pivot—harmonize the supreme pole—below enrich the multitude—put moral relations in order—surely something worth observing—light benefiting the great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Summon him with full honors to tutor the throne.

sentences.zh: 若寧固執匪石，守志箕山，追迹洪崖，參蹤巢、許。

translations.literal: If Ning stubbornly remains unyielding as stone—guards his intent on Mount Ji—traces Hong Ya—follows in the footsteps of Chao and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: If he insists on life like the sages of Ji Mountain,

sentences.zh: 斯亦聖朝同符唐、虞，優賢揚歷，垂聲千載。

translations.literal: This too lets the sacred court match Tang and Yu—in promoting worthies and displaying experience—to hang fame for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: the court still shines like Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 〈《今文尚書》曰「優賢揚歷」，謂揚其所歷試。

translations.literal: The Jinwen Shangshu says "promote worthies and display experience"—meaning to display what they experienced in trial.
translations.idiomatic: (Pei Songzhi glosses the phrase as displaying worthies by broadcasting what they proved in office trials.

sentences.zh: 左思《魏都賦》曰：「優賢著於揚歷」也。〉

translations.literal: Zuo Si's Wei du fu says: "promote worthies manifests in displayed experience."〉
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si’s Wei capital fu echoes the phrase.)

sentences.zh: 雖出處殊塗，俯仰異體，至於興治美俗，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Though emerging and dwelling follow different paths—and bowing and raising belong to different bodies—as for raising order and beautifying custom—the principle is one.
translations.idiomatic: Serve or retreat—both orders the age.

sentences.zh: 於是特具安車蒲輪，束帛加璧聘焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they specially prepared a comfortable carriage with rush wheels—and bundled silk with added jade to hire him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the full carriage-and-jade summons.

sentences.zh: 會寧卒，時年八十四。

translations.literal: It happened that Ning died—at that time age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning died at eighty-four before the escort arrived.

sentences.zh: 拜子邈郎中，後為博士。

translations.literal: His son Miao was appointed Gentleman—and later became erudite.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan Miao became gentleman and academician.

sentences.zh: 初，寧妻先卒，知故勸更娶，寧曰：「每省曾子、王駿之言，意常嘉之，豈自遭之而違本心哉？」

translations.literal: Earlier Ning's wife had died first—friends knowing the story urged him to remarry—Ning said: "Whenever I reflect on Zengzi and Wang Jun's words—my heart always praises them—how could I encounter this myself yet violate my original heart?"
translations.idiomatic: When urged to remarry he cited Zengzi on fidelity to one wife.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：寧以衰亂之時，世多妄變氏族者，違聖人之制，非禮命姓之意，故著《氏姓論》以原本世系，文多不載。

translations.literal: The Fuzi states: Ning in the age of decay and chaos—when the age falsely changed many clan names—violating the sage's system—not the ritual intent of commanded surnames—therefore composed Treatise on Clan Surnames to trace the original lineages—text lengthy so not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: (The Fuzi notes his Treatise on Surnames against fraudulent genealogies.

sentences.zh: 每所居姻親、知舊、鄰里有困窮者，家儲雖不盈擔石，必分以贍救之。

translations.literal: Wherever he dwelt—in-laws, old friends, neighbors who faced hardship—though family stores did not fill a dan of grain—he always divided to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: He split his last grain with needy kin and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 與人子言，教以孝；

translations.literal: With people's sons he spoke—teaching filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: To sons he preached filial piety;

sentences.zh: 與人弟言，訓以悌；

translations.literal: with people's younger brothers he spoke—instructing fraternal duty;
translations.idiomatic: to younger brothers, fraternity;

sentences.zh: 言及人臣，誨以忠。

translations.literal: speaking of people's ministers—he instructed loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: to officials, loyalty.

sentences.zh: 貌甚恭，言甚順，觀其行，邈然若不可及，即之熈熈然，甚柔而溫，因其事而導之於善，是以漸之者無不化焉。

translations.literal: His appearance was very respectful—his speech very compliant—viewing his conduct—distantly seeming beyond reach—approaching him warm and mild—very soft and gentle—according to the matter he guided toward good—therefore those gradually influenced by him were all transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He looked stern afar, gentle up close—every pupil bent toward good.

sentences.zh: 寧之亡，天下知與不知，聞之無不嗟歎。

translations.literal: At Ning's death—those in the world who knew and who did not—hearing of it none did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: All China mourned Guan Ning—friend or stranger.

sentences.zh: 醇德之所感若此，不亦至乎！〉

translations.literal: That pure virtue moves thus—is this not the utmost!〉
translations.idiomatic: Such was the power of his purity.)

sentences.zh: 張臶、胡昭

translations.literal: Zhang Qian, Hu Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian and Hu Zhao

sentences.zh: 時鉅鹿張臶，字子明，頴川胡昭，字孔明，亦養志不仕。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Qian of Julu—courtesy name Ziming—and Hu Zhao of Yingchuan—courtesy name Kongming—also nurtured resolve and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian of Julu (styled Ziming) and Hu Zhao of Yingchuan (styled Kongming) likewise refused office.

sentences.zh: 臶少游太學，學兼內外，後歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Qian in youth studied at the Imperial Academy—learning embraced inner and outer—and afterward returned to native village.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian studied at the imperial academy, mastering classics and technical lore, then went home.

sentences.zh: 袁紹前後辟命，不應，移居上黨。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao previously and afterward summoned him—he did not respond—and moved residence to Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored Yuan Shao’s repeated summons and moved to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 并州牧高幹表除樂平令，不就，徙遁常山，門徒且數百人，遷居任縣。

translations.literal: Shepherd of Bingzhou Gao Gan memorialized appointing him Magistrate of Leping—he did not go—and fled to Changshan—disciples nearly several hundred persons—and moved residence to Ren county.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan nominated him for Leping magistrate; he fled to Changshan with hundreds of pupils, then to Ren county.

sentences.zh: 太祖為丞相，辟，不詣。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor as Chancellor summoned him—he did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored Cao Cao’s summons as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太和中，詔求隱學之士能消災復異者，郡累上臶，發遣，老病不行。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era an edict sought reclusive scholars able to dispel disasters and restore anomalies—the commandery repeatedly memorialized Qian—issued dispatch—old age and illness prevented going.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe edicts sought miracle-working hermits; the county nominated Zhang Qian but age and illness blocked travel.

sentences.zh: 廣平太守盧毓到官三日，綱紀白承前致版謁臶。

translations.literal: Administrator of Guangping Lu Yu arrived at office three days—clerks reported continuing former practice of submitting visiting-card to call on Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu’s clerks wanted to pay Zhang Qian a formal visit.

sentences.zh: 毓教曰：「張先生所謂上不事天子，下不友諸侯者也。

translations.literal: Yu instructed saying: "Mr Zhang—what men call one who above does not serve the Son of Heaven—below does not befriend feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu said Zhang Qian neither serves the emperor nor courts lords.

sentences.zh: 此豈版謁所可光飾哉！

translations.literal: How could visiting-cards brighten him!
translations.idiomatic: Calling cards cannot polish such a man!

sentences.zh: 」但遣主簿奉書致羊酒之禮。

translations.literal: Only dispatch chief clerk bearing letter presenting lamb and wine ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Send only letters and modest gifts.

sentences.zh: 青龍四年辛亥詔書：「張掖郡玄川溢涌，激波奮蕩，寶石負圖，狀像靈龜，宅于川西，嶷然磐峙，倉質素章，麟鳳龍馬，煥炳成形，文字告命，粲然著明。

translations.literal: Qinglong fourth year xinhai edict: "In Zhangye commandery the Dark River overflowed surging—waves rose fiercely—precious stone bore chart—shape like spirit tortoise—dwelling west of the river—towering like massive pillar—plain substance plain pattern—unicorn phoenix dragon horse—brilliantly formed—written characters proclaiming mandate—radiantly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: A 236 CE edict described a Zhangye flood revealing a tortoise-shaped stone covered with omens.

sentences.zh: 太史令高堂隆上言：古皇聖帝所未甞蒙，實有魏之禎命，東序之世寶。」

translations.literal: Director of Astronomy Gao Tanglong memorialized: ancient sage emperors never received such—it is truly Wei's auspicious mandate—the eastern hall's treasure of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong called it Wei’s heavenly mandate—the treasure of the eastern hall.

sentences.zh: 〈《尚書·顧命篇》曰：「大玉、夷玉、天球、河圖在東序。

translations.literal: The Shangshu Gu ming chapter states: "Great jade, barbarian jade, celestial sphere, River Chart lie in the eastern hall.
translations.idiomatic: (The Gu ming chapter lists the River Chart among eastern-hall treasures.

sentences.zh: 」注曰：「河圖，圖出於河，帝王聖者之所受。」〉

translations.literal: Commentary states: "River Chart—the chart emerging from the river—what sage emperors receive."〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentators say the River Chart comes from the Yellow River for sage kings.)

sentences.zh: 事班天下。

translations.literal: The matter was promulgated all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The edict circulated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 任令于綽連齎以問臶，臶密謂綽曰：「夫神以知來，不追已往，禎祥先見而後廢興從之。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Ren Yu Chuo repeatedly carried it to ask Qian—Qian secretly said to Chuo: "As for spirit—it knows what comes—it does not chase what has passed—auspicious signs appear first—then rise and fall follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chuo asked Zhang Qian’s reading; Zhang said omens foretell the future, not the past.

sentences.zh: 漢已乆亡，魏已得之，何所追興徵祥乎！

translations.literal: Han long since perished—Wei already obtained it—what is there to chase in rising auspicious signs!
translations.idiomatic: Han is gone and Wei holds power—why parade omens of mandate?

sentences.zh: 此石，當今之變異而將來之禎瑞也。

translations.literal: This stone—is today's anomaly—and will be tomorrow's auspicious portent.
translations.idiomatic: This stone marks today’s prodigy—tomorrow’s blessing.

sentences.zh: 」正始元年，戴鵀之鳥，巢臶門陰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengshi—the hoopoe bird nested in the shade of Qian's gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 240 a hoopoe nested in Zhang Qian’s doorway.

sentences.zh: 臶告門人曰：「夫戴鵀陽鳥，而巢門陰，此凶祥也。

translations.literal: Qian told disciples: "The hoopoe is a yang bird—yet it nests in gate shade—this is ill omen."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian called it ill-omened—a sun bird nesting in shadow.

sentences.zh: 」乃援琴歌詠，作詩二篇，旬日而卒，時年一百五歲。

translations.literal: Thereupon took zither and sang—composed two poems—within ten days died—at that time age one hundred five.
translations.idiomatic: He sang, wrote two poems, and died ten days later at one hundred and five.

sentences.zh: 是歲，廣平太守王肅至官，教下縣曰：「前在京都，聞張子明，來至問之，會其已亡，致痛惜之。

translations.literal: That year Administrator of Guangping Wang Su arrived at office—instructed the counties saying: "Formerly in the capital I heard of Zhang Ziming—coming here I asked—happened that he had already died—I extended deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su mourned arriving too late to meet Zhang Qian.

sentences.zh: 此君篤學隱居，不與時競，以道樂身。

translations.literal: This lord studied deeply and dwelt hidden—not competing with the age—using the Way to delight his person.
translations.idiomatic: He studied in seclusion and found joy in the Way.

sentences.zh: 昔絳縣老人屈在泥塗，趙孟升之，諸侯用睦。

translations.literal: Formerly the old man of Jiang county bent in mud—Zhao Meng raised him—and the feudal lords became harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Like Zhao Meng honoring Jiang’s elder, honor worthies and lords unite.

sentences.zh: 愍其耄勤好道，而不蒙榮寵，書到，遣吏勞問其家，顯題門戶，務加殊異，以慰旣往，以勸將來。」

translations.literal: Pity his aged diligence loving the Way—yet not receiving glory and favor—when the letter arrives—dispatch clerks to console his household—mark his gate prominently—strive to add exceptional marks—to console the past—to encourage the future."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su ordered county honors for Zhang Qian’s house.

sentences.zh: 胡昭始避地冀州，亦辭袁紹之命，遁還鄉里。

translations.literal: Hu Zhao first fled to Ji Province—also declined Yuan Shao's command—and secretly returned to native village.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhao fled to Ji, refused Yuan Shao, then slipped home.

sentences.zh: 太祖為司空丞相，頻加禮辟。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor as Minister of Works and Chancellor—repeatedly added ritual summons.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao summoned him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 昭往應命，旣至，自陳一介野生，無軍國之用，歸誠求去。

translations.literal: Zhao went to answer the command—already arrived—personally stated he was one rude wild man—without use for army or state—sincerely sought to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhao answered the summons but begged off as useless to state affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「人各有志，出處異趣，勉卒雅尚，義不相屈。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said: "People each have intent—emerging and dwelling follow different inclinations—strive to complete your elegant ideals—righteousness does not bend you."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said: “Each man has his path—I will not force you.

sentences.zh: 」昭乃轉居陸渾山中，躬耕樂道，以經籍自娛。

translations.literal: Zhao thereupon moved to dwell in Luhun mountains—personally plowed and delighted in the Way—using classics to entertain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhao retired to Luhun, farmed, and read.

sentences.zh: 閭里敬而愛之。

translations.literal: Village and hamlet revered and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors revered him.

sentences.zh: 〈《高士傳》曰：初，晉宣帝為布衣時，與昭有舊。

translations.literal: The Gaoshi zhuan states: Earlier—when Jin Xuandi was common cloth—he had old ties with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: (Huangfu Mi: Sima Yi knew Hu Zhao before power.

sentences.zh: 同郡周生等謀害帝，昭聞而步陟險，邀生於崤、澠之間，止生，生不肯。

translations.literal: Fellow commandery Master Zhou and others plotted to kill the emperor—Zhao heard and walked climbing peril—intercepted Sheng between Xiao and Mian—stopped Sheng—Sheng would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors plotted against Sima Yi, Hu Zhao crossed mountain passes to stop them.

sentences.zh: 昭泣與結誠，生感其義，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhao wept and bound sincerity—Sheng was moved by his righteousness—and thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Tears and earnest pleas turned the plotters.

sentences.zh: 昭因與斫棗樹共盟而別。

translations.literal: Zhao thereupon with him chopped a jujube tree—jointly swore alliance—and parted.
translations.idiomatic: They cut a jujube tree as covenant.

sentences.zh: 昭雖有陰德於帝，口終不言，人莫知之。

translations.literal: Though Zhao had hidden virtue toward the emperor—to the end did not speak—none knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhao never told Sima Yi what he had done.

sentences.zh: 信行著於鄉黨。

translations.literal: Trustworthy conduct manifested in village.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity was locally famous.

sentences.zh: 建安十六年，百姓聞馬超叛，避兵入山者千餘家，飢乏，漸相劫略，昭常遜辭以解之，是以寇難消息，衆咸宗焉。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an—the common people hearing Ma Chao rebelled—those avoiding troops entering mountains numbered over a thousand households—starving and exhausted—gradually mutually robbed one another—Zhao constantly used yielding words to resolve it—thereby bandit hardship subsided—all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao’s revolt drove refugees into the hills, Hu Zhao mediated feuds until calm returned.

sentences.zh: 故其所居部落中，三百里無相侵暴者。〉

translations.literal: Therefore within the tribal settlement where he dwelt—three hundred li none invaded or brutalized.〉
translations.idiomatic: No raider touched his valley for three hundred li.)

sentences.zh: 建安二十三年，陸渾長張固被書調丁夫，當給漢中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jian'an—chief of Luhun Zhang Gu received documents conscripting laborers—to supply Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 218 Luhun district was ordered to ship corvée labor to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 百姓惡憚遠役，並懷擾擾。

translations.literal: The common people hated and feared distant service—and together harbored turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: People dreaded the long march.

sentences.zh: 民孫狼等因興兵殺縣主簿，作為叛亂，縣邑殘破。

translations.literal: Commoners Sun Lang and others thereupon raised troops killing the county chief registrar—making rebellion—the county seat was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lang killed the registrar and sacked the town.

sentences.zh: 固率將十餘吏卒，依昭住止，招集遺民，安復社稷。

translations.literal: Gu led over ten clerks and soldiers—relied on Zhao's dwelling—gathered surviving people—and restored the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Gu rallied survivors at Hu Zhao’s camp and rebuilt the district.

sentences.zh: 狼等遂南附關羽。

translations.literal: Lang and others thereupon south attached to Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lang then joined Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽授印給兵，還為寇賊，到陸渾南長樂亭，自相約誓，言：「胡居士賢者也，一不得犯其部落。

translations.literal: Yu conferred seals and issued troops—returned as bandit raiders—reached south of Luhun at Changle pavilion—mutually swore an oath saying: "Layman Hu is a worthy—none may violate his tribal settlement."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu’s raiders swore to spare Hu Zhao’s valley.

sentences.zh: 」一川賴昭，咸無怵惕。

translations.literal: The whole river valley relied on Zhao—all without fear.
translations.idiomatic: The whole basin slept safely thanks to him.

sentences.zh: 天下安輯，徙宅宜陽。

translations.literal: All under Heaven settled and joined—he moved residence to Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When peace returned he moved to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《高士傳》曰：幽州刺史杜恕甞過昭所居草廬之中，言事論理，辭義謙敬，恕甚重焉。

translations.literal: The Gaoshi zhuan states: Governor of Youzhou Du Shu once passed Zhao's thatched hut—discussing affairs and reasoning—word and meaning humble and respectful—Shu greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: (Du Shu visited Hu Zhao’s hut and admired his discourse.

sentences.zh: 太尉蔣濟辟，不就。〉

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Jiang Ji summoned—did not go.〉
translations.idiomatic: He refused Grand Commandant Jiang Ji.)

sentences.zh: 正始中，驃騎將軍趙儼、尚書黃休、郭彝、散騎常侍荀顗、鍾毓、太僕庾嶷、

translations.literal: In Zhengshi—General of Agile Cavalry Zhao Yan—Ministers Huang Xiu, Guo Yi—Regular Palace Attendants Xun Yi, Zhong Yu—Grand Coachman Yu Yi—
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, Zhao Yan, Huang Xiu, Guo Yi, Xun Yi, Zhong Yu, Yu Yi,

sentences.zh: 〈案《庾氏譜》：嶷字劭然，頴川人。

translations.literal: Investigating the Yu lineage register: Yi courtesy name Shaoran—Yingchuan person.
translations.idiomatic: (Pei notes: Yu Yi, styled Shaoran, from Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 子䨹字玄默，晉尚書、陽翟子。

translations.literal: Son Yun courtesy name Xuanmo—Jin Minister—noble of Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Yun rose in Jin.

sentences.zh: 嶷弟遁，字德先，太中大夫。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Dun—courtesy name Dexian—Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Yu Dun was grand counsellor.

sentences.zh: 遁胤嗣克昌，為世盛門。

translations.literal: Dun's descendants flourished—became a great clan of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan flourished.

sentences.zh: 侍中峻、河南尹純，皆遁之子，豫州牧長史顗，遁之孫，太尉文康公亮、司空冰皆遁之曾孫，貴達至今。〉

translations.literal: Attendant-in-chief Jun and Governor of Henan Chun were Dun's sons—Prefectural Chief Secretary Yi was Dun's grandson—Grand Commandant Wen Kang Gong Liang and Minister Bing were Dun's great-grandsons—noble and eminent to this day.〉
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants filled Jin offices down to the present.)

sentences.zh: 弘農太守何楨等

translations.literal: Administrator of Hongnong He Zhen and others
translations.idiomatic: He Zhen of Hongnong and others

sentences.zh: 〈《文士傳》曰：楨字元幹，廬江人，有文學器幹，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: The Wenshi zhuan states: Zhen courtesy name Yuanqian—Lujiang person—had literary talent and capacity—appearance very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: (Wenshi zhuan: He Zhen, styled Yuanqian, from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 歷幽州刺史、廷尉，入晉為尚書光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Served as Governor of Youzhou—Commandant of Justice—entered Jin as Minister and Minister of Court Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He served Youzhou, justice, then Jin ministries.

sentences.zh: 楨子龕，後將軍；

translations.literal: Zhen's son Kan—later general;
translations.idiomatic: Son He Kan became a general;

sentences.zh: 勗，車騎將軍；

translations.literal: Xu—general of chariots and cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: He Xu, general of chariots;

sentences.zh: 惲，豫州刺史；

translations.literal: Yun—Governor of Yu Province;
translations.idiomatic: He Yun, governor of Yu;

sentences.zh: 其餘多至大官。

translations.literal: The rest mostly reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: The rest rose high.

sentences.zh: 自後累世昌阜，司空文穆公充，惲之孫也，貴達至今。〉

translations.literal: Afterward for generations prosperous—Minister Wen Mu Gong Chong—was Yun's grandson—noble and eminent to this day.〉
translations.idiomatic: He Chong descended from this line.)

sentences.zh: 遞薦昭曰：「天真高絜，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: In turn recommended Zhao saying: "Heavenly truth high and pure—old yet more devoted.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly praised Hu Zhao’s purity.

sentences.zh: 玄虛靜素，有夷、皓之節。

translations.literal: Dark void quiet plain—has the integrity of Yi and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He rivals Boyi and the Four Elders.

sentences.zh: 宜蒙徵命，以勵風俗。」

translations.literal: Ought receive summons with exception—to encourage customs."
translations.idiomatic: Summon him to reform morals.

sentences.zh: 〈《高士傳》曰：朝廷以戎車未息，徵命之事，且須後之，昭以故不即徵。

translations.literal: The Gaoshi zhuan states: The court because war chariots had not ceased—matters of summons—must await afterward—Zhao on this account was not immediately summoned.
translations.idiomatic: (War delayed Hu Zhao’s summons.

sentences.zh: 後顗、休復與庾嶷薦昭，有詔訪於本州評議。

translations.literal: Afterward Yi and Xiu again with Yu Yi recommended Zhao—there was edict to inquire in native commandery for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xun Yi and Huang Xiu renewed the plea; the court polled his county.

sentences.zh: 侍中韋誕駮曰：「禮賢徵士，王政之所重也，古者考行於鄉。

translations.literal: Attendant Wei Dan refuted saying: "Courtesy toward worthies and summoned gentlemen—is what royal governance esteems—in ancient times conduct was examined in the village.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan urged village vetting as ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 今顗等位皆常伯納言，嶷為卿佐，足以取信。

translations.literal: Now Yi and others rank all regular ministers bearing speech—Yi is minister aide—sufficient to earn trust.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers can vouch for him.

sentences.zh: 附下罔上，忠臣之所不行也。

translations.literal: Currying favor below and deceiving above—faithful ministers do not practice this.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery of inferiors is unworthy.

sentences.zh: 昭宿德耆艾，遺逸山林，誠宜加異。

translations.literal: Zhao's long-standing virtue aged gray—drifting hidden in mountains and forests—truly ought receive exception.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hu Zhao’s virtue deserves honor.

sentences.zh: 」乃從誕議也。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon followed Dan's deliberation.〉
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Wei Dan’s view.)

sentences.zh: 至嘉平二年，公車特徵，會卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: By the second year of Jiaping—imperial carriage made special summons—it happened he died—age eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In 250 the court summoned him—he died at eighty-nine first.

sentences.zh: 拜子纂郎中。

translations.literal: His son Zuan was appointed Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Son Hu Zuan became a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 初，昭善史書，與鍾繇、邯鄲淳、衞覬、韋誕並有名，尺牘之迹，動見模楷焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhao excelled at clerical script—together with Zhong Yao, Handan Chun, Wei Ji, Wei Dan all had fame—the traces of his letters—whenever seen became models.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhao ranked with Zhong Yao and Handan Chun in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：胡徵君怡怡無不愛也，雖僕隷，必加禮焉。

translations.literal: The Fuzi states: Hu Summoned Gentleman was gentle and kind to all—though slaves—he always added ritual.
translations.idiomatic: (Fu Xuan says Hu Zhao loved everyone, even slaves.

sentences.zh: 外同乎俗，內秉純絜，心非其好，王公不能屈，年八十而不倦於書籍者，吾於胡徵君見之矣。

translations.literal: Outwardly same as common—inwardly holding pure cleanliness—heart not his liking—princes and dukes cannot bend him—age eighty yet not weary of books—I have seen this in Hu Summoned Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly ordinary, inwardly pure—no prince could break him—still reading at eighty.

sentences.zh: 時有隱者焦先，河東人也。

translations.literal: At that time there was a recluse Jiao Xian—a Hedong person.
translations.idiomatic: The narrative turns to Jiao Xian of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：先字孝然。

translations.literal: The Wei lue states: Xian courtesy name Xiaoran.
translations.idiomatic: (Wei lue: Jiao Xian, styled Xiaoran.

sentences.zh: 中平末，白波賊起。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhongping—the White Wave bandits arose.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongping’s end the White Wave rebels rose.

sentences.zh: 時先年二十餘，與同郡侯武陽相隨。

translations.literal: At that time Xian was over twenty—together with fellow commandery Hou Wuyang followed each other.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Xian, twenty, fled with Hou Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 武陽年小，有母，先與相扶接，避白波，東客揚州取婦。

translations.literal: Wuyang was young—had a mother—Xian together with him supported and escorted—avoiding White Wave—east guested at Yangzhou to take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: They fled east to Yangzhou where Hou married.

sentences.zh: 建安初來西還，武陽詣大陽占戶，先留陝界。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an came west returning—Wuyang went to Dayang to register household—Xian remained at Shan border.
translations.idiomatic: Returning west, Hou registered at Dayang while Jiao stayed in Shan.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，關中亂。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year—Guanzhong was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: By 211 Guanzhong exploded.

sentences.zh: 先失家屬，獨竄於河渚間，食草飲水，無衣履。

translations.literal: Xian lost family dependents—alone fled among river islets—eating grass drinking water—without clothes or shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Xian lost his family and lived naked on a river bar.

sentences.zh: 時大陽長朱南望見之，謂為亡士，欲遣船捕取。

translations.literal: At that time chief of Dayang Zhu Nan saw him from afar—thought him a fugitive gentleman—wished to dispatch boats to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhu Nan thought him a deserter.

sentences.zh: 武陽語縣：「此狂癡人耳！

translations.literal: Wuyang told the county: "This is only a mad deranged man!
translations.idiomatic: Hou Wuyang said he was a harmless lunatic.

sentences.zh: 」遂注其籍。

translations.literal: Thereupon noted him on the register.
translations.idiomatic: So they listed him as such.

sentences.zh: 給廩，日五升。

translations.literal: Granted grain ration—five sheng per day.
translations.idiomatic: The county gave five sheng of grain daily.

sentences.zh: 後有疫病，人多死者，縣常使埋藏，童兒豎子皆輕易之。

translations.literal: Afterward there was pestilence—many people died—the county often ordered burial—children and boys all treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: During plague the county used him for burials; boys mocked him.

sentences.zh: 然其行不踐邪徑，必循阡陌；

translations.literal: Yet his walking did not tread evil paths—always followed field-paths;
translations.idiomatic: He walked only ridge paths—never shortcuts;

sentences.zh: 及其捃拾，不取大穗；

translations.literal: when gathering fallen grain—did not take large ears;
translations.idiomatic: when gleaning he left the largest heads;

sentences.zh: 饑不苟食，寒不苟衣，結草以為裳，科頭徒跣。

translations.literal: when hungry did not eat rashly—when cold did not clothe rashly—knotted grass to make skirt—bare head bare feet.
translations.idiomatic: he starved and froze rather than steal—wore grass and went barefoot.

sentences.zh: 每出，見婦人則隱翳，須去乃出。

translations.literal: Whenever going out—seeing women then hid—must wait for them to leave before emerging.
translations.idiomatic: He hid from women on the road.

sentences.zh: 自作一瓜牛廬，淨埽其中。

translations.literal: He himself built a one-room snail hut—and swept it clean within.
translations.idiomatic: He built a tiny hovel and swept it clean.

sentences.zh: 營木為牀，布草蓐其上。

translations.literal: Arranged wood as bed—spread grass mat atop.
translations.idiomatic: A plank bed and straw mat.

sentences.zh: 至天寒時，搆火以自炙，呻吟獨語。

translations.literal: When heaven cold—built fire to roast himself—moaning and talking alone.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he huddled by a fire, muttering alone.

sentences.zh: 饑則出為人客作，飽食而已，不取其直。

translations.literal: When hungry he went out as hired labor for others—ate his fill only—and did not take wages.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger drove him he day-labored for meals alone—never kept pay.

sentences.zh: 又出於道中，邂逅與人相遇，輙下道藏匿。

translations.literal: Again when going out on the road—if by chance meeting people—always stepped off the road and hid.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he dove into ditches whenever anyone approached.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，常言「草茅之人，與狐兔同羣」。

translations.literal: Some asked his reason—he constantly said "a man of straw huts—with foxes and hares in one herd."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he muttered that grass-dwellers belong with beasts.

sentences.zh: 不肯妄語。

translations.literal: Unwilling to speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He refused idle chatter.

sentences.zh: 太和、青龍中，甞持一杖南渡淺河水，輙獨云未可也，由是人頗疑其不狂。

translations.literal: In Taihe and Qinglong—he once held a staff crossing the shallow river south—yet alone said "not yet"—thereby people somewhat suspected he was not mad.
translations.idiomatic: Once he refused to ford a stream alone—folk wondered if he was sane after all.

sentences.zh: 至嘉平中，太守賈穆初之官，故過其廬。

translations.literal: By Jiaping—Administrator Jia Mu first took office—therefore passed his hut.
translations.idiomatic: New prefect Jia Mu made a point of visiting his shack.

sentences.zh: 先見穆再拜。

translations.literal: Xian saw Mu and performed double obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Xian bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 穆與語，不應；

translations.literal: Mu spoke with him—he did not respond;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mu spoke; Xian stayed mute.

sentences.zh: 與食，不食。

translations.literal: gave food—he did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Offered food; he refused.

sentences.zh: 穆謂之曰：「國家使我來為卿作君，我食卿，卿不肯食，我與卿語，卿不應我，如是，我不中為卿作君，當去耳！

translations.literal: Mu said to him: "The state sent me to be lord for you—I eat your food—you refuse to eat—I speak to you—you do not respond to me—like this—I am not fit to be lord for you—I ought to depart!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mu said: “The court made me your magistrate—you ignore my food and words—I cannot serve you—I will leave.

sentences.zh: 」先乃曰：「寧有是邪？

translations.literal: Xian then said: "Could there be such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian whispered: “Can that be true?

sentences.zh: 」遂不復語。

translations.literal: Thereupon did not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Then fell silent again.

sentences.zh: 其明年，大發卒將伐吳。

translations.literal: The next year—greatly mobilized troops planning to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wei launched the Wu campaign.

sentences.zh: 有竊問先：「今討吳何如？

translations.literal: Someone secretly asked Xian: "Now attacking Wu—how will it go?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked how the Wu war would end.

sentences.zh: 」先不肯應，而謬歌曰：「祝衂祝衂，非魚非肉，更相追逐，本心為當殺牂羊，更殺其羖䍽邪！

translations.literal: Xian would not respond—but wrongly sang: "Zhu nou Zhu nou—not fish not meat—mutually chasing one another—the heart originally meant to kill the ram ewe—again kill the kid?"
translations.idiomatic: He chanted nonsense: “Blunt snouts, blunt snouts—neither fish nor flesh—chasing in circles—were we meant to slaughter the Wu ewe or the Wei kid?”

sentences.zh: 」郡人不知其謂。
