translations.literal: County people did not know what he meant.
translations.idiomatic: Nobody understood the riddle.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍敗，好事者乃推其意，疑牂羊謂吳，羖䍽謂魏，於是後人僉謂之隱者也。

translations.literal: When the various armies were defeated—enthusiasts then inferred his intent—suspecting ram ewe meant Wu—kid meant Wei—thereupon afterward people all called him a recluse.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat listeners decided “ewe” meant Wu and “kid” meant Wei—and hailed him a prophet.

sentences.zh: 議郎河東董經特嘉異節，與先非故人，密往觀之。

translations.literal: Gentleman Consultant Dong Jing of Hedong especially praised his exceptional integrity—though not old friends with Xian—secretly went to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jing admired him and spied on his hut.

sentences.zh: 經到，乃奮其白鬚，為如與之有舊者，謂曰：「阿先闊乎！

translations.literal: When Jing arrived—Xian then flourished his white beard—as if having old ties—said: "Ah Xian—it has been long!
translations.idiomatic: Xian stroked his beard and cried: “Brother Xian—long time!

sentences.zh: 念共避白波時不？

translations.literal: Remember together avoiding the White Wave—do you not?"
translations.idiomatic: Remember the White Wave days?”

sentences.zh: 」先熟視而不言。

translations.literal: Xian stared fixedly and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xian stared through him.

sentences.zh: 經素知其昔受武陽恩，因復曰：「念武陽不邪？

translations.literal: Jing always knew he formerly received Wuyang's kindness—therefore again said: "Remember Wuyang—do you not?"
translations.idiomatic: Dong tried Hou Wuyang next.

sentences.zh: 」先乃曰：「已報之矣。

translations.literal: Xian then said: "Already repaid him."
translations.idiomatic: Xian muttered: “Paid that debt.

sentences.zh: 」經又復挑欲與語，遂不肯復應。

translations.literal: Jing again repeatedly pressed wishing to speak with him—thereupon refused again to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Further questions met silence.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘病亡，時年八十九矣。

translations.literal: Afterward over a year fell ill and died—at that time age eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year at eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 《高士傳》曰：世莫知先所出。

translations.literal: The Gaoshi zhuan states: the age does not know Xian's origins.
translations.idiomatic: (Huangfu Mi: no one knew Jiao Xian’s origins.

sentences.zh: 或言生乎漢末，自陝居大陽，無父母兄弟妻子。

translations.literal: Some say born end of Han—from Shan dwelling Dayang—without parents brothers wife children.
translations.idiomatic: Some say he left Shan for Dayang alone.

sentences.zh: 見漢室衰，乃自絕不言。

translations.literal: Seeing Han house decline—thereupon cut himself off from speech.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s fall sealed his lips.

sentences.zh: 及魏受禪，常結草為廬於河之湄，獨止其中。

translations.literal: When Wei received abdication—constantly knotted grass into hut on the river bank—dwelling alone within.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei took the mandate he built a grass hut on the river.

sentences.zh: 冬夏恒不著衣，卧不設席，又無草蓐，以身親土，其體垢汙皆如泥漆，五形盡露，不行人間。

translations.literal: Winter and summer constantly wore no clothes—lying without mat—also without straw pad—using body to touch earth—his body filthy as mud lacquer—five forms all exposed—did not walk among people.
translations.idiomatic: He slept naked on earth year-round—black with grime.

sentences.zh: 或數日一食，欲食則為人賃作，人以衣衣之，乃使限功受直，足得一食輙去，人欲多與，終不肯取，亦有數日不食時。

translations.literal: Sometimes several days one meal—wishing to eat then worked hired labor for others—people clothed him—then made him limit work receive wages—enough for one meal then left—people wished to give more—always refused to take—also had times of several days not eating.
translations.idiomatic: He ate when he earned a meal—never took charity.

sentences.zh: 行不由邪徑，目不與女子逆視。

translations.literal: Walking did not use evil paths—eyes did not meet women's gaze.
translations.idiomatic: He avoided shortcuts and women’s eyes.

sentences.zh: 口未甞言，雖有驚急，不與人語。

translations.literal: Mouth never spoke—though there was alarm and urgency—did not speak with people.
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke—even in crisis.

sentences.zh: 遺以食物皆不受。

translations.literal: Given food he all did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused food gifts.

sentences.zh: 河東太守杜恕甞以衣服迎見，而不與語。

translations.literal: Administrator of Hedong Du Shu once with clothes went to welcome see—and did not speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shu brought clothes; Xian stayed mute.

sentences.zh: 司馬景王聞而使安定太守董經因事過視，又不肯語，經以為大賢。

translations.literal: Sima Jingwang heard and ordered Administrator of Anding Dong Jing because of affairs pass observe—and again refused to speak—Jing thought him greatly worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi sent Dong Jing to observe; Xian still would not talk.

sentences.zh: 其後野火燒其廬，先因露寢。

translations.literal: Afterward wildfire burned his hut—Xian therefore slept in the open.
translations.idiomatic: A wildfire destroyed his hut—he slept under sky.

sentences.zh: 遭冬雪大至，先袒卧不移，人以為死，就視如故，不以為病，人莫能審其意。

translations.literal: Met winter snow greatly arrived—Xian lay bare without moving—people thought him dead—approached to look—still as before—did not consider it illness—none could fathom his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He lay naked in blizzard—seemed dead yet unharmed.

sentences.zh: 度年可百歲餘乃卒。

translations.literal: Estimated age could be over a hundred then died.
translations.idiomatic: He died past one hundred.

sentences.zh: 或問皇甫謐曰：「焦先何人？

translations.literal: Someone asked Huangfu Mi: "What sort of man was Jiao Xian?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked Huangfu Mi who Jiao Xian was.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾不足以知之也。

translations.literal: He said: "I am not sufficient to know him."
translations.idiomatic: Mi answered: “Beyond my ken.

sentences.zh: 考之於表，可略而言矣。

translations.literal: Examining him in the chart—can speak in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet tables sketch his type.

sentences.zh: 夫世之所常趣者榮味也，形之所不可釋者衣裳也，身之所不可離者室宅也，口之所不能已者言語也，心之不可絕者親戚也。

translations.literal: As for what the age constantly hurries toward—glory and flavor—what form cannot release—clothing—what body cannot leave—house and dwelling—what mouth cannot stop—speech—what heart cannot cut off—kin.
translations.idiomatic: Men chase flavor, clothes, houses, talk, and kin.

sentences.zh: 今焦先棄榮味，釋衣服，離室宅，絕親戚，閉口不言，曠然以天地為棟宇，闇然合至道之前，出羣形之表，入玄寂之幽，一世之人不足以挂其意，四海之廣不能以回其顧，妙乎與夫三皇之先者同矣。

translations.literal: Now Jiao Xian abandoned glory and flavor—released clothing—left house and dwelling—cut off kin—closed mouth without speech—vastly taking Heaven and Earth as rafters and roof—darkly joining before the utmost Way—emerging beyond the throng of forms—entering the quiet of dark silence—people of one generation not sufficient to hook his intent—the four seas' breadth cannot turn his glance—wonderful—same as before the Three August Ones!
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Xian shed every human tie and merged with the Way.

sentences.zh: 結繩已來，未及其至也，豈羣言之所能髣髴，常心之所得測量哉！

translations.literal: Since knotted cords—not reached his utmost—how could crowd speech imitate—or ordinary hearts measure!
translations.idiomatic: Since legendary times none matched him.

sentences.zh: 彼行人所不能行，堪人所不能堪，犯寒暑不以傷其性，居曠野不以恐其形，遭驚急不以迫其慮，離榮愛不以累其心，損視聽不以汙其耳目，舍足於不損之地，居身於獨立之處，延年歷百，壽越期頤，雖上識不能尚也。

translations.literal: He walks what people cannot walk—endures what people cannot endure—violates cold and heat without harming his nature—dwells wild wastes without fearing his form—meets alarm and urgency without pressing his thoughts—leaves glory and love without burdening his heart—damages sight and hearing without fouling ears and eyes—plants feet on ground that cannot be harmed—places body in standing alone—extends years past hundred—life crosses century expectation—though highest understanding cannot surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi piles paradox on paradox—cold cannot hurt him, exile cannot scare him.

sentences.zh: 自羲皇已來，一人而已矣！

translations.literal: Since Fuxi—only one person!
translations.idiomatic: Since Fuxi—only one such man.

sentences.zh: 」《魏氏春秋》曰：故梁州刺史耿黼以先為「仙人」也，北海傅玄謂之「性同禽獸」，並為之傳，而莫能測之。〉

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu states: former Inspector of Liangzhou Geng Fu took Xian as "transcendent"—Beihai Fu Xuan called him "nature same as birds and beasts"—both composed biographies—yet none could fathom him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Some called him immortal, Fu Xuan likened him to beasts—none understood him.)

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》又載扈累及寒貧者。

translations.literal: The Wei lue also records Hu Lei and Han Pin.
translations.idiomatic: (Wei lue adds Hu Lei and “Cold Poverty.”

sentences.zh: 累字伯重，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Lei courtesy name Bozhong—Jingzhao person.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lei, styled Bozhong, from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 初平中，山東人有青牛先生者，字正方，客三輔。

translations.literal: In Chuping—a man of Shandong called Master Green Ox—courtesy name Zhengfang—guested in Sanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuping a Shandong man called Master Green Ox (styled Zhengfang) lived in Sanfu.

sentences.zh: 曉知星曆、風角、鳥情。

translations.literal: He understood star calendars—wind angles—bird augury.
translations.idiomatic: He knew astrology, wind lore, and bird omens.

sentences.zh: 常食青葙芫華。

translations.literal: Constantly ate celosia and wild chrysanthemum.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on herbs.

sentences.zh: 年似如五六十者，人或親識之，謂其已百餘歲矣。

translations.literal: Age seemed like fifty or sixty—some personally knew him—said he was already over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He looked sixty yet people swore he was a century old.

sentences.zh: 初，累年四十餘，隨正方游學，人謂之得其術。

translations.literal: Earlier Lei was over forty—followed Zhengfang traveling to study—people said he obtained his arts.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lei studied under Green Ox in middle age.

sentences.zh: 有婦，無子。

translations.literal: Had a wife—no children.
translations.idiomatic: He had a barren wife.

sentences.zh: 建安十六年，三輔亂，又隨正方南入漢中。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an—Sanfu in turmoil—again followed Zhengfang south into Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 211 he fled to Hanzhong with Green Ox.

sentences.zh: 漢中壞，正方入蜀，累與相失，隨徙民詣鄴，遭疾疫喪其婦。

translations.literal: Hanzhong collapsed—Zhengfang entered Shu—Lei lost track of him—followed relocated people to Ye—met plague and lost his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanzhong fell, Green Ox went to Shu; Hu Lei trekked to Ye and lost his wife to plague.

sentences.zh: 至黃初元年，又徙詣洛陽，遂不復娶婦。

translations.literal: By the first year of Huangchu—again moved to Luoyang—thereupon never again took a wife.
translations.idiomatic: By 220 he lived in Luoyang and never remarried.

sentences.zh: 獨居道側，以㼾甎為障，施一廚牀，食宿其中。

translations.literal: Dwelling alone beside the road—using tile as screen—set one kitchen bed—ate and slept within.
translations.idiomatic: He slept in a tile pen by the road.

sentences.zh: 晝日潛思，夜則仰視星宿，吟詠內書。

translations.literal: Daytime silently pondered—night then gazed at stars—chanting inner books.
translations.idiomatic: Days he meditated; nights he read stars and esoteric texts.

sentences.zh: 人或問之，閉口不肯言。

translations.literal: People asked him—closed mouth unwilling to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Questions met silence.

sentences.zh: 至嘉平中，年八九十，裁若四五十者。

translations.literal: By Jiaping—age eighty or ninety—appearance only like forty or fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaping he looked fifty though eighty.

sentences.zh: 縣官以其孤老，給廩日五升。

translations.literal: County office because he was solitary and old—granted grain ration five sheng per day.
translations.idiomatic: The county gave five sheng daily.

sentences.zh: 五升不足食，頗行傭作以裨糧，糧盡復出，人與不取。

translations.literal: Five sheng insufficient to eat—often went hired labor to supplement grain—grain exhausted again went out—people offered—he did not take.
translations.idiomatic: He moonlighted when rations ran out—still refused handouts.

sentences.zh: 食不求美，衣弊縕故，後一二年病亡。

translations.literal: Eating did not seek flavor—clothes worn and patched—after one or two years fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He wore rags and died of illness soon after.

sentences.zh: 寒貧者，本姓石，字德林，安定人也。

translations.literal: Han Pin—original surname Shi—courtesy name Delin—Anding person.
translations.idiomatic: “Cold Poverty” was born Shi Delin of Anding.

sentences.zh: 建安初，客三輔。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an—guested in Sanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jian’an he lived in Sanfu.

sentences.zh: 是時長安有宿儒欒文博者，門徒數千，德林亦就學，始精詩、書。

translations.literal: At that time Chang'an had an old scholar Luan Wenbo—disciples several thousand—Delin also went to study—first mastered Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with the famous Luan Wenbo.

sentences.zh: 後好內事，於衆輩中最玄默。

translations.literal: Afterward loved inner techniques—among the crowd most darkly silent.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to esoteric Daoism and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，關中亂，南入漢中。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year—Guanzhong in turmoil—south entered Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 211 he fled south to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 初不治產業，不畜妻孥，常讀老子五千文及諸內書，晝夜吟詠。

translations.literal: At first did not manage property—did not keep wife and children—constantly read Laozi's five thousand words and various inner books—day and night chanting.
translations.idiomatic: He owned nothing—chanted Laozi and inner scriptures.

sentences.zh: 到二十五年，漢中破，隨衆還長安，遂癡愚不復識人。

translations.literal: By the twenty-fifth year—Hanzhong broken—followed crowd returning Chang'an—thereupon stupid and foolish no longer recognized people.
translations.idiomatic: After 220 he wandered back to Chang’an—dementia silenced him.

sentences.zh: 食不求味，冬夏常衣弊布連結衣。

translations.literal: Eating did not seek flavor—winter and summer constantly wore worn cloth patched robe.
translations.idiomatic: He wore ragged stitched robes in every season.

sentences.zh: 體如無所勝，目如無所見。

translations.literal: Body as if unable to bear—eyes as if unable to see.
translations.idiomatic: He looked frail and blind.

sentences.zh: 獨居窮巷小屋，無親里。

translations.literal: Dwelling alone poor lane small hut—without kin or neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: He lived alone in a hovel—no kin.

sentences.zh: 人與之衣食，不肯取。

translations.literal: People gave him clothes and food—unwilling to take.
translations.idiomatic: He refused charity.

sentences.zh: 郡縣以其鰥窮，給廩日五升，食不足，頗行乞，乞不取多。

translations.literal: Commandery and county because he was widowed and destitute—granted grain ration five sheng per day—food insufficient—often went begging—begging did not take much.
translations.idiomatic: The county ration failed—he begged sparingly.

sentences.zh: 人問其姓字，口不肯言，故因號之曰「寒貧」也。

translations.literal: People asked his surname and name—mouth unwilling to speak—therefore on account of this was titled "Cold Poverty."
translations.idiomatic: He never gave his name—so folk called him Cold Poverty.

sentences.zh: 或素有與相知者，往存恤之，輙拜跪，由是人謂其不癡。

translations.literal: Some had always been acquainted—went to console him—he always bowed and knelt—thereby people said he was not stupid.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends still drew bows from him—proving sense lingered.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍郭淮以意氣呼之，問其所欲，亦不肯言。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Guo Huai with bold spirit called him—asked what he desired—also unwilling to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai shouted questions—no answer.

sentences.zh: 淮因與脯糒及衣，不取其衣，取其脯一朐、糒一升而止。

translations.literal: Huai thereupon gave dried meat and provisions and clothes—did not take the clothes—took only one piece of dried meat and one sheng provisions then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai offered clothes and food—he took one strip of jerky and one sheng of grain.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案《魏略》云：焦先及楊沛，並作瓜牛廬，止其中。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates the Wei lue stating: Jiao Xian and Yang Pei—both made melon-snail huts—dwelling within.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi cites Wei lue on snail huts for Jiao Xian and Yang Pei.

sentences.zh: 以為瓜當作蝸；

translations.literal: Thought gua ought to read wo;
translations.idiomatic: “Gua” should read “wo” (snail),

sentences.zh: 蝸牛，螺蟲之有角者也，俗或呼為黃犢。

translations.literal: snail—spiral shell creature having horns—common speech sometimes calls yellow calf.
translations.idiomatic: meaning spiral shells—folk call them “yellow calves.”

sentences.zh: 先等作圜舍，形如蝸牛蔽，故謂之蝸牛廬。

translations.literal: Xian and others made round huts—shape like snail shell covering—therefore called snail huts.
translations.idiomatic: Their round huts looked like snail shells.

sentences.zh: 《莊子》曰：「有國於蝸之左角者曰觸氏，有國於右角者曰蠻氏，時相與爭地而戰，伏尸數萬，逐北旬有五日而後反。

translations.literal: Zhuangzi states: "There is a state on the snail's left horn called Chu Clan—there is a state on the right horn called Man Clan—they constantly dispute territory and war—corpses lie in myriads—pursuing north fifteen days then return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi’s parable of kingdoms on a snail’s horns illustrates the point.

sentences.zh: 」謂此物也。〉

translations.literal: Speaks of this thing."〉
translations.idiomatic: That is the image.)

translations.literal: 【Evaluation】
translations.idiomatic: Evaluative note

sentences.zh: 評曰：袁渙、邴原、張範躬履清蹈，進退以道，

translations.literal: Evaluation states: Yuan Huan, Bing Yuan, Zhang Fan personally tread purity—advancing and retreating according to the Way,
translations.idiomatic: The historian praises Yuan Huan, Bing Yuan, and Zhang Fan for walking purity and timing every step.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為蹈猶履也，「躬履清蹈」，近非言乎！〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that tread still means walk—"personally tread purity tread"—is this not nearly redundant speech!〉
translations.idiomatic: (Pei Songzhi winces at the phrase “tread purity tread.”)

sentences.zh: 蓋是貢禹、兩龔之匹。

translations.literal: They are a match for Gong Yu and the two Gongs.
translations.idiomatic: They rank with Gong Yu and the Gongs of Han.

sentences.zh: 涼茂、國淵亦其次也。

translations.literal: Liang Mao and Guo Yuan are next after them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Mao and Guo Yuan follow.

sentences.zh: 張承名行亞範，可謂能弟矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Cheng's fame and conduct ranked below Fan—may be called a capable younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng stood worthily in his brother’s shadow.

sentences.zh: 田疇抗節，王脩忠貞，足以矯俗；

translations.literal: Tian Chou resisted principle—Wang Xiu was loyal and steadfast—sufficient to reform custom;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou’s resolve and Wang Xiu’s loyalty set the tone.

sentences.zh: 管寧淵雅高尚，確然不拔；

translations.literal: Guan Ning was profound, elegant, lofty, and unshakeable;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning towered immovable.

sentences.zh: 張臶、胡昭闔門守靜，不營當世：故并錄焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian and Hu Zhao closed gates guarding quietude—not scheming for the age—therefore all are recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian and Hu Zhao shut the world out—so they close the chapter.
